waves.goal: Make what already exists trustworthy and correct: one run context for Do runs, durable and multi-replica-safe runs, declared tool risk with MCP callable, audit delivery, ZDR live, learning and memory governance, cache and cost basics, render performance, release and CI guardrails.

Close the agent-loop and governance gaps users feel in chat and Do mode: approvals v2, plan-continue and ask_user, working connectors and agent browser, history foundation, Spaces as projects, verified Office deliverables, scheduled Do runs, the attention model, file tools, the action registry for agents and the org policy registry; start the sandbox-computer seam.

Deliver the research, creation and personalisation table-stakes on top: deep and wide research, citations to passages, readable long runs, artifact canvas, decks, Agents and Automations hubs, takeover, goals, skills lifecycle, scoped memory and personalisation, model record and Gemini, eval gates, egress tiers and the microVM sandbox.

Become a computer-using platform: computer use in the sandbox desktop, the live computer panel, inline widgets and MCP Apps on a user-content origin, sharing, event triggers, replay, images, custom connectors, plugins, public Agent API and bring-your-own providers.
Nice-to-have backlog, scheduled on demand or when a dependency makes them cheap.

adrNeeded.topic: Sandbox computer backend and thread-scoped workspace (microVM per thread, snapshot retention and destruction, cost metering)
adrNeeded.why: Moves execution from hermetic per-call bwrap processes to long-lived machines and introduces durable state outside Spaces; must show ZDR snapshot destruction, that a thread workspace never bypasses Space ACLs, supply-chain ownership of guest images, and VM-second billing.

adrNeeded.topic: Computer-use scope: desktop control only inside Verevon's sandbox VM; user-desktop control stays parked
adrNeeded.why: The owner parked OS-level desktop control; the Endpoint Plane can capture and inject input on real machines. An ADR should fix the boundary (sandbox only, consent tiers if ever unparked) and keep the 'Model proposes, executor executes' rule for desktop actions.

adrNeeded.topic: Spaces as the chat project container, instruction precedence and multi-author authority (OD19)
adrNeeded.why: Projects must not become a second container beside Spaces; precedence between org, Space, project and persona instructions, and whose delegated token runs a collaborator-triggered agent turn, need a ruling so Space access never widens an owner-plane ACL.

adrNeeded.topic: Agent-browser domain policy ownership and model-blind credentials (OD13)
adrNeeded.why: Decides whether broker, Control or Quarry owns the domain fence and per-site read/act consent, and how vault secrets are substituted by Quarry so the Model never sees them, preserving 'the Model proposes browser actions and Quarry executes or rejects them'.

adrNeeded.topic: Unattended authority: scheduled, goal and trigger runs, stored consent with expiry, renewable delegated credentials (owner ruling 2026-09-28, OD8, D10)
adrNeeded.why: Today scheduled runs are draft-only by owner ruling and the delegated bearer lives 300 s. Tool-using unattended runs need a signed, expiring consent contract, a non-delegable set and a renewal path through Control, not a service-principal shortcut.

adrNeeded.topic: Share model, public links and artifact hosting origin under ZDR and residency
adrNeeded.why: Public snapshots, published artifacts and a dedicated user-content origin create new egress and retention paths; connectors called from a shared artifact must run with the viewer's credentials. Must state which content types (ZDR threads, private connector content) can never be shared.

adrNeeded.topic: Learned and distributed behaviour: three-tier skill library (vendor, org, user), promotion gate and plugin supply chain
adrNeeded.why: The promotion gate is deliberately unbuilt pending a product decision while the loop already writes org-matchable skills; executable skill and plugin bundles add code supply-chain risk. One ADR should define scopes, approval, pinning and kill lists.

adrNeeded.topic: Model entitlements and provider credentials ownership (allowed_models has no owner; BYO keys custody)
adrNeeded.why: model-gateway refuses the OrgPolicy allowed_models field because no service owns it. Control Plane should decide and Model Plane enforce; bring-your-own provider keys must stay in Integration Core custody with ZDR and residency attestation per connection.

adrNeeded.topic: LLM reviewers on the permission path (revisit HAP WS-3 and ownership-matrix rule 12 for tighten-only monitors)
adrNeeded.why: Codex-style guardian reviewers conflict with the standing 'no LLM on the permission hot path' decision; only a tighten-only (deny or escalate, never grant) design could be compatible and needs an explicit ruling.

adrNeeded.topic: Connector content in shared Spaces and ZDR propagation for connector and web reads
adrNeeded.why: Personal mailbox and drive content read by an agent in a Space thread must not become visible to other members, and ZDR must propagate to connector reads, citations and research ledgers.

dropped.reason: Local execution host companion is explicitly parked by the owner and only applies to desktop/IDE products; Verevon is a cloud web product whose execution belongs in the per-thread sandbox computer (F-t3-009). Revisit only if user-desktop control is unparked by ADR.

Best-of-N parallel workspace attempts come from one IDE source (Cursor), conflict with the 2026-08-24 decision-ledger ruling against workspace isolation for parallel agents, and Verevon is not an IDE; multi-model comparison for answers is covered by the Model Council nice-to-have (F-t3-092).

items.title: One server-assembled run context for Do, Plan and scheduled runs: instruction stack, thread history, persona, memory and run notes
items.summary: Extract the ADR-0003 resolver (platform, org, Space, persona, summoned agent) that Ask turns already use into one shared function, add the missing fields to RunAgentRequest, and seed every Do, Plan and scheduled run with the resolved instructions, prior thread turns under the compaction budget, memory prefetch and attachments, with completeness flags on the run record. Automations later get a per-schedule notes block.
items.whyItMatters: Three consolidators found the same defect from different angles (runtime, extensibility, memory): the governed agent loop starts from a preamble plus the goal, so org policy, Space instructions, persona and memory are silently ignored exactly where the agent can take actions. Every reference agent inherits its conversation and instructions. It is the cheapest high-impact fix in the audit and it is a governance gap, not only a quality gap.

items.title: Durable agent loop: checkpoint every round and pause, resume in place after approval, answer or crash, close dangling tool calls, effect ledger
items.summary: Persist the Do loop's fold inputs in session-core at every round and before each effectful call, and add a continuation worker that re-enters the loop at the checkpoint when an approval, a clarifying answer or a crash recovery arrives, instead of re-executing three whitelisted effects from a cold descriptor. Close tool calls that never returned with typed closers, record effects in an exactly-once ledger, park turns whose providers are exhausted, and replay open interaction requests on reconnect.
items.whyItMatters: Today the LLM loop does not resume reasoning after an approval: only execute_provider_action, book_shipment and tickets.create are re-run from a descriptor. That makes every approval a dead end for multi-step tasks and blocks plan-continue, ask_user, scheduled runs with approvals, goals and the computer-use loop. Five of twelve references have durable resume; DeepSeek and Hermes show the exact mechanism.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: DeepSeek (checkpoint before model requests, tool effects and next steps; cold resume repairs the log tail) ; Hermes Agent
others: Hermes (refreshed turn lease with stall watchdog; about 30 failover reasons with a parked-turn countdown)
Cursor (auto-continue of interrupted agents, durable question delivery)
Manus (action ledger keyed by sessionUid and actionId with payload digest and replay horizon; only source)
Claude Desktop, Codex (visible reconnect, per-step model switch)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: R-t3-04-02: 5 of 12 sources for durable resume (common), 6 of 12 for provider retry and failover (common), 1 of 12 for the exactly-once ledger (unique to Manus) | R-t3-13-02: 3 of 12 (differentiator)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Persist before each model call and before each effectful tool. Hermes: the runtime sends a blocking request {id, method, payload, deadline} and the agent thread awaits the answer;

items.approach: Define a run-state schema in session-core (round cursor, message fold, pending interaction, effect ledger keyed by action id). Execution-core writes it before model requests, tool effects and pauses; a leased continuation worker resumes on decision events from the existing durable approval outbox. Implement typed closers (aborted-before-dispatch, not-started, outcome-unknown) so the model is told the truth about interrupted calls. Reuse Quarry-style receipts for the ledger. Depends on the renewable delegated credential (OD8) because the 300 s bearer expires during long pauses.
items.planeOwner: Model Plane (execution-core loop and continuation worker, session-core run state)
items.risks: Resuming with a stale or expired delegated bearer would either fail or tempt a service-principal shortcut: resume must re-authorise through Control. Exactly-once semantics for external effects are only as good as provider idempotency keys. ZDR runs must keep checkpoints content-free or memory-only.

verevon.constraints: ZDR: durable step records are content-redacted under ZDR and truncated to 2000 chars otherwise, so the fold cannot be rebuilt from step records and a ZDR run must not checkpoint content durably (refuse resume or keep it memory-only). Resume must re-authorize through Control with a fresh delegated bearer (OD8); a service-principal shortcut would break the delegated-identity rule. Model proposes / Quarry executes: browser_agent resumption stays excluded until a browser run itself survives a pause, and MCP tools have unknown idempotency so no exactly-once promise can be made for them. Fallback exhaustion handling lives in inference-core (FallbackChain), so parking is a gateway or run-state concern, not a provider change.
verevon.approachAdjustment: The item assumes an execution-core continuation worker re-entering the loop. The repo already has Temporal workflows with approval signals and per-turn checkpointed activities, but they drive ExecuteStep, and the chat Do path (model-gateway agentic_run_stream to RunAgent) bypasses Temporal; the item should state the host decision explicitly. Stage it: first a manual or automatic continue that starts a fresh run seeded by F-t3-001 context plus completed step summaries (plan B7 and OD6), then true in-place resume from a scrubbed fold checkpoint. Do not list replaying open interaction requests as new work (approvals already rehydrate, SSE replay exists); ask_user and park-on-provider-exhaustion are separable smaller items.
verevon.effortNote: Unchanged for the core slice (fold checkpoint plus in-place resume using the existing outbox and checkpoints table). If closers, effect ledger, parking, ask_user and credential renewal stay in one item it is XL, so split it.
verevon.verdictReason: The gap is real and verified (the Do loop cannot continue after an approval), but the item under-states what exists (outbox, descriptor worker, checkpoints table, rehydration, Temporal) and bundles at least four separable pieces.

items.title: Declared tool side-effect classes, a never-auto set and per-tool allow/ask/never policy, so MCP tools become callable through the signed gate
items.summary: Replace the substring classifier is_risky_tool with a declared SideEffectClass (read, read_sensitive, local_mutation, open_world_mutation, external_effect) bound in capability-core's trusted map for every built-in, provider action and discovered MCP tool (unknown defaults to external_effect), add a non-delegable never-auto set, and expose per-connector and per-tool allow/ask/never policy. With registry-owned capability bindings, MCP tools stop being refused by the gate and become usable in Do and, read-only, in Ask.
items.whyItMatters: The model cannot call any MCP tool today (plain chat strips mcp__ names; Do mode offers them but trusted_capability_id returns None so the gate refuses). MCP is table-stakes (6 of 12) and per-tool policy is the standard way references keep it safe. The substring classifier is also the weakest link in an otherwise strong signed-gate design: risk should be declared data, not guessed from names.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Hermes (MCP runtime: supervision and recovery, SRC) plus Perplexity web (per-tool allow/ask/never with thread grants, DOC) ; Manus (five declared side-effect levels plus MCP annotations drive policy) for the taxonomy; ChatGPT (graduated Always ask / read / low-risk / all app permissions) with Claude (per-connector never-allow set, Microsoft 365 write-path throttles) for connector policy
others: Claude desktop (direct MCP host, per-server process isolation)

items.approach: Add side_effect_class and MCP annotation hints to capability-core rows; derive MCP tool rows at discovery (readOnlyHint, destructiveHint) as children of the mcp_server capability with a durable digest so a changed tool list needs re-approval. Execution-core and model-gateway read the class instead of substrings; the autonomy rung table maps classes to allow/ask. Ship a per-tool policy store (allow, ask, never) at user and org scope, enforced in EvaluatePolicy, and a forged-call denial test.

items.risks: Mis-declared classes become silent over-permission, so unknown must default to the strictest class and declarations need review. MCP tool lists can change after approval (rug-pull); pin by digest. ZDR: MCP servers outside the attestation boundary must be refused for ZDR turns.

verevon.exactGap: Tool risk is judged by two undeclared mechanisms: execution-core matches name substrings and treats every mcp__ name as risky (permission/mod.rs:195-293), and capability-core rows carry only a 3-level risk_level that EvaluatePolicy consumes (models/capability.go:23-37; policy/engine.go:112-152), with no per-tool side-effect class. MCP tools are offered to Do runs but trusted_capability_id is a static map that returns None for them (capability_policy.rs:741-840), so execute_step_inner refuses every call before dispatch (runtime_loop/mod.rs:502; capability_policy.rs:361-362), and the inline Ask path refuses them by design (tool_loop.rs:625-642). The MCP annotation classifier McpToolAnnotations::side_effect exists with no production consumer (mcp_jsonrpc.rs:65-125), the static never-auto set is only tickets.create (permission/mod.rs:72-79), and there is no per-tool allow/ask/never store (hooks are an in-memory registry written only by gRPC RegisterHook).

McpToolAnnotations::side_effect() (ReadOnly, Destructive, NonDestructiveWrite, Undeclared) as the discovery-time input for MCP tool rows
The existing autonomy rung ladder: rung_required_for and check_autonomy_rung (permission/mod.rs:100-140) so classes map to rungs instead of adding a second table
requires_durable_owner_approval and requires_consent_to_disclose as the seed of the non-delegable never-auto set
integration_tools::operation_is_write (unknown fails safe to write) as the model for default-strictest classification
The PreToolUse hook engine for ask/deny rules that match mcp__* names, once hooks have a durable store
verevon.constraints: Model Plane owns capabilities, so declared classes and MCP tool rows must be registry-owned in capability-core and bound server-side; the binding may never be synthesised from a model-supplied name (capability_policy.rs:836-838), and trusted_capability_id is a synchronous static map today, so dynamic rows need an async registry lookup in execution-core. The code states that two risk tables would diverge (permission/mod.rs:81-92), so the declared class must replace is_risky_call as the input to rung_required_for rather than sit beside it. The inline loop has no continuation contract and the code says a gateway proxy for Ask would be an authority bypass until one exists (tool_loop.rs:625-638), so Ask-mode MCP reads are a later, separate contract. ZDR must propagate: ZDR turns run no inline tool loop (zdr_features.rs:150-185) and agentic runs carry zdr (execution.proto:100-107), so MCP servers outside the attestation boundary must be refused there. Hooks are an in-memory registry in model-gateway (state.rs:317, runtime_registries.rs:2003) with no gateway or SPA write path found, so they are not a policy store.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Reuse capability-core risk_level and the rung ladder: add a side_effect_class (or map risk_level plus annotations) on the capability row, derive MCP tool rows at discovery as children of the mcp_server row with a digest, make trusted_capability_id resolve dynamic mcp__server__tool names through the registry, and have rung_required_for and the permission engine read the class. Deliver Do-mode first; treat "read-only in Ask" as a follow-on that needs the inline continuation contract. Store per-tool allow/ask/never in capability-core (durable, user and org scope), not in the hook registry.
verevon.effortNote: L holds for Do mode (registry rows, async binding, class-driven rung mapping, policy store, forged-call test). Adding Ask-mode MCP reads would push it toward XL and should be split out.
verevon.verdictReason: The central claim is confirmed (MCP tools are offered but always refused, risk is name-guessed), but the item should build on the existing risk_level, rung ladder and McpSideEffect type, correct "unknown defaults" wording against those, and separate Ask-mode MCP into a later step.

items.title: Deliver the AI-action audit trail, then make it tamper-evident with a compliance query API and SIEM export
items.summary: Deploy the built-but-undeployed session-core audit outbox fixes from postmortem 0002 (publisher fix, requeue function, metrics), replay the 4,992 stuck governed-action events into audit-core and alert on the terminal-row gauge. Then add a per-org hash chain with a verifier, time-range export and a scoped compliance read API with webhook/SIEM fan-out in Control Plane Audit Core.
items.whyItMatters: Two categories flagged the same fact: governed agent actions were recorded but never reached the audit store. For a B2B agent product that takes actions on behalf of users this is a live compliance gap, and every enterprise reference (ChatGPT Compliance API, Claude, Perplexity) offers an exportable audit trail.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: claude ; ChatGPT (immutable Compliance Logs Platform plus a stateful API with per-category admin keys) and Perplexity (audit JSON streamed by webhook to Splunk/Slack); Cursor for breadth of recorded events (tool, hook, sandbox, classifier)

deepseek (counter-example: approvals recorded without actor identity)

referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Claude writes a per-session append-only audit.jsonl in which every entry carries an HMAC chained to the previous entry's hash, plus a verifier that reports the first broken entry. Transactional outbox per service -> audit core (append-only, hash-chained) -> query API with scoped admin keys plus webhook/SIEM fan-out;

items.title: Approvals v2: scoped decisions, typed cause codes, decision provenance, denial memory and step-up for high-risk effects
items.summary: Extend the approval decision from approve/reject to once, this run, this thread or always-as-a-reviewed-rule (an 'always' on a card is held at session scope until confirmed in settings), remember denials within a run, and compute a typed ApprovalCause at the point each permission, hook, capability or browser-risk decision is made. Carry {actor, verdict, cause, rule_id} in the approval event, the durable run log and audit, render a plain localised reason on every card, and require step-up for never-auto or high-risk effects.
items.whyItMatters: Approvals are already durable and stronger than most references (encrypted exact-effect descriptors, postcondition re-checks), but the cards say only that a tool requires approval and every decision is single-use, which produces approval fatigue and teaches users to click through. Codex, Claude and Antigravity show scoped decisions and typed causes as the fix.

items.title: Govern and prove the skill-learning loop: learned skills start as owner-scoped proposals, a seeded eval proves the loop, and a learning ledger supports undo
items.summary: Make every skill written by the background review a proposal owned by the user whose run produced it and not matchable by anyone else, with a Settings > Learning inbox (diff, reason, source run); promotion to org scope needs an admin decision. Then prove the loop end to end with a seeded eval (a real Do run authors a skill a later turn uses) and cost controls, and project memory and skill lineage into a 'What Verevon learned' ledger with undo and rollback.
items.whyItMatters: The learning loop runs by default and its candidates become org-wide matchable skills with no review, owner or scope. That is a data-governance risk (one user's run can change every colleague's agent) as well as a quality risk, and the loop has never been shown to produce a useful skill. Hermes, the reference for self-improvement, stages writes fail-closed and keeps a reversible ledger; Manus emits proposals.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: manus (proposal events); hermes (fail-closed staging) ; hermes ; hermes
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: R-t3-08-04: 4 of 12 sources (common). | R-t3-08-03: 2 of 12 sources (differentiator). | R-t3-10-06: 1 of 12 sources; unique
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Manus records each learning proposal as a KnowledgeEvent {CREATE/UPDATE/DELETE, PENDING/ACCEPTED/REJECTED, trigger, session_uid, session_event_uid} linked to the session event that produced it, and accepted items can later be enabled or disabled. Hermes forks a background review after the reply is delivered: only if a final response exists and the turn was not interrupted or unattended, it reviews a snapshot of the messages on a cheap model with whitelisted tools (memory, skill_manage) and read-before-write, capped at 16 iterations, with three prompt variants. A JSONL mutation ledger with a row per change {actor, entity, before_hash, after_hash, run_id};

items.title: Agent browser in chat and Do mode on real broker grants, with per-site read/act consent, admin allow/block lists and model-blind logins
items.summary: Replace the placeholder grant id 'session:{id}' with a real browser-broker grant minted per run, whose AllowedDomains come from a per-user site table (control, read only, no access) intersected with admin allow/block lists and the Space decision (block wins). Then expose browser_agent to the model in web-enabled chat and Do mode as a browser subagent with its own profile, budget and recording reference, add a read-only browsing objective usable from Ask and as a deep-research fallback, per-action state diffs, and secret substitution so logins never reach the model.
items.whyItMatters: Verevon already has the strongest browser contract in the comparison (revision-bound refs, risk-classified approvals, model proposes and Quarry executes), but it is unreachable from chat: agent browser runs fail closed because the broker only knows grants it minted. A working, governed agent browser is the first visible step toward the Manus-style 'acts like a PC' vision, and site governance is table-stakes (7 of 12).

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Antigravity (widest browser vocabulary, DOM/pixel/hybrid modes, per-action state diffs, recorded browser subagent) plus Manus (hybrid accessibility+DOM snapshot, versioned 22-tool contract with snapshot/ref/revision binding) ; Claude (per-site consent, admin default site policy with allow/block lists, DNS-pinned private origins) plus Perplexity Comet's per-domain Control / Read only / No access model; Manus for model-blind secrets ; Antigravity (separate read_url and execute_url permissions with a fail-closed server denylist; recording stored as an artifact and embedded in walkthroughs) plus Claude (approvals batched by site with an explicit allow-all switch) ; Manus web (web-manus-web-product-024 and -025, DOC) for live view and take-over; Claude (claude-product-ux-079, SRC) for the consent model

items.title: Per-thread sandbox computer behind a SandboxBackend seam: microVM backend, persistent thread workspace, typed executor protocol and visible lifecycle
items.summary: Add a SandboxBackend trait to sandbox-manager (leases already carry backend_id and endpoint) with bwrap as implementation 1 and a microVM backend (Firecracker or Kata, or one attested managed provider) as implementation 2 that stops when idle and snapshots to encrypted object storage. Extend the CAS workspace from Space scope to thread scope, define a typed executor protocol (the cloud loop proposes, the host executes), expose lifecycle states, typed failure causes and a heartbeat in the UI, and harden path handling.
items.whyItMatters: Every 'do the work' reference (Manus, ChatGPT agent, claude.ai, Perplexity) gives each task its own computer; Verevon runs hermetic per-call bwrap processes inside the execution-core container that cannot install tools, keep state or host a browser or desktop. This is the foundation for file analysis at scale, app building, the computer panel and computer use, and it is the biggest single architectural gap against the Manus/Claude vision.

items.approach: Phase 1 (W2): introduce the seam with bwrap as impl #1, lifecycle states and typed failures, thread-scoped workspace manifests. Phase 2 (W3): microVM backend with idle stop and encrypted snapshots, VM-seconds metering in cost-core, Control-signed lease decisions. Phase 3 (W4): browser and desktop inside the VM for F-t3-024. Keep bwrap/Landlock/seccomp as the in-guest second layer.

items.risks: Cost of idle VMs and snapshot storage; ZDR requires snapshot destruction and no content in logs; a thread workspace outside Spaces must not become a back door around Space ACLs; microVM supply chain and kernel patching become Verevon's responsibility. Needs an ADR before phase 2.

items.title: Connected apps that work in chat: prove Gmail, Outlook, Drive and Calendar reads end to end, add Ask-mode reads, @-connector scoping, citations, then approved writes
items.summary: integration-corev2 already implements real read operations (mail search and get, Drive search and content, windowed calendar). Close the Model Plane half: update execution-core's agent catalogue to the real operations, ship the read-only provider tool that does not stall on approval, expose the same reads in Ask mode behind the source-scope filter, add @connector mention and per-turn account scoping, cite connector sources, live-prove against real mailboxes, then enable writes behind per-action approval.
items.whyItMatters: Connected apps are table-stakes (6 of 11) and the main way a B2B assistant becomes useful on a user's own data. The plumbing exists on both sides but has never run end to end against a real account, and Ask-mode reads are parked (F12), so users cannot ask about their own mail in normal chat.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: ChatGPT connectors (web-chatgpt-web-product-043, DOC) for breadth and read vs write gating; Manus (manus-product-ux-041, SRC) for per-task toggles and account defaults ; Claude desktop (bundled GitHub server with device-code sign-in, token bound to host/client/scope, read-only and toolset switches, admin policy entries; SRC) plus Perplexity web (widest catalogue, project-level binding; DOC); Hermes for the in-chat connect flow (SRC)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: R-t3-03-04: 6 of 11 sources; table-stakes | R-t3-05-02: First-party connector catalogue: 4 of 12 sources, common; model-suggested connection flows: 3 of 12, differentiator
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Connector registry (OAuth per user, optionally per org) -> per-connector action catalogue tagged read or write -> per-task enablement and account selection resolved explicit > project > user default -> agent calls actions, writes need approval -> an @mention narrows the turn to one connector. Connector = provider OAuth app + curated action catalogue (typed inputs, read/write class, confirmation rule) + scopes;

Treat mail bodies and file text as untrusted content with the existing trust-class framing; respect ZDR by not persisting connector content on ZDR turns; tokens stay in integration-corev2.

items.title: Finish human-in-the-loop: plan approve-then-continue, a typed ask_user tool, and docked approval, plan, question and queue trays
items.summary: After a plan is approved the run continues on its own (grant and plan persisted in session-core, no extra user message). Add ask_user as a non-effectful builtin in both loops: a durable pause with a user_question ChatEvent and a card that supports single/multi select, free text and skip, resumed through the existing route. Render pending approvals, plan proposals, questions and the message queue as trays docked above the composer in priority order.
items.whyItMatters: Plan mode is table-stakes (9 of 12) and structured clarifying questions are common (6 of 12). Verevon has the editable plan card but the run stops after approval and there is no way for the agent to ask a question, so agents either guess or stall. Docked trays (Cursor, DeepSeek) keep the request visible during long runs.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Codex (decision-complete proposed_plan after a read-only interview; sync and async request_user_input) for plans; Manus (typed human-request socket messages) for questions ; Claude desktop (SRC) plus Antigravity (SRC) ; Cursor (trays for plan, questionnaire, queue, goal and subagents docked above the prompt) plus DeepSeek (timed question card with drafts and late replies; editable queue promotable to steering)
others: Cursor (late answers delivered durably into the paused run)
Claude Desktop, DeepSeek, T3 Code, web Manus and Perplexity (plan mode)
Hermes Agent (typed approval, clarify and masked secret prompts)

referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Plan: a mode flag on the run; A builtin ask_user tool with schema {questions:[{question, options[], multi_select, allow_write_in, rank}]} suspends the run and emits a typed event. Server to client request events {kind: approval|clarify|secret|plan, id, options, deadline};

Notify away users through the attention model of F-t3-015. Echo answers into the transcript as Q/A text so the context stays honest.

verevon.exactGap: Exists: plan mode with autonomy rung enforced at dispatch, the editable PlanApprovalControl and tool ApprovalRequests cards, a durable approval pause (execution-core mints an approval, flips the run to AwaitingApproval, returns early, resume re-invokes run_agent), and mid-run queued input (/v1/invoke/:id/queue, QueuedInputStrip). Missing: approving a plan does not start the executing run (approveTurnPlan only records the grant and turns plan mode off, and warns that the next message may lack the grant if it was not persisted; the closure plan carries B2, B5 and B7), the grant lives in the gateway's in-memory PlanModeStore (one replica, lost on restart), there is no ask_user tool, event or card anywhere in Model Plane or Frontend (grep), and approvals, plan card and queue render inside the transcript rather than as trays docked above the composer.

session-core SetRunMode (already durably persists run mode) as the carrier for a thread-scoped grant
PlanApprovalControl, ApprovalRequests and QueuedInputStrip components and the queued-input route
composer dock wrapper in ChatPage.tsx for the trays

verevon.constraints: ZDR: a ZDR credential is refused for plan approval, resume and any durable continuation (zdr_posture::continuation_gate, owner decision 17) because a ZDR run keeps no plan, todo or approval to advance, so approve-then-continue and a durable ask_user pause work only on persistent or waived runs; ZDR threads need an in-stream, non-durable ask or no ask_user. User answers are conversation content and follow normal persistence/redaction rules. The grant must be minted and validated server-side (the browser never selects authority) and bound to the run's receipts (plan B9). ask_user is a model proposal to the human, so it fits Model proposes / user decides, but it must be non-effectful and budgeted per run.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Sequence plan continuation first, as already planned (B2, B5, B7): move the thread-scoped grant from the gateway's in-memory map into session-core and start the executing run on approval. Model ask_user as a new interaction kind in the existing durable approval pause rather than a second pause state machine, and gate it off or make it ephemeral for ZDR threads. The docked trays are a layout change in the ChatPage composer dock and can ship independently of any backend work.
verevon.effortNote: Unchanged; trays alone are S to M, plan continuation is the already-planned M to L, ask_user is M.
verevon.verdictReason: The item's account of today matches the code (no continuation run, in-memory grant, no ask_user, in-transcript cards); the plan half is already planned work and the ZDR continuation constraint needs adding, but nothing here exists to drop.

reference.corrections: 1) Codex is not a model for 'approve-then-continue'. Its Plan Mode tells the model not to ask whether to proceed; the user switches out of Plan mode and asks for implementation in a new turn, which is what Verevon does today. Keep Codex as best-in-class only for the decision-complete plan content. For a plan approval that resumes the same run, cite DeepSeek: its exit_plan_mode review is an ask_user wait with an Approve card, so approving resumes the run (SRC README). The C-t3-04-024 mechanism claim that the run 'then continues automatically' is not supported by the Codex evidence. 2) Manus is mis-attributed for questions. The SRC record (manus-product-ux-127) covers typed confirmation and approval socket messages (touchpoint, cascade workflow, connector re-OAuth, and similar), not clarifying questions. items.title: Conversation history foundation in session-core: durable message tree with versions and fork, full-text search, a recall tool, paging and thread organisation
items.summary: Give messages a parent pointer, sibling ordinal and active-leaf pointer so regenerate and edit create persisted versions (with model or effort override), forks record lineage, and rewind is a confirmed supersede, never a delete. Add an owner-scoped Postgres full-text index with a search route and sidebar search, a read-only recall_conversations tool returning snippets as untrusted data, @thread references, cursor paging that removes the 80-thread cap, and archive, unread and star fields.
items.whyItMatters: Four consolidators asked for the same data model. Fork, versions and search are table-stakes (7-9 of 12) and users notice immediately when regenerated answers vanish on reload or old chats cannot be found. Hermes and Claude show the mechanism; the plan already has I8-I12, so this is mostly sequencing one shared schema instead of four features.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Hermes Agent (truncating rewind with durable row ids; FTS5 plus trigram search and a recall tool) ; Claude desktop (SRC) for fork, lineage and message actions; Perplexity and ChatGPT (DOC) for regenerate with model or effort ; Claude desktop (SRC) for search; T3 Code (SRC) and Claude desktop (SRC) for thread organisation ; hermes (search tool); deepseek (reference snapshot)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: R-t3-13-05: C-043: 1 of 12 (unique). C-011: 3 of 12 (differentiator). C-015: 2 of 12 (differentiator) | R-t3-01-02: 8 of 12 sources (fork) and 4 of 12 (message actions); table-stakes | R-t3-01-03: 7 of 12 sources (search) and 9 of 12 (organisation); table-stakes | R-t3-08-02: Search: 3 of 12 in the records (common, but table-stakes in practice since every chat product has it). Past-chat reference: 4 of 12 (common).
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Hermes: the user message is written durably before the turn runs; Each assistant turn stores model, mode and effort. A worker-backed index over transcripts per owner (limit 50, up to 200 sessions, archived optional) behind a palette with snippets and jump-to-message, plus an agent tool search_past_conversations(query, scope) whose snippets are treated as untrusted data and rendered as a visible tool call. Hermes: one tool with four shapes (discover, scroll around an anchor, read, browse) and no LLM calls;

verevonToday.gap: R-t3-13-05: SRC/DOC: the gateway has thread list, archive, delete, messages and events-replay routes but no fork, rewind, supersede or search route, and no tsvector or trigram index exists in session-core migrations (the only Postgres full-text work is in Data Plane v2). | R-t3-01-02: Edit-and-resubmit ships and effectful turns are immutable, but regenerate keeps 1/N versions for the final exchange only and loses them on reload; | R-t3-01-03: Only a client substring filter over a BFF list capped by MAX_THREADS = 80 (SRC history.rs:21,351) with no paging. | R-t3-08-02: No search RPC, no index, no UI search over message text, no agent recall tool, no @thread reference and no reference-chat-history setting.

items.approach: One session-core migration for the tree (parent_id, sibling ordinal, superseded_by, lineage root) and a tsvector index that excludes ZDR content and honours hard deletes; context assembly follows the active leaf. Then routes: regenerate/edit/fork/rewind/search/paging; then SPA. recall_conversations makes no model call and is owner-scoped; shared-Space threads need a Control-signed Space read decision.
items.planeOwner: Model Plane (session-core single writer, model-gateway routes) with Frontend Plane (sidebar, versions UI)
items.risks: Context leakage between siblings if assembly does not follow the active leaf; search index must never index ZDR turns and must honour erasure; recall snippets are a prompt-injection channel; branch semantics need owner decision OD19.

The @thread reference phase is not in that plan.

verevon.exactGap: Server side has thread list, archive, presentation (pinned_at, archived_at), messages and events-replay routes plus a memory lineage pattern, but no message parent/sibling/active-leaf, no fork, rewind or supersede route, no tsvector or trigram index, no search RPC, no recall_conversations tool (recall_memory is semantic memory and reattach_context reads only the current thread), no unread or star fields, and the BFF list is capped at MAX_THREADS = 80 with no cursor. Regenerate and edit versions are deliberately client-only, final-exchange-only and session-lifetime (chat-versions.ts) because an earlier persisted, nestable design was rejected in review (CHAT_RESUME_AND_VERSIONS_SPEC.md); sidebar search is a client substring filter and projects/filters live in client storage (chat-organization.ts). The plan carries I8 (branch), I9 (supersede) and I12 (search plus recall_conversations) with owner decision OD19 open.

plan rows I8, I9, I12 and OD19
verevon.constraints: No cross-plane DB: the full-text index must live in session-core (Model Plane Postgres), not in Data Plane v2 whose tsvector migration is documents only. ZDR turns must be excluded from the index and indexed rows must honour the durable erase contract on thread delete (http_routes.rs); Space-audience threads (migration 0025) need a Control-signed Space read decision for search and recall and must never widen an owner ACL. The rejected-design failure modes recorded in CHAT_RESUME_AND_VERSIONS_SPEC must be designed out: context assembly, learning review (ListConversation), Dreaming memory extraction, compaction and audit must read the active path only, effectful turns stay immutable, and branch semantics (OD19) are unresolved. recall results are a prompt-injection channel and stay owner-scoped.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Reword as reopening a previously rejected design with an active-path read model, and decouple the pieces: ship cursor paging, an owner-scoped full-text index with search route, and recall_conversations first (M, independent of branch semantics), then fork-as-copy with lineage (I8), then persisted versions/supersede (I9) only after OD19 and after ListConversation returns the active path for every consumer. 'One migration for four features' is the risky part, so sequence the tree last. Unread and star are small additive columns; pin and archive need only UI wiring.
verevon.effortNote: Unchanged in total; search, paging and recall are about M and the persisted message tree with active-path consumers is the L.
verevon.verdictReason: Gaps are real (no tree, search, recall, paging) but the item understates that persisted versions were explicitly rejected once and that server-side pin and archive already exist; the tree must be sequenced after the independent search and paging work.

items.title: Make Spaces the chat project: instructions, knowledge, members and a retrieval indicator in Ask and Do
items.summary: Replace the browser-only localStorage project organiser with Space-backed projects. A Space already carries governed instructions, Data Plane v2 knowledge and members, so add a project picker and folder view to the chat sidebar, apply Space instructions and retrieval scope in Do runs as well as Ask, and show a knowledge-mode indicator (in context versus retrieval). Also confirm and expose the multi-author Space room threads that session-core already stores.
items.whyItMatters: Projects are how every comparable product organises ongoing work (7 of 12 sources) and, for Verevon, they are the container that carries org governance: who sees what and which knowledge a run may retrieve. Today chat projects do not survive a browser change and Do runs ignore Space-authored instructions, so the vision of project-scoped agents is visibly missing.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Manus (SRC) plus Claude desktop (SRC) and claude.ai (DOC)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 7 of 12 sources; table-stakes
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: A project entity holds versioned, restorable instructions, files and links, default connectors and skills, members with read/write/full roles and a visibility policy (Manus ProjectService, 37 RPCs). Threads carry project_id and inherit that configuration. Knowledge stays in context while it fits and switches to a retrieval tool when it outgrows the window, with a visible indicator (Claude, claude.ai). Real-time multi-user use (C-031) is DOC-only: Manus lets up to 49 collaborators instruct one task, Perplexity uses head-checked optimistic concurrency.

verevonToday.gap: Chat projects are a client-only organiser (max 100) with no instructions, files, memory or sharing. The server container is Spaces, whose instructions are layered into Ask turns but not Do runs, and chat shows no knowledge-mode indicator. session-core already persists space_id, audience refs and a per-message author_subject_id (SRC, migrations 0023/0035), which suggests multi-author Space room threads exist at the data layer, but whether the Application Plane or SPA exposes them as a shared agent thread was not verified.

First step for the collaboration facet: read the Space room implementation and the author_subject_id read path and write down which actor's delegated token runs a collaborator-triggered agent turn.

items.title: Verified Office deliverables through executable SKILL.md bundles: docx, xlsx, pptx and pdf skills with structural checks, render-and-look and an in-panel previewer
items.summary: Accept the open Agent Skills format (SKILL.md plus references, templates and scripts) as bundles stored in object storage and run their scripts in the hermetic code_interpreter with the bundle mounted read-only. Prove it with first-party document skills: after writing a file the agent runs a checker (zip/XML validity, relationships, formula recalculation, slide count, page thumbnails via headless LibreOffice in bwrap without network) and only then returns a typed artifact, which the Output panel previews with a renderer registry.
items.whyItMatters: Producing real documents is table-stakes for an assistant that does work (5 of 11 sources create Office files through skills and a sandbox) and SKILL.md bundles are table-stakes for extensibility (9 of 12). Today Office files come from ad-hoc python scripts with no verification, so broken files reach users. DeepSeek's verify-and-render step plus Claude's skill-plus-sandbox shape is the best combination.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: DeepSeek harness (DOC) for the verify-and-render step, combined with Claude desktop (SRC) and claude.ai (DOC) for the skill-plus-sandbox shape; DeepSeek and Manus for the previewer ; claude.ai (open standard with three-stage loading, DOC) plus Claude desktop (six always-on document skills with scripts and validators, SRC)
others: Codex (tested helpers, distinct skill approval category)

referenceBestPractice.mechanism: One skill per file type (instructions, helper library, examples) injected when the request names a format. Parse SKILL.md frontmatter (name <= 64, description <= 200, optional dependencies);

Plans H3-H6 cover adjacent pieces; this item adds the verification and bundle shape they lack.

items.risks: Image size and cold start; LibreOffice parser CVEs (keep inside bwrap, no network); fidelity differences from Microsoft Office; third-party skill scripts are code execution and need the supply-chain rules of F-t3-059.

verevon.verdictReason: Gap confirmed (no bundles, no verification, no docx/xlsx/pptx preview), but the item bundles three separable deliverables and should name the CAS and sandbox pieces and plan items that already exist.

items.title: Attention model for long-running agents: closed run-state vocabulary, attention-ordered work list, typed alerts with Web Push, a live shell stream and an installable PWA
items.summary: Publish one server-derived run-state enum (working, needs_approval, needs_input, plan_ready, completed, failed, archived) on thread rows and rebuild the sidebar around it (Waiting for you, Working, Unseen results, Settled), mixing chats and agent runs. Emit typed attention events (approval, input, done, failed) as notification-core workflow types with a per-user channel matrix, add a tab badge, Web Push and an installable PWA, and push sidebar state over a per-user SSE shell stream instead of polling.
items.whyItMatters: Agents that run for minutes or hours are only useful if users learn when they are needed. Five of twelve references have typed notifications and the T3/Claude inbox pattern is the clearest UX in the comparison. Verevon has a per-run 'notify me when done' watcher but free-form status strings mapped to two chip tones and no push.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Claude desktop (per-type off|badge|banner for permission, idle and question, sounds, actionable notifications, a sessions-waiting-for-you list) plus Antigravity (distinct sounds for action-required and done, web push for remote sessions) ; T3 Code (inbox-style sidebar: pinned, active with status pills and elapsed time, snoozed, collapsed Settled) combined with Claude (closed state vocabulary, mark-completed, sections, group-by, bulk select, auto-archive, mixed chat and task Recents) ; T3 Code (live sync); Antigravity (one UI bundle for web, PWA, desktop and remote view)
others: Perplexity web (automations notify only when something noteworthy changed)
Claude.ai web and ChatGPT web (mobile parity and push)
ChatGPT web (Chat|Work toggle with mixed Recents)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: R-t3-12-02: Notifications: 5 of 12 sources; multi-platform and mobile reach: 6 of 12 (both table-stakes). | R-t3-12-01: Mixed Recents of chats and tasks: 6 of 12 sources (table-stakes). Attention-ordered inbox: 2 of 12 and sidebar organisation: 2 of 12 (differentiators). | R-t3-13-06: C-010: 4 of 12 (common). C-033: 5 of 12 (common). C-022: 3 of 12 (differentiator)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Run events map to a closed set of attention kinds {needs_approval, needs_input, finished, failed}. A server-derived state enum on every thread/run row; T3: the server attaches the live event buffer before taking the snapshot so no event is lost, coalesces per aggregate so bursts become one refetch per thread per window, and resumes after the client's snapshot sequence;

verevonToday.gap: R-t3-12-02: A per-run Notify me when done watcher exists (RunNotifyButton, capability-core runwatch to notification-core, delivered in the notification bell), and notification-core already has per-workflow, per-channel preferences and a retention_mode (standard|zdr) on every request (SRC). | R-t3-12-01: chatRunStatusChip maps free-form strings (queued/pending, running/in_progress, awaiting_approval/waiting_approval/paused/blocked/ambiguous, failed/timed_out/denied/rejected) to two chip tones, so there is no closed vocabulary shared with notifications and no attention ordering, snooze, settled tail or mark-completed... | R-t3-13-06: SRC: the SPA keeps a ZDR-aware derived localStorage cache and fetches thread lists and run states by REST.

items.approach: Phase 1: closed enum in mp-contracts plus thread-list paging; Phase 2: attention events into notification-core with the existing retention_mode (standard|zdr); Phase 3: PWA manifest, shell-only service worker, Web Push channel, per-user shell stream fed by the session-core outbox and NATS.
items.planeOwner: Model Plane (run-state, shell stream) with Application Plane (notification-core) and Frontend Plane (sidebar, PWA)
items.risks: Notification noise; push payloads must be content-free on ZDR threads; a service worker must never cache authenticated content.

verevon.exactGap: A per-run 'notify me when done' watcher exists end to end (RunNotifyButton.tsx -> runs-client watchRun -> capability-core runwatch consumer -> notification-core types modelplane.run_completed and run_failed, in-app on by default, email opt-in) on top of a notification-core with per-user per-channel preferences, retention_mode standard|zdr and a navbar bell, but runwatch maps only RUN_COMPLETED and RUN_FAILED. Run state travels as free strings (runs.proto comment, session-core is_terminal_run_status, CoreSidebar chatRunStatusChip, chat-organization.ts status sets, three divergent client unions), so there is no closed vocabulary, attention ordering, needs_approval or needs_input alert, tab badge, per-user shell stream, service worker, manifest or Web Push (no PushManager, VAPID or manifest code in verevonv3 or Application Plane). The only typed seeds are execution-core's RunStatus enum and the run.paused_for_approval and approval.state_changed event names, whose orchestrator-core publishers the broker drops.
reuse: runwatch consumer plus the notification-core registration-migration pattern (013) for each new attention type
notification-core preferences/channels API and retention_mode (standard|zdr)
execution-core RunStatus enum and the durable approval pause as the source of needs_approval
chat-organization.ts attention/active sets and CoreSidebar chip as the client seed for the closed enum
CoreNavbar unread badge and /api/v1/notifications client for the in-app side
existing per-run run_events SSE as the model for a per-user shell stream
verevon.constraints: ZDR must propagate: notification-core README says the full payload still reaches Novu and ZDR content delivery must stay off until a provider-side contract is proven, so every attention notification must be content-free (generic title plus deep link) on all threads, not only ZDR ones. Do not rely on orchestrator-core's mp.v1.orchestration.* publishers: the publishers registry lists its plan, todo, approval, subagent and run subjects as known gap rows (deploy/nats.conf grants it only mp.v1.run.*.event, so the broker drops them) and the postmortem found MP_ORCHESTRATION_EVENTS empty, so typed run-state events must be written by session-core (single writer of run state) through its outbox/terminalization path, or the grants must be fixed first. Application Plane owns notifications and realtime projections, so Web Push subscriptions and the per-user shell stream belong there or in the gateway BFF, with Model Plane only publishing typed events; the service worker must never cache authenticated content; no cross-plane DB reads.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Re-home the shell stream and Web Push: Model Plane publishes the closed run-state enum and typed attention events, Application Plane (notification-core plus a realtime projection) owns push subscriptions and the per-user stream, Frontend owns PWA and sidebar. Split the XL into three shippable deliverables: (1) enum plus needs_approval/needs_input/plan_ready events plus sidebar ordering, (2) Web Push plus manifest plus content-free payloads, (3) shell stream replacing REST refetch. Fix the orchestrator-core publish-grant gap, or use the session-core outbox, before anything depends on NATS fan-out.
verevon.effortNote: Unchanged: three planes, a new subscription store, and a broker-grant fix; deliverable (1) alone is L.
verevon.verdictReason: The item's description of today (watcher exists, free-form status strings, no push, no PWA) matches the code; only the plane placement of the shell stream and push and the broker-drop constraint need correcting, which approachAdjustment covers.

items.title: Multi-replica-safe run control: shared cancel, queued-input, plan-mode and turn state, durable send receipts and an editable message queue
items.summary: Move process-local run control in model-gateway (cancel flags, queued input, plan-mode flags, team workers, the chat-turn map, hook and command registries) behind run-id-keyed shared state in Redis/Dragonfly with NATS fan-out, and make duplicate-send protection durable using session-core receipts. Turn on the Redis stream buffer in every environment. On top, add queue routes (list, reorder, cancel, promote), a queue dock and a split send button (interrupt, steer at the next boundary, or queue).
items.whyItMatters: A model-gateway restart or a replica move currently loses in-flight cancels, queued messages and plan state; the stream buffer is in memory unless REDIS_URL is set. No reference is multi-tenant and multi-replica, so this is Verevon's own problem to solve, and it is a precondition for durable runs, ask_user and the attention stream.

verevon.constraints: Queued mid-run input is deliberately classified by the model at the round boundary (the code says the caller cannot know), so a user-picked interrupt, steer or queue split button contradicts a documented design ruling and needs an explicit decision. Buffered frames and queued text hold content, so ZDR turns stay memory-only (compose notes the ZDR path does not buffer). The compose files read configure no model-gateway replicas, so multi-replica safety hardens a topology that is not deployed; Dragonfly runs cache-mode at 256 MB shared and can evict, and Redis becoming a hard dependency needs a down-behaviour rule. Ordering across replicas needs idempotent operation ids.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Remove "turn on the Redis stream buffer in every environment" (already set in the compose block; only confirm it is deployed). Reword the problem: graceful redeploys are covered by drain, so the loss window is a crash, OOM or replica move. Scope shared state to cancel and enqueue routed through a request_id-keyed NATS subject, as the in-code notes propose, and reuse session-core idempotency for durable receipts rather than a new store. Drop the editable queue and split send button from this item unless the owner overrides the model-classifies design.
verevon.effortNote: Reduced from L: the Redis buffer, drain and durable receipts are already in place and the queue UX conflicts with the current design; the remaining shared cancel and queue state is M.
verevon.verdictReason: Real but a scale-readiness hardening for a single-replica deployment with drain and Redis resume already shipped, and it is not a precondition for durable runs because approvals already persist in session-core; the queue UX part needs a design decision first.

reference.corrections: T3 Code is the best source for idempotent command receipts, not for multi-replica safety. Its engine is a single-process, single-writer in-memory queue and read model; only the receipts and events are durable in SQL. No reference implements multi-replica run control: DeepSeek only documents that it is process-local, so C-057 is effectively 0 of 12 solving it. In Claude, stream recovery as observed is poll-based: fast polls, then a slow-poll phase after maxPollAttempts, then 'exhausted'. That recovery path is used for detached or pending replies. 'Resumes the stream first, then polls' was not observed, so drop 'resumes first' or mark it INF. Claude's queue operations are local desktop IPC (LocalSessions), not server-side state shared across replicas.
caveats: Priority for multi-replica safety derives from Verevon's own code, not from any reference

items.title: Attachments v2: fail closed on unsupported media, durable reference-based uploads, and sandbox analysis of the user's files
items.summary: First (quick win) expose model capability fields to the composer, refuse unsupported media with a stated reason instead of silently stripping attachments on the ChatGPT subscription route, and pass images as parts on vision routes instead of diverting the whole turn to AnalyzeImage. Then wire the existing durable upload route so turns carry Data Plane document ids instead of 1 MB of pasted text, add PDF page images and local OCR, and stage attachments read-only into the code_interpreter workspace (plan H6) with a per-thread session workspace.
items.whyItMatters: Uploading a spreadsheet and asking for analysis is table-stakes (4 of 11 for analysis, 4 of 11 for multi-format attachments) and Verevon caps files at 1 MB and 60k characters while peers accept 30-512 MB. Silent attachment stripping is an honesty bug that contradicts Verevon's own 'never fake success' rule.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: claude.ai (DOC) with the Claude desktop document funnel (SRC) for limits and conversion; DeepSeek harness (DOC) for the store; T3 Code (SRC) for the client queue ; DeepSeek harness read_image (SRC) for fail-closed tools and Antigravity (SRC) for the composer-level MIME table ; claude.ai (DOC) and ChatGPT web (DOC), equivalent; Perplexity (DOC) uses Firecracker microVMs
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: R-t3-02-02: Attachments: 4 of 11 sources (3 distinct vendors), table-stakes (class adjusted by comparator). Content-addressed store and queue: 2 of 11, differentiator. Link chips: 1 of 11, unique | R-t3-02-03: 2 of 11 sources; differentiator | R-t3-02-04: 4 of 11 sources, all documentation-only; table-stakes (class adjusted by comparator)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Presigned direct upload into object storage so no bytes pass through the chat API. Each model catalogue entry declares input modalities, supported MIME types and a max size per type. A per-conversation sandbox session, stateful across calls, with uploaded files mounted read-only at a known path, preinstalled data libraries, a per-call limit measured in minutes, an org egress policy (off, package managers, allowlist, all), and outputs (PNG charts, CSV, XLSX) returned as artifacts and rendered in an expandable viewer.

verevonToday.gap: R-t3-02-02: Caps are 1 MB per file, 60,000 characters per file and 120,000 per turn (SRC prepare-chat-attachments.ts:6-43). | R-t3-02-03: The SPA sends attachments: [] when the provider is the ChatGPT subscription route (SRC chat-client.ts:1144), and also disables tools, web, image generation, deep research and skills there; | R-t3-02-04: The code_interpreter contract already accepts files_in {name, content_b64} and handle_code_interpreter forwards it (SRC), but the only source of those bytes is the model's own base64, so a chat attachment cannot reach the sandbox (plan H6 not built).

items.approach: Phase 1 (W1): capability gating and typed refusals (R-t3-02-03) plus H6 staging (resolve attachment references to files_in server-side). Phase 2 (W2): durable uploads with per-route token budgets, retrieval for the remainder, OCR (H9), upload queue with content-addressed ids scoped per org. Bytes are read through Data Plane APIs, never by direct DB access.
items.planeOwner: Model Plane (gateway, execution-core) with Data Plane (blob store, extraction) and Frontend Plane (composer, queue)
items.risks: Storage and retention must follow org policy and ZDR (refuse persistence under ZDR); cross-tenant dedup leaks existence, so hash per org; deletion must cascade to derived documents and workspaces.

verevon.constraints: ZDR and sovereignty: durable upload is refused under ZDR (412) and OD18 recommends holding binaries in memory only for the run, so durable-by-default conflicts with ZDR; make durability an org-policy opt-in and hash content per org. The existing durable route is text-only and asynchronous (the sending turn saw only the first chunk when measured), so wiring it as-is recreates the failure that client-side inlining fixed. Bytes must reach the sandbox through Data Plane or an ephemeral model-gateway store, never by direct DB access, and a Do run only receives what model-gateway resolves into RunAgentRequest. Vision turns are already refused for waived ZDR turns.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Correct the premise: on the subscription route only image parts are dropped; text and extracted PDF, DOCX, XLSX and PPTX still reach the model because they are inlined into content. The cheapest first step is client-only: read the existing vision feature flag from the catalogue, disable or explain image attach on routes without it, and send images as parts on vision routes instead of diverting the turn (sse.rs:1409). For H6 add a bounded attachment-reference field to RunAgentRequest resolved by model-gateway from an ephemeral per-run store; treat durable reference-based uploads, PDF page images and OCR as a later phase, and size against OD18 (4 MB, 60k chars) rather than the 30-512 MB of peers.
verevon.effortNote: Unchanged as a whole; phase 1 (capability gating, image parts, typed refusal) is S to M and can ship alone.
verevon.verdictReason: Gaps are real, but the silent-strip claim applies to images only, the durable route is text-only and async, and capability fields already exist server-side, so the phasing and approach must change.

reference.corrections: 1) 'Presigned direct upload into object storage so no bytes pass through the chat API' is not shown by any cited reference. T3 Code uses signed upload URLs to its own local server, which writes files to disk. DeepSeek stores content-addressed objects on the local filesystem under DSH_HOME. Label this as Verevon design (INF). 2) The claude.ai limits conflict between articles: the upload article gives 500MB per chat file (30MB for project files), but the file-creation/code-execution article gives 30MB per file for uploads and downloads in the sandbox. State both rather than '500MB' alone. 3) The egress tiers are confirmed for claude.ai Team/Enterprise (DOC), with plan-specific defaults: Team defaults to package managers, Enterprise defaults to off. 4) 'Uploaded files mounted read-only at a known path' and 'per-call limit measured in minutes' were not found in the claude.ai articles checked. Mark as INF or remove the attribution to claude.ai. 5) Best-in-class for the store: DeepSeek is backed by in-repo README plus source files (store.ts, file-store.ts), so it could be upgraded from DOC to SRC, but it is single-machine. The T3 Code queue is image-only; generic files follow a different path. 6) The fail-closed parts (DeepSeek read_image, Antigravity per-model supported_mime_types plus refusal copy) are confirmed SRC.
caveats: Sandbox data analysis (C-t3-02-027) is DOC-only for all four sources (claude.ai, ChatGPT, Manus, Perplexity). Perplexity Firecracker was not re-verified.

The Antigravity link-chip feature is a single-source SRC record at medium confidence.
The presigned object-storage upload path is a design proposal (INF), not reference behavior.

items.title: Scheduled runs become governed, tool-using Do runs with a stored approval contract, non-delegable tools, result delivery and origin attribution
items.summary: Replace the single no-tool 1,024-token call in ExecuteScheduledStep with a normal budgeted Do run started by the Temporal supervision, seeded with context. At schedule creation the owner signs a consent card whose approved capabilities are stored with an expiry; at run time an effect proceeds only if covered and delegable, otherwise the run drafts and notifies off-surface (without an Allow button for high-risk tools). Deliver results ('See results'), and tag runs with origin.
items.whyItMatters: Scheduled agents are near-universal (10 of 12) and the Agents pages promise them, but each Verevon step is a stateless completion. The owner ruling of 2026-09-28 (draft-only) is compatible with this design: the stored contract can start as read plus draft-only and widen later by explicit decision.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Hermes (cron jobs as full agent runs with skills, context chaining, multi-platform delivery and an at-most-once ledger) ; Claude (scheduled tasks store approvedPermissions with expiry, a non-delegable tool set, and notifications that drop the Allow action for high-risk tools) with Hermes (headless modes deny by default with a narrowed toolset and auto-pause on injection hits)
others: Manus (schedule model with expiry and run target)

verevon.constraints: Authority is Control Plane: the signed decision already binds the template digest, an expiry and a ZDR refusal, and is re-verified at fire and per step, so a stored approved-capabilities contract belongs in the Control-committed template or action schema (plan D3 run profile, with D2 digest parity first), not a new Model Plane table. Schedules are Space-scoped and service-owned; unattended effects need the D10 identity and an ADR amending the draft-only ruling, and no Control bearer may persist in Temporal history. Approvals cannot use the interactive pause (the workflow fails closed), so they need Application Plane delivery; ZDR schedules stay blocked.

verevon.verdictReason: The gap is verified (single tool-less completion, no stored contract, results disabled) but much of the proposal duplicates planned rows D3 to D11, and the contract must live in Control rather than Model Plane.

items.title: Real Agents and Automations hubs: versioned agent definitions, named agents, automations with run now and pause, and a working Fleet console
items.summary: Introduce a versioned agent definition (name, instructions, tool allowlist bound to capability ids, model policy, autonomy cap, knowledge scope, schedules, owner and Space scope) in the capability registry and use it three ways: selectable roles for subagents, a builder with sandbox preview, and persistent named agents with their own thread and memory. Turn the agent pages from design previews into hubs over owner-plane resources, add an Automations hub over /api/v1/cron with Active/Paused/Completed and Run now/Pause/Edit, and fix the Fleet console, which calls a route that does not exist.
items.whyItMatters: The audit is about the chat and agent pages, and the agent pages are largely blueprints: preset agents have empty action sets, the workflow builder and chatbot studio are previews, and the fleet console has no backend route. Perplexity and Manus show hubs; Cursor, Codex and ChatGPT Workspace Agents show definitions and builders.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Perplexity web (hubs for tasks, connectors, automations with Active/Paused/Completed and Run now/Pause/Edit/Pin/Delete, skills, memory) plus Manus (Agents tab, Automations panel) ; Manus (named persistent agents with their own email, phone, computer and skills) for identity; Cursor (agent definition files with tools, model and permission mode) for roles; ChatGPT Workspace Agents (versioned spec, preview, deployment with activity log) for the builder
others: Cursor (team-published named agents pinned to member sidebars)
Perplexity (Computer from forwarded email, Slack-bound projects)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: R-t3-12-04: 3 of 12 sources (differentiator). | R-t3-04-06: persistent named agents 5 of 12 (common); custom roles 2 of 12; builder and deployment 2 of 12; non-app entry points 4 of 12
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Each hub is a list over an owner-plane resource with a state filter and row actions bound to typed APIs. Agent{id, owner, persona, instructions, memory scope, skills, channels[], autonomy_cap, version}.

items.approach: Phase 1 (W3, after F-t3-018): Automations hub and Fleet console on existing APIs; remove honesty-badged previews from navigation until backed. Phase 2: agent definition record and builder, with action sets populated from the typed action registry (F-t3-025). Phase 3: persistent named agents with scoped memory (F-t3-060).
items.planeOwner: Model Plane (capability registry, runs) with Application Plane (cross-Space agent registry, ADR-0002) and Frontend Plane (hubs)
items.risks: Scope creep into a workflow product; persistent agent identities need an authority model (whose token runs a named agent) that must not widen owner-plane ACLs.

verevon.exactGap: Schedules are already managed in Settings (CronSchedulesSection) and in chat (ScheduleDialog and ScheduledRunsPanel, which has pause and delete), with Space Work linking to /settings/cron (SpaceWorkPanel.tsx:182), over /api/v1/cron with enable/pause toggle, create and delete (CronSchedulesSection.tsx:229; cron-client.ts:54-103); but capability-core serves only list, create, get, patch and delete (workplane_apis.go:856-871), so there is no Run now and no run history ("See results" is a disabled stub, ScheduledRunsPanel.tsx:10-30,141). The Fleet console fetches /v1/fleets/:id (FleetRunConsole.tsx:27-33) which the dev proxy does not forward (vite.config.ts:65-75), the gateway has no fleets route, and only quarry-edge defines it (fleet_routes.rs:6-13); preset agents have empty action sets (preset-agents.ts:48-64), agent installations have a GET-only route (spaces.rs:688-691), and the agents page marks its blueprint surfaces with the design-preview badge (AgentsPage.tsx:285; DesignPreviewBadge.tsx:3-12). Agent definitions already exist in the Application Plane Convex agents table (name, systemPrompt, model, tools, knowledgeBindings, embed) plus Space bindings with in-room create, bind, pause and revoke, but they are unversioned with string tool names, and subagent.task has no role parameter (agent.rs:4278).
reuse: Convex agents definition table plus spaceAgents bindings and the gateway Space agent routes (create, bind, pause, revoke, installations) from ADR-0002
capability-core CronHandler, cron.Sweeper and ControlFireAuthorizer, plus cron-client.ts and the two existing schedule UIs (CronSchedulesSection, ScheduleDialog/ScheduledRunsPanel)
AgentRunConsole run, plan and proof APIs and decideApproval
quarry-edge /v1/fleets routes (create, get, members, budget) behind a Quarry-audience BFF proxy, following the artifact proxy pattern in json_handlers.rs:440-447
The internal SubagentRole::Researcher tag (execution-core research_fan_out) as the seed for selectable subagent roles
DesignPreviewBadge honesty contract for anything left unbacked
verevon.constraints: Agent definitions already live in the Application Plane (Convex agents plus Space bindings, ADR-0002) and Control owns the Space membership of service principals, so putting a new definition in the capability registry would create a second definition store. Cron fires are re-authorised by Control on every fire (cron-client.ts:33-36; capability-core main.go:316-325), so Run now must use the same Control fire authorisation and not call StartWorkflow directly. Fleets are a Quarry/Control concept (quarry_fleets); no producer exists in Model Plane or the gateway, so a Fleet console needs a Quarry-audience BFF proxy and Quarry org scoping. Named persistent agents need an explicit authority model (whose delegated token runs) and must not widen owner-plane ACLs; room agents today are presentation plus Control service membership.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Phase 1 is not "on existing APIs" for Run now and run history: capability-core needs a Control-authorised run-now endpoint and a fires/runs listing (cron_fires has no thread link, per ScheduledRunsPanel.tsx:10-30), while Pause, Resume and Edit already work through PATCH. For the Fleet console either add a gateway /api/v1/fleets proxy to quarry-edge or remove the route until something creates fleets. Phase 2 should extend the Convex agents definition and Space binding (version history, tool allowlist as capability ids, autonomy cap) and have Model Plane consume the resolved definition at invoke time, as inject_mentioned_space_agent_persona already does for personas. Consolidate the two existing schedule UIs into the hub rather than adding a third.
verevon.effortNote: Unchanged. Phase 1 alone (hub over existing PATCH/list, Fleet proxy or removal) is M; adding run-now plus run history is M more; versioned definitions, builder and persistent agents are the XL part.
verevon.verdictReason: Preview-only pages and the broken Fleet route are confirmed, but the item ignores the existing Convex agent definitions and Space agent flow, misplaces the definition store in capability-core, and understates the backend work behind Run now.
