items.title: User and org memory controls: on, pause, reset and org policy
items.summary: Add a user memory state (on, paused, off) and a Reset all memory action, plus an org policy that can disable memory and the learning review, enforced in session-core at every place memory is written or read: the Dreaming loop, prefetch, save_memory, recall_memory and the skill review. Add an immediate in-chat 'remember this' path in Ask mode that confirms the save, refused under ZDR.
items.whyItMatters: Users and enterprise admins expect to be able to stop the assistant learning about them, and a product that learns by default needs this before it can be sold to Norwegian and EU buyers. It is table-stakes (9 of 12 sources) and today half built: you can view, correct and delete entries but not switch learning off or wipe it in one action. Raised to priority from the comparator's recommended because of the governance inconsistency described below.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: web-claudeai / claude desktop
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 9 of 12 sources (table-stakes); org-level governance 3 of 12 (common).
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Claude keeps topic-based entries saved during chat, each visible and editable, with 'remember' and 'forget' in chat, separate pause (keep rows, stop using and generating) and reset (erase) actions, an org opt-in on Team plans and a transcript indicator when memory is read or written. Perplexity lets the org owner switch derived features on or off for all members. Implementation shape: per-account flags generate and reference give on, paused and off; paused keeps rows but skips prefetch and extraction.

evidence: apps/Model Plane/rust/services/session-core/migrations/0039_memory_user_control.sql (user_memory_controls holds only extract_after and forgotten ids, not a switch)
apps/Model Plane/rust/services/session-core/src/dreaming.rs:146-150 (Dreaming interval and batch configured only by env; no per-user or org gate)
apps/Model Plane/rust/services/session-core/src/dreaming.rs:1-8 (deterministic phrase matcher already catches Norwegian husk at / jeg heter, but only when Dreaming runs, with no confirmation)
apps/Control Plane/user-core/internal/http/handlers.go:1405-1421 (AISettings has memoryEnabled with default false, personalizationEnabled and dataCollectionEnabled)
No reader of memoryEnabled or personalizationEnabled in apps/Model Plane (rs, go, proto) or the SPA src (SRC grep); gateway dispatchers.rs:666 uses settings/ai only for workflowPolicies
verevonToday.gap: No user-level memory on, pause or off switch, no Reset all, no org-level memory policy found (bounded grep of Control Plane for memory_enabled, memoryPolicy, allow_memory found only the user-core settings above), and injection and extraction are unconditional server-side. Control Plane already models a memoryEnabled flag that defaults to false, yet nothing enforces it and the Model Plane learns regardless, so the stored setting and actual behaviour disagree. Ask-mode chat has recall_memory only; save_memory is Do-only.

items.approach: Use Control Plane as the single source of truth: reuse user-core AISettings (memoryEnabled, personalizationEnabled) and add an org policy {memory_allowed, member_default}. Deliver the decision to the Model Plane signed with the session or run decision (no cross-plane DB access), and enforce it in session-core in the Dreaming loop, memory_prefetch.rs, save_memory and recall_memory, and in the capability-core skill review (R-t3-08-03). States: on, paused (rows kept, prefetch and extraction skipped), off. Add a ResetMemory RPC that reuses memory_erasure.rs for both tiers. Frontend: toggles and Reset in MemorySection, an admin control in org settings, and a visible indicator on the turn when memory is read or saved (the memory_recall event already exists). Add a gateway write route for an immediate Ask-turn 'remember this' that returns a confirmation chip. Decide and document the default (the user-core default is off; the current Model Plane behaviour is on) and migrate existing users deliberately.
dependencies: Control Plane user settings and org policy
items.planeOwner: Model Plane (enforcement); Control Plane (settings and org policy); Frontend Plane (controls)
items.risks: A paused state must also stop the background extractor and the skill review, or memories and skills appear while paused. Changing the default affects existing users. ZDR orgs should be treated as memory-off for writes.

verevon.exactGap: Users can list, correct and delete memories (memory.rs:50-54; MemorySection.tsx:69; memory-client.ts:69-101) but there is no on/paused/off state, no Reset all and no org memory policy: user_memory_controls holds only extract_after and forgotten ids (0039_memory_user_control.sql:3-8), Dreaming is configured by env only (dreaming.rs:146-150), and the chat recall gate checks only conversation_only, web-only scope and trivial prompts (sse.rs:1655). Control Plane user-core already stores memoryEnabled (default false) and personalizationEnabled in AISettings (handlers.go:1405-1421) but nothing else in apps reads them, so the stored default (off) contradicts actual behaviour (learning on); Ask turns can recall but not save (inline_tool_allowed refuses save_memory, tool_loop.rs:639), and only per-turn exclusions exist (ZDR turns neither read nor write, zdr_features.rs:166; conversation_only skips extraction, dreaming.rs:223).
reuse: session-core user_memory_controls (add a state column) as the enforcement copy, instead of a new table
memory_erasure::erase_semantic_copies and the gdpr bulk erase (memory_erasure.rs:112; gdpr.rs:444) for Reset across both tiers
BFF stamping precedent apply_org_zdr_posture (shared.rs:95-117): a server-set field stripped from client bodies, for request-time recall and save gates
org_quota-style service-principal pull from org-core for org policy and for the Dreaming worker, which has no request context
user-core AISettings (memoryEnabled, personalizationEnabled) as the user preference store, once the default conflict is resolved
Existing per-turn gates to extend: conversation_only in sse.rs:1655 and dreaming.rs:223, memory_tool_preflight (runtime_loop/mod.rs:2125)
verevon.constraints: Memory data and learning are Model Plane (session-core) but user preference and org policy belong to Control Plane (CLAUDE.md:23), with no cross-plane DB reads: request-time paths can take a BFF-stamped server-set field, while the Dreaming worker and the skill/learning review run without a request and need a service-principal pull or a pushed projection. Pause must also gate the background extractor and the learning/skill review (session-core learning_events.rs and capability-core learning/reviewer.go exist per grep and were not re-read), otherwise memories or skills appear while paused. ZDR must propagate: ZDR turns already skip memory (zdr_features.rs:166), and ZDR orgs should be treated as memory-off for writes. Changing the default from today learning-on to the stored off value affects every existing user and needs a deliberate migration.
verevon.approachAdjustment: The item's "signed with the session or run decision" is heavier than the codebase needs: use the BFF-stamp pattern for chat turns and a service-principal pull (org_quota.rs pattern) for Dreaming and learning review, or make session-core user_memory_controls the single enforcement copy written through a gateway route when the user toggles, keeping user-core AISettings.memoryEnabled as a mirror or retiring it so there are not two switches. Settle the memoryEnabled=false versus learning-on default before shipping. Keep the Ask-mode "remember this" path as a separate optional step.
verevon.effortNote: M for a user-level on/paused/off switch plus Reset (session-core state column, Dreaming and recall gates, gateway route, MemorySection controls). Org policy, learning-review gating and the Ask-mode remember path make the full item L.
verevon.verdictReason: Gap is accurate and verified (no switch, no reset, no org policy, stored flag unread), so the recommendation stands; the approach should reuse the BFF-stamp and org_quota pull patterns, and effort is larger than M once org policy and learning review are included.

items.title: Transcript performance: benchmark first, then block-level streaming render, a virtualised timeline and paged transcript reads
items.summary: Add a long-transcript render benchmark and a cold-start request budget in Playwright, then ship the planned block-level incremental Markdown render (re-parse only the trailing block, frame-batched deltas), virtualise the message list with a live-follow rule and scroll-to-end pill, move heavy highlighting to a worker, load transcripts tail-first through a paged message endpoint, and reload once on unrecoverable chunk errors.
items.whyItMatters: Long agent runs are exactly where Verevon wants to win, and today every streamed token re-parses the whole message and nothing is virtualised. Users notice jank immediately. T3 Code and Claude show the mechanism; plan I5 covers only part of it.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Claude desktop (REA: 257 lazy modules registered in three tiers with largeClosure markers and a reload policy for unrecoverable chunk errors) plus T3 Code (virtualised timeline, lazy heavy panels, capped hidden mounts, workers) ; T3 Code (SRC) for the virtualised timeline; DeepSeek harness (DOC) for freezing completed blocks
others: DeepSeek (e2e test that counts startup RPCs against a budget)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: R-t3-12-05: 4 of 12 sources (common). | R-t3-01-06: 4 of 12 sources; common
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Message list virtualisation with measured row heights; Memoise all but the trailing one or two blocks, keep an open code fence's parse node and resume the highlighter grammar state line by line, skip colouring very long lines.

verevonToday.gap: R-t3-12-05: Route-level lazy loading exists (31 lazy routes, a lazy chart). | R-t3-01-06: No list virtualisation in chat (a grep for 'virtual' in features/chat matches only chat-code-highlight.ts, apparently incidental);

items.approach: Measure first, then I5, then virtualisation and paged reads (session-core before_seq/limit). Keep Mermaid/KaTeX deferral; ensure find-in-page and accessibility survive virtualisation (hidden=until-found pattern from DeepSeek).
items.planeOwner: Frontend Plane (renderer, virtualiser) with Model Plane (paged reads)
items.risks: Variable-height rich content causes scroll jumps; selection, find and screen readers need care.

The benchmark, budget test, worker and chunk self-heal are not planned. | R-t3-01-06: Partly: plan I5 block-level streaming render and frame-batched deltas (apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/apps/verevon-web/plans/system-audits/CHAT_GAP_CLOSURE_PLAN_2026-10-01.md:217); virtualisation and paged reads are not in the plan

There is no DOM-level long-transcript benchmark, no cold-start request budget and no vite:preloadError self-heal, and plan I5 (block-level render) is still unbuilt.

items.summary: Turn on and measure what is built: enable the OpenAI stable-prefix order in staging, record cache read/write tokens and a cache-miss reason per route, then define a prompt-tier contract in mp-contracts for both loops (org and Space blocks in the shared prefix, per-user memory and volatile injections such as time, recall, skills and approved plan in an append-only tail), lineage-scoped cache keys, todo recitation in the tail, and compaction as a bracketed transaction with a visible marker.

items.title: Org and role model entitlements: Control Plane decides, Model Plane enforces at admission
items.summary: Give the refused allowed_models policy field a real owner: a Control Plane entitlement policy (org, role, group, plan) with allow/deny model lists, maximum effort, admin default model/effort per surface, and an explain endpoint for one member's effective access. Model Plane receives the resolved entitlement in the auth context, filters ListModels, and refuses disallowed models at admission with a typed reason, never silently substituting.
items.whyItMatters: Enterprise buyers expect to restrict expensive or non-EU models per role. The code itself flags this hole: the gateway refuses the allowlist by name because no service owns it, so operators currently cannot restrict models at all.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: web-chatgpt (web-chatgpt-web-product-105)
others: claude (152, per-role effort caps, most permissive role wins)
codexagent (045, 043, plan lists and access programs as catalogue data)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 5 of 12 sources; table-stakes (judgement: web-only sources expose little internals)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Admins set starting model, reasoning level and speed separately per surface; new models are off by default for enterprise; roles are additive (union of allows) and the most permissive effort cap wins; a Model Test tool shows a member's effective access. [DOC for ChatGPT, SRC for Claude desktop and Codex]

evidence: apps/Model Plane/rust/services/model-gateway/src/grpc.rs:148-160 (verified: allowed_models is the only policy field with no owner and is refused by name)
verevonToday.gap: No per-org or per-role model allowlist, no role-level effort cap, no admin default per surface, no effective-access explainer. The privacy-tier floor in admission already fails closed but is not an entitlement system.

items.approach: Control Plane: policy schema {subject, allow_models[], deny_models[], max_effort, default_model, default_effort} with resolution (union of role allows, intersect with plan, most permissive effort cap) and an explain API. Model Plane: extend mp-authctx claims to carry the resolved entitlement; inference-core filters ListModels and enforces in admission next to the privacy-tier floor. Frontend Plane: admin page beside the router-policy page (apps/gateway/src/domains/router_policy.rs). The entitlement can only narrow access; it must never widen an owner-plane ACL or a Space's rights.
items.planeOwner: Control Plane (policy) with Model Plane (enforcement) and Frontend Plane (admin UI)
items.risks: Resolution order must be documented and tested; entitlement must not widen Space or owner-plane ACLs; stale cached entitlements could allow a revoked model.

verevon.exactGap: No per-org, per-role or per-plan model allowlist exists: OrgPolicy.allowed_models has no owning service and SetPolicy refuses it by name (grpc.rs:148-160; gateway.proto:1343-1357), the only live allowlist is the deployment-wide ALLOWED_MODELS env var applied in normalize.rs:360-384, and list_models ignores the caller claims (http_routes.rs:7603-7606; inference-core grpc.rs:394-424). There is also no effort cap, admin default per surface or effective-access explainer, and the Convex org settings mirror fields allowedModels and defaultModel are never read for Model Plane admission (convex schema.ts:19-23).
reuse: org-core org_entitlements table, GET /orgs/{id}/entitlements and the session-core aggregation with app.session.entitlements_changed (org-core types.go:266-291, repository.go:663-667, session-core org_client.go:124-148); today it holds only feature flags such as feature.chat and a computed ZDR entitlement
The org_quotas pull pattern: model-gateway org_quota::fetch_org_limits against org-core with a service principal (org_quota.rs:1-24, sse.rs:1154-1155, grpc.rs:2173-2215)
auth-core signed-claim precedent for org posture: retentionPosture claim with a 60 second token TTL cap for staleness (convex-token.service.ts:152-173)
normalize.rs allowlist check as the single admission choke point (normalize.rs:360-384) and list_models, which already receives Claims (http_routes.rs:7603-7606)
Router-policy admin page and gateway proxy (router_policy.rs) as the UI neighbour
verevon.constraints: CLAUDE.md:23 assigns entitlements and quotas to Control Plane, so policy storage, resolution and the explain API belong in org-core (Go) with Model Plane only reading and enforcing; there is no cross-plane DB access, so enforcement needs a service-principal pull (org_quota.rs pattern) or a signed claim. Fail closed: the existing org_quota fetch deliberately fails OPEN on an org-core outage (sse.rs:1154), which is wrong for a deny list, so use last-known-good with a short TTL or refuse. An entitlement may only narrow access and must not widen a Space or owner-plane ACL. The router-policy admin gate is the SPA RequireWorkspaceAdmin plus a forwarded x-user-role header (router_policy.rs:9-10), which is not sufficient authority for an entitlement writer, so the write must be role-checked in org-core. ZDR: an allowlist must not silently remove every ZDR-attested model for a ZDR org, so admission should refuse with a typed reason rather than substitute a model.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Extend org-core (org_entitlements/org_quotas pattern) rather than a new Control schema, and say so. Enforce in model-gateway, which already owns the env allowlist in normalize.rs and receives Claims in list_models; inference-core ListModels takes only modality and provider and has no org input, so it is not the filter point (its chain selection may take the allowlist as defense in depth next to the privacy-tier floor). Deliver by short-TTL service-principal pull for lists (claims would bloat and go stale; the ZDR claim needs a 60 second TTL cap for exactly that reason) or add a compact policy version claim. Roles are not in mp-authctx Claims (claims.rs:10-38), so org-core must resolve role to allowlist before Model Plane sees it.
verevon.effortNote: M for an org-level allow/deny list with default model and ListModels filter using the org_quota pull pattern; role/group/plan resolution, effort cap and the explain endpoint make the full item L.
verevon.verdictReason: The gap is real and unbuilt, so the item stands, but its placement is partly off (inference-core filter) and it omits the existing org-core entitlement and org_quota pull infrastructure that should be reused.

items.title: Computer use inside the agent's own sandbox desktop (consent tiers only if user-desktop control is ever unparked)
items.summary: Add a computer tool whose Model-proposed actions (screenshot plus accessibility tree, click, type, scroll) are executed by a guest agent on a desktop inside the item 3 sandbox VM, with receipts for every action. Adopt the 'typed connectors first, then browser, then screen' hierarchy now as policy; build Claude-style per-app consent tiers and an Endpoint Plane executor only if the owner later allows control of user machines.
items.whyItMatters: 'Controls a computer, acts like a PC' is part of the stated vision, and desktop computer use is a table-stakes feature in 8 of 12 sources. Doing it in the agent's own VM delivers the capability while respecting the owner's decision not to drive users' own desktops and the rule that the Model proposes and the executor acts.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Manus (accessibility-first engine: UI Automation tree with short handles, element-targeted actions, synthesized input only as fallback, strict window-identity ladder) plus Claude (per-app consent tiers, deny list, machine lock, restoration at turn end)
others: Hermes (any-model computer use via a cua-driver MCP with numbered elements)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 8 of 12 sources (table-stakes); consent tiers are a differentiator (2 of 12)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: get_app_state returns {a11y tree with handles, optional screenshot with capture id}; act{handle | coords+capture_id}; targets resolve through a window-identity ladder and ambiguous targets are refused; provider-native computer-use schemas map onto the same engine. Consent: request_access{app} gives a tier from the app category (view-only browsers, click-only terminals, full otherwise), enforced on every action against the frontmost app, with a deny list, a global lock and restoration of windows and clipboard at turn end.

verevonToday.gap: There is no computer-use tool anywhere in Model Plane. OS-level desktop control was parked by the owner (recorded in the chat parity audit). The Endpoint Plane is a native Rust remote-desktop host with screen capture, input injection and a consent prompt, but no agent tool targets it. Verevon's typed-actions-first policy already matches Claude's connectors-then-browser-then-screen hierarchy in spirit, but it is not written as a rule the model sees.

items.approach: Phase 1 (after item 3): an Xfce or Wayland desktop in the VM image; execution-core exposes a computer tool (screenshot, AT-SPI accessibility tree, xdotool or ydotool input); the guest agent executes and returns structured receipts reusing Quarry's receipt and tri-state verification model (step_receipts.rs); every action passes capability policy and the Model never executes. Write the tool-hierarchy rule into the system prompt and capability policy now. Phase 2, only if the owner unparks user-desktop control: the Endpoint Plane agent as executor with per-app consent tiers, deny list and machine lock.
items.planeOwner: Model Plane (execution-core computer tool, guest agent); Endpoint Plane only for phase 2
items.risks: Pixel-agent reliability, prompt injection from on-screen content, vision-token cost, and the owner's parked decision on user-machine control; consent tiers add little value until phase 2.

verevon.exactGap: No computer or desktop tool exists in Model Plane: the Do-mode catalogue offers only browser.observe/browser.act (Quarry browser runs; the act schema refuses coordinates, URLs and raw CDP) and code_interpreter, the execution substrate is a one-shot bubblewrap child (sandbox.rs capability profile: ephemeral, bounded_oneshot, no durable computer), the sandbox-manager image carries no desktop packages and 'desktop' is rejected as a browser-broker grant mode. The Endpoint Plane Verevon Agent is a Windows-only RustDesk-protocol host (cfg(windows) capture and input, native consent dialog) that no Model Plane tool targets, and OS-level desktop control is recorded as parked by the owner. The only shipped analogue is browser-level: Quarry's AgentAction with snapshot-scoped ClickRef/TypeRef refs and generation checks, a CDP accessibility projection, and append-only step receipts.

ChatPanels agent-screen figure and ChatLiveRunPanel frames as the viewer (F-t3-035); the packages/remote-core RustDesk-protocol browser client is a possible desktop viewer only if a Linux host is ever built (INF)
verevon.constraints: Model proposes, executor acts: a desktop executor inside a sandbox VM is not Quarry, so the browser rule does not transfer by itself; keep Model Plane as proposer, run the guest agent under a lease bound to one Space and a Control-signed capability decision, and route every action through capability_policy (trusted_capability_id fails closed for any unmapped tool id, so a new cap id is needed). The browser tool deliberately refuses coordinates; a desktop tool with coords + capture_id reopens the pixel channel that surface closed, so it needs an ADR and per-action risk classes. Web access must stay on Quarry (ingestion executes or rejects, BrowserBroker grants, egress policy); a desktop browser inside the VM must not become a second, ungoverned browser path. ZDR must propagate to screenshots and receipts (Quarry AgentActionRequest already carries ZdrMode), and Space access must never widen an owner-plane ACL. Driving the user's own desktop is parked by the owner, so phase 2 stays parked.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Do not present phase 1 as a standalone execution-core tool: the Xfce VM and guest agent it names are F-t3-009's microVM backend, which does not exist (today's substrate is a bubblewrap one-shot child). Order it as: (1) S, now: write the typed connector > Quarry browser > screen hierarchy into the Do system prompt and capability policy (no such rule text was found in model-gateway or execution-core prompts); (2) after F-t3-009 and F-t3-035: extend that item's typed executor protocol with a desktop surface (accessibility snapshot with short handles and generation counters modelled on Quarry ClickRef, receipts reusing the step-receipt shape) instead of inventing a parallel protocol; (3) keep the coordinate fallback off until an ADR. The existing Endpoint Plane agent cannot be reused inside a Linux VM (Windows-only), and Linux AT-SPI coverage of real GUI apps is unverified.

verevon.verdictReason: The absent claim is correct, but the item reads as a standalone first-rank build when it is the capstone of F-t3-009 and F-t3-035 plus an ADR. Browser-level computer use (a11y refs, receipts, approvals) already ships in Quarry and should be the model, and the pixel-coordinate fallback conflicts with a deliberate current policy. Split out the S hierarchy rule.

items.title: Open the typed action registry to the agent: classify every action, admit reads first, mint per-run scoped tokens
items.summary: Verevon's single typed action registry shared by the UI and agents is the reference design, but only 8 actions are model-executable. Classify every action by model access (none, read, write-with-approval, write) and risk, admit read actions per owning plane through the capability gate, then writes under item 01's exact-effect approval, and mint per-run delegated tokens scoped to the thread and capability set.
items.whyItMatters: This is the core of the AI-first thesis: the user can say 'move this to my Space and notify the team' and the agent performs it with the same actions and guards as the UI. 4 of 12 sources expose their own product to the agent; Claude desktop and T3 Code show the pattern.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Claude desktop (built-in MCP servers for sessions, sidebar, settings and host actions; each Preferences key declares whether the model may read or change it; SRC) plus T3 Code (per-session scoped bearer credential stored only as a hash; SRC)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 4 of 12 sources; common
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: A typed action registry shared by UI and agent; each action declares model access (none | read | write-with-approval | write) and risk; admitted actions become tools with honest annotations (readOnly, destructive, idempotent); a per-session scoped token limited to the thread and capability set is issued and stored only as a hash.

verevonToday.gap: The registry has 168 typed actions (chat/agents baseline v-chat-agents-ui-088; not recounted here), but the model-eligibility allowlist admits only 8: tickets.create, inbox.follow_conversation, inbox.set_csat_preference, inbox.review_ai_action, chat.save_thread_snapshot, chat.submit_feedback, org.mark_exported and org.acknowledge_deletion (SRC). There are no per-setting model-access classes and no session-scoped tool credentials recorded. Each admission needs owner-plane proof (contract, attestation, forged-call denial test), which is why the list is deliberately short.

items.approach: Frontend Plane action registry plus Model Plane capability gate. Add model-access and risk metadata to ActionDescriptor and a CI ratchet that follows the AI-first plan (M2: at least 10 eligible low-risk actions; M3: all eligible actions with explicit exemptions). Treat each admission as per-owner design work (owner contract, capability binding, health attestation, forged-call denial test). Keep security, billing and identity settings non-model-accessible. Writes use item 01's policy and exact-effect approval; the BFF gateway mints a per-run scoped delegated token bound to the thread and capability set.
items.planeOwner: Frontend Plane (registry, token minting at the BFF gateway) with the Model Plane capability gate and each owning plane
items.risks: Agents acting on account settings (keep security and identity settings out); admitting an action without owner proof ships a dead or unsafe tool (the repo has hit this before); delegated authority needs a Control decision.

alreadyPlanned.where: Verevon-ai-first-plan.md milestones M2 and M3 (lines 42-43, 92-102): at least 10 eligible actions by M2, all eligible actions by M3 with CI enforcement.

verevon.exactGap: ActionDescriptor already carries risk, requiresApproval and reversible, and a versioned, hashed catalog manifest with allowedActorTypes and an executionContract exists (types.ts:15-24, catalog-manifest.ts:32-70), but there is no read versus write model-access class, no human-only exempt marker and no CI ratchet; isModelExecutableAction admits 8 of 168 actions (model-eligibility.ts:126-140). A per-run, per-action signed authority already exists in Control (run-action-v1 and model-action-view-v1, bound to run id, thread id, subject, schema hash, payload digest and idempotency key), but runActionTarget accepts only tickets.create (run_action_decision.go:340-347) and the model-action view is a pinned single action, with a bespoke Model Plane adapter (ticket_tools.rs). The BFF mints per-audience per-user bearers (chat/shared.rs:187-260), not per-run tokens.
reuse: ActionDescriptor fields risk, requiresApproval and reversible, and buildActionCatalogManifest (deterministic hash, allowedActorTypes)
catalog-manifest.test.ts allowlist assertion as the seed of the CI ratchet
Control user-core RunActionDecision and ModelActionView signing, plus capability-core ControlModelActionViewVerifier
execution-core ticket_tools.rs as the pattern for an owner-action adapter (Control decision, then owner receipt)
Verevon-ai-first-plan.md three-tier model (model-eligible, approval-gated, human-only exempt) and scoreboard idea
verevon.constraints: Control resolves actor, org, Space, audience and privacy itself; the caller supplies only identifiers and commitments (model_action_decision.go:13-24), so scoped authority must be minted by Control user-core, not by the BFF gateway. The current decision requires Space evidence and a non-ZDR run (ZeroDataRetention must be false), so ZDR turns and non-Space contexts cannot use owner actions. Each admission needs owner contract, capability-core binding and health attestation, and a forged-call denial test (model-eligibility.ts header); the decision carries no target-resource grant and the owner re-authorizes the target. No cross-plane DB access. Writes need exact-effect approval.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Replace "the BFF gateway mints a per-run scoped delegated token" with generalising Control run-action-v1 and model-action-view-v1 from the single tickets.create case into a per-action table keyed by the catalog schema hash; the BFF keeps minting only per-audience user bearers. Add a model-access class (none, read, write-with-approval) and an exempt reason to ActionDescriptor (risk already exists) and turn the catalog-manifest allowlist test into the CI ratchet. The item restates plan milestones M2 and M3, so reference the plan rather than redefine them.
verevon.effortNote: M holds for the framework tranche (classification fields, CI ratchet, generalising the Control decision table, first read actions). Each further admission is its own M of owner-plane work.
verevon.verdictReason: Risk metadata and per-run scoped authority already exist in part, and the token should be minted by Control rather than the BFF; reword to generalising the existing Control decision, adding model-access classes and the CI ratchet.

items.title: Human takeover and hand-back from live views: agent-requested takeover for logins, 2FA and CAPTCHAs, then point-and-comment steering
items.summary: Add a request_human_takeover action that pauses the browser run, switches the hosted browser to human control with a takeover card in chat, and resumes on hand-back with the user's note and a fresh snapshot; human-typed input never flows to the model or into replays. Second track: point-and-comment on live previews and artifacts so the user can steer by clicking an element or drawing a region.
items.whyItMatters: Logins, 2FA and CAPTCHAs end most real browser tasks; five of twelve references hand control to the human and back (Manus, T3 Code input arbitration). Manual takeover already exists in the hosted browser, so the missing piece is the Model Plane pause and the chat surface.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Manus (agent-suggested takeover cards, hand-back message) plus T3 Code (real human-vs-agent input arbitration by recording expected synthetic input and treating anything else as human) ; Manus (DOC strings: choose a computer, view, take over, pause, exit takeover; a login done during takeover can carry over to similar tasks) for takeover, and Cursor (SRC: design mode in the in-app browser to click elements or draw a region and comment; pausable VNC view; steer from phone) for point-and-comment
others: Manus web (select region plus instruction across builder, slides and design)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: R-t3-06-02: 5 of 12 sources (common) | R-t3-12-11: 2 of 12 sources for each track (differentiators).
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: The agent emits suggest_takeover{surface, reason}; Live view stream (VNC or CDP screencast) in a pane with a takeover state machine {agent_driving, user_driving, paused};

verevonToday.gap: R-t3-06-02: Manual takeover works in the hosted browser: controlMode human_takeover blocks model actions in the BFF. | R-t3-12-11: The Work panel shows a live agent screen, but chat turns cannot yet drive a browser, agent browser runs fail closed without a broker grant (DOC), and live view plus takeover is planned as E10 (L to XL) with E9 (Open in browser from a message) as its predecessor;

items.approach: Plan E9/E10 plus the durable pause of F-t3-002; T3-style arbitration (record expected synthetic input, treat anything else as human). Point-and-comment reuses the typed annotation part of F-t3-031.
items.planeOwner: Model Plane (pause and resume) with Ingestion Plane (Quarry control mode) and Frontend Plane (takeover card, live view)
items.risks: Credentials typed by the human must never reach the model or recordings; a scoped carry-over grant for repeated logins needs an expiry.

Human-typed input must stay out of model-visible observations, replay events and receipts, and ZDR runs keep no replay. A human wait is unbounded, so the pause cannot rest only on the in-memory execution-core StateStore (lost on restart, single process); use the durable approval primitive in session-core. Credentials typed by the human never reach the model; any carry-over grant needs an expiry. Space and browser-grant authority are unchanged.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Re-slice: (1) wire takeover and hand-back into ChatLiveRunPanel (pass onBrowserControlMode, show takeover state), which is mostly frontend and closes the plan's E10; (2) agent-requested takeover as a new 'human_assist' kind on the existing approval gate, triggered by Quarry ChallengeSignal (captcha or login) and by a planner action, resuming with the user's note appended to planner context and a fresh observation (the gate's ApprovalOutcome has a bounded wait with a TimedOut result, browser_risk.rs:95-110, so a human-assist kind needs its own longer budget); (3) point-and-comment as a separate later item on top of the F-t3-031 annotation part. Drop the T3-style synthetic-input arbitration: the BFF already separates Agent and Human actors and Quarry holds the single control-mode state, so arbitration reduces to that state.
verevon.effortNote: L to M for the takeover track because live frames, pause/resume, control mode, BFF enforcement and the durable approval gate already exist; point-and-comment stays a separate M item. Plan E10 is listed as planned (2026-10-01) but the chat live panel is already in code.
verevon.verdictReason: The need holds, but the chat surface is further along than stated (live panel, pause/resume built; takeover merely not wired) and the missing core is an agent-requested, durable human-assist pause on top of the existing approval gate; effort and slicing change.

items.title: Deep research v2: clarifying questions and an editable plan, mid-run steering, a gap-driven second pass with a claim ledger, and knowledge plus connector sources in one cited report
items.summary: Split run_deep_research into a plan phase (sub-queries, optional domain scope, one to three clarifying questions, approve or auto-start) and a run phase that streams interim findings and accepts refocus. Then add a second pass: extract a claim-to-source ledger from pages actually read, issue targeted follow-up queries for gaps and conflicts, stop when new sources add little, and include Data Plane v2 and connector sources so one report cites web, knowledge and apps.
items.whyItMatters: Verevon already ships honest one-pass research (mandatory 'could not verify' section, cited artifact). Plan transparency (ChatGPT) and gap-driven passes (Codex method, Perplexity scale) are what make research reports trustworthy at depth. Reference evidence here is documentation-only.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: ChatGPT deep research (web-chatgpt, DOC) ; Codex deep-research skill (codexagent-plugins-and-extensibility-097, DOC) for method; Perplexity (web-perplexity-web-product-034, DOC) for scale
others: Perplexity advanced research (web-perplexity, DOC): interim key findings and a streamed editable report
Claude research (claude-product-ux-075, SRC): explicit 'research plan created' state
Manus start card (SRC): an 'Always auto-start' opt-out, a pattern to reuse for plan approval
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: R-t3-03-01: 3 of 11 sources; differentiator | R-t3-03-02: 5 of 11 sources; common (reference evidence is DOC-only)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Run state machine: clarify (optional, only when the query is broad) -> plan_proposed (structured sub-questions plus allowed or prioritised domains) -> user edits or accepts -> running, emitting source-reading and finding events -> a follow-up or changed site list injected mid-run re-plans the remaining steps -> report streamed incrementally. Loop: plan sub-questions -> pass 1 broad search and read -> extract claims into a claim-to-source ledger -> identify gaps and conflicts -> pass 2 targeted queries -> stop when new sources add little (diminishing-returns test) or the budget is hit -> synthesise from the ledger only, labelling inference -> render and check the artifact.

verevonToday.gap: R-t3-03-01: SRC: the plan is shown as one checklist row per sub-query and the Kilder tab fills before synthesis, but the run starts immediately. | R-t3-03-02: SRC: one pass (plan up to 9 sub-queries, concurrent search, read of 16 pages, one synthesis with [n] citations, mandatory 'Kunne ikke verifiseres' section, document artifact, wall clock bound).

items.approach: Refactor deep_research.rs into plan/run first, reuse plan_proposed and queued_input semantics; then the ledger and pass 2 with per-pass caps; longer evidence windows via the chunked reader of F-t3-054.
items.planeOwner: Model Plane
items.risks: Cost of extra passes (synthesis input dominates); client-edited plans are untrusted and must be re-clamped; ZDR blocks persisting the ledger; deep research is rejected on the subscription route.

verevon.exactGap: run_deep_research (deep_research.rs:2413) is one in-stream, web-only pass: plan up to 9 sub-queries (already shown as a per-sub-query checklist before any search), concurrent search, read about 16 pages, citations emitted before synthesis so the Kilder tab fills early, one synthesis with a mandatory could-not-verify section; user-pasted URLs also seed the source list. There is no clarification step, no plan approve or edit (plan_proposed and queued_input serve only the agentic tool loop), no claim ledger or second pass, and no knowledge or connector source: the file has no knowledge or connector code and sse.rs:953 rejects knowledge_only scope together with deep research. Deep research is also refused under ZDR.
reuse: deep_research.rs coverage, read_order, number_and_bound and coverage_statement honesty machinery (keep the mandatory unverified section)
ResearchEvents::Live sink and the existing per-sub-query step rows for plan transparency
plan-approval node and PlanApprovalControl editable step list as UI only
knowledge_search, knowledge_graph_search and knowledge_wiki_search tool definitions in tool_loop.rs (viewer-scoped Data Plane v2 retrieval) for knowledge sources
queued_input registry shape (per request id, tenant and user bound) if steering is kept
linked_source_urls user-seeded sources as the first form of domain scoping
verevon.constraints: The pipeline runs in-process inside one SSE connection with a wall clock and dies with the stream (deep_research.rs header: deliberately not Temporal; queued_input is in-memory single-replica), so an approve-before-run gate cannot wait inside the stream. A research plan approval is not an authority grant: do not reuse PlanProposed rung-grant semantics, only the editable-list UI. Knowledge and connector sources must go through the existing viewer-ACL retrieval path and respect retrieval_scope (auto, knowledge_only, web_only) and Space authority. ZDR and waived-route turns refuse deep research, so the ledger and any plan record are never persisted for them.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Do not refactor one plan/run state machine inside the stream. Ship three independent slices: (1) a plan turn that returns the sub-query list (and at most one clarifying question) as an editable node, then a run turn that carries the edited list and is re-clamped server-side to the 9/10 ceilings; (2) an in-process second pass driven by coverage_of (unread and shortfall are already computed) with one extra search round inside the existing wall clock and page caps, adding a claim ledger only if the synthesis prompt is changed to extract claims (extra inference cost); (3) knowledge and connector sources by calling existing retrieval inside the pipeline under scope rules. Demote mid-run steering: queued_input is delivered only at tool-round boundaries (tool_loop.rs) and deep research is not a tool loop.
verevon.effortNote: Raised from L: the bundle is three separate M to L slices (plan turn, second pass with ledger, knowledge sources) plus steering; as independent items each is M or L.
verevon.verdictReason: The baseline is partly richer than described (plan checklist, early Kilder, user-linked URLs) and the proposed state machine does not fit an in-stream, single-replica pipeline; the item should be split and steering demoted.

items.title: Live run-cost meter with pre-run estimate, cost by token category, quota display and allowance warnings
items.summary: Emit cumulative usage_progress events after every provider call and metered tool charge, show a live meter in the Work panel and Run Console, warn at 80 percent of the run or org ceiling, and show a labelled estimate on the plan-approval card. Extend the usage record with disjoint uncached input, cache read, cache write, output and reasoning tokens with role, tool and subagent attribution, aggregate per turn and thread, and show per-user allowance and quota resets.
items.whyItMatters: Agent runs spend real money; Manus and Perplexity show live cost and estimates, and an allowance page is table-stakes (7 of 12). Verevon's honesty contract (cost null when unknown, cost basis distinguishes subscription usage) is a strength to extend, not replace.

verevon.approachAdjustment: Start from plan I16 (progress frames plus warning) and add the cache read/write fields to the existing Usage frame, since the data already flows from inference-core to the ledger. Surface the silent 80 percent tier downgrade to the user as part of the warning instead of building a second threshold. Drop "extend the usage record with reasoning tokens" (providers report reasoning as a subset of output, not a disjoint count) and treat role, tool and subagent attribution, thread aggregation and the plan-card estimate as separate later work. Per-user allowance needs Control Plane billing support because only org-level allowances exist today.
verevon.effortNote: Unchanged as a whole; the core (progress frames, live meter, 80 percent warning, cache fields) is M per plan I16, while pre-run estimate, attribution and per-user allowance are the L remainder.
verevon.verdictReason: Much of the supporting data and surfaces already exist (cost basis, ledger cache tokens, org allowances, quotas with reset, subscription windows) and the live meter is already planned as I16; reword to the genuinely missing parts and split the core from the estimate and attribution work.

items.title: Canonical reasoning-effort ladder mapped per model to each provider wire format
items.summary: Define one canonical effort scale (none, minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh) and a single resolve_effort() in inference-core that every provider adapter calls: clamp the request to the nearest weaker level the model supports, then map it to the provider vocabulary (OpenAI/Azure reasoning effort, Anthropic thinking budget, Codex reasoning_effort, later Gemini thinking level). Start with a static per-model table and move it into the model record (R-t3-09-05) later; keep the composer's Auto / Raskt svar / Dyp research dial as presets over the canonical scale.
items.whyItMatters: Budget/Balance/Genius defaults are mostly OpenAI-family models, and that route currently sends no reasoning effort at all, so the user's depth choice is ignored on the most-used path. This is a code-verified gap with a small, well-understood fix that six of twelve references implement.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: hermes (hermes-architecture-and-surfaces-096)
others: codexagent (032, best declared per-model ladder with descriptions)
deepseek (092, refuses unsupported values before dispatch)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 6 of 12 sources; table-stakes
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: An EFFORT_LADDER plus named per-generation wire vocabularies and clamp_effort() that picks the nearest weaker supported level instead of sending a value that returns 400; capability probes are cached per (model, base_url). The composer renders only the levels the selected model declares. [SRC for Hermes/Codex/DeepSeek]

evidence: grep of inference-core/src/provider/openai.rs finds no reasoning_effort (verified read-only); only codex_subscription.rs sets it
verevonToday.gap: Quick/Standard/Deep profiles produce an Anthropic thinking budget and a Codex low/high effort only. The OpenAI and Azure chat path sends no effort, there is no per-model declared ladder, no clamp-to-nearest rule, and no per-role or per-surface cap.

items.approach: Model Plane: add an Effort enum and resolve_effort(model, requested, role_cap) in inference-core/src/provider (shared by openai.rs, anthropic.rs, codex_subscription.rs); wire OpenAI/Azure reasoning models first and declare 'none' for non-reasoning ids such as gpt-4o-mini; keep model-gateway/src/thinking.rs profiles as the preset layer that picks a canonical level instead of a raw budget. Log the clamp on the run and show the cost multiplier for high levels. Composer reads supported levels from the model record once R-t3-09-05 exists.
items.planeOwner: Model Plane
items.risks: Higher effort raises cost and latency; tie default levels to budget posture and show the multiplier. Do not send effort to models that reject the parameter.

verevon.exactGap: Effort is a three-value profile (quick, standard, deep mapped to thinking.rs budgets of 1,024, 0 and 4,096 tokens) that becomes an Anthropic thinking budget and a Codex low or high reasoning_effort only. The OpenAI and Azure builder (openai.rs:430-455) sends no reasoning effort even for gpt-5 and o-series ids (is_reasoning_model only switches to max_completion_tokens), the governed agent loop hard-sets thinking_budget_tokens to 0 (agent.rs:1334-1340), and capability records carry only a boolean supports_thinking per provider. There is no canonical ladder, no per-model declared levels and no clamp-to-nearest rule; the composer and wire expose only quick, standard and deep.
reuse: thinking.rs budget_tokens as the preset layer that picks a level
codex_reasoning_effort (budget to low/high) as the mapping precedent for OpenAI/Azure
anthropic.rs exclusion list and floor check as the model-capability precedent
ProviderCapabilities and the fallback chain for clamping and per-provider support
InferRequest.thinking_budget_tokens (proto field 13) as the existing carrier
verevon.constraints: Plane is Model Plane (inference-core and model-gateway). Effort changes cost, so default levels must tie to the budget posture in intent.rs and cost-core, and a per-role or per-org cap is a Control-owned entitlement, not a Model Plane constant. The agent loop deliberately disables thinking (agent.rs:1336-1339: effort is a chat-surface control), so extending it to Do runs is a product decision. On the Codex subscription route cost is not metered (CostBasis::Subscription), so a USD multiplier display does not apply there. Reasoning deltas follow the usual ZDR persistence rules.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Start with the smallest correct slice: derive OpenAI and Azure reasoning_effort from the existing thinking_budget_tokens the way codex_reasoning_effort does (quick low, deep high, standard omitted) for gpt-5 and o-series ids only. A real six-level canonical ladder needs an additive InferRequest field (next free number in inference.proto) and a refreshed buf baseline, so it is a second step. Keep the static per-model table inside inference-core; moving it into capability-core is later because the picker catalogue is built from inference-core, not that table. Note effort is applied only to the final answer inference (sse.rs:2670), not to tool-loop rounds.
verevon.effortNote: S holds only for the OpenAI/Azure slice; the full ladder needs an additive proto field, gateway plumbing, three adapters, tests and composer levels.
verevon.verdictReason: Confirmed code gap: the OpenAI-family path (including the gpt-5-nano and gpt-5-mini defaults for Budget and simple Balance in intent.rs) ignores the user effort choice; the fix is small and well understood.

items.title: Workspace file tools for Do mode: versioned read, grep, glob and list, plus governed edit and write on one small Rust edit engine
items.summary: Add bounded read tools over the hydrated Space workspace (ranged read with line numbers and a content hash, ripgrep-shaped grep, glob/list) and governed fs.edit and fs.write tools built on one Rust edit engine (unique-match replace with whitespace/CRLF tolerant fallback, did-you-mean errors, per-path lock, stale-read guard from the read hash), returning before/after hunks.
items.whyItMatters: Every agent harness in the reference set edits files with a dedicated tool; Verevon agents can only change workspace files by writing a whole program through code_interpreter, which is slow, error-prone and hard to review. Verevon is not an IDE, but agents still produce and revise documents, data and code in workspaces.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Cursor (StrReplace matching ladder, structured result, shared per-file lock) ; Cursor (ripgrep-shaped grep with broad-glob guard, versioned read schema with negative offsets and line numbers)
others: DeepSeek harness (stale-read version guard with a remedy message)
Antigravity (lazy-edit detection, fuzzy-distance cap, partial success)
Codex (apply_patch variant of the same capability)
Claude Code and Manus (str_replace style editors)
T3 Code (strict index budgets: 25k entries, 15 s scan, idle eviction)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: R-t3-07-01: 3 of 9 sources have detailed records (Cursor, DeepSeek, Antigravity); every coding-capable reference ships an edit tool in some form; table-stakes for agent harnesses | R-t3-07-02: 3 of 9 sources; common
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Schema {file_path first, old_string, new_string, replace_all?}; grep maps onto a bundled ripgrep with workdir-relative paths, output_mode, -A/-B/-C, multiline, head_limit and a truncated flag, and refuses an unbounded broad glob.

verevonToday.gap: R-t3-07-01: Workspace half: space workspace files can only be changed by writing a whole python or sh program through code_interpreter, and there is no file read, edit or write tool in the Do-mode catalogue (process_tool_defs and code_interpreter are the file-adjacent tools). | R-t3-07-02: There are no grep, glob or read tools over a Space workspace.

items.approach: Read tools first (S, low risk), then edit/write under the local_mutation class of F-t3-003; capability-core migration for the new ids; works over the existing Space CAS workspace and later the thread workspace of F-t3-009.
dependencies: Do mode on the product route (OD2)
items.planeOwner: Model Plane (execution-core tools, capability-core ids)
items.risks: Edits outside workspace roots (use the safe-path hardening of F-t3-009); concurrent agent and human edits need the version guard.

verevon.exactGap: No read, grep, glob, list, edit or write tool for workspace files exists in either tool catalogue: Do mode offers code_interpreter and the process_* family (agent.rs), chat mode offers only artifact tools (create/read/update_artifact, whole-content replace) and the only file-named tools are MCP allowlist fixtures. Agents change hydrated Space workspace files only by running a python or sh program through code_interpreter, whose changes are diffed against a CAS hash baseline by workspace_hydrate::diff_and_upload and merged by sandbox-manager Promote with a per-path base_hash compare-and-swap. A stale-read guard therefore already exists at promote time (run overlay versus Space), but not per edit.
evidence: apps/Model Plane/rust/services/execution-core/src/runtime_loop/agent.rs:4090,4190-4222 (process_start, browser and code_interpreter definitions; no file tools)
apps/Model Plane/rust/services/model-gateway/src/tool_loop.rs:4324-4365 (create/read/update_artifact; update replaces the complete content)
apps/Model Plane/rust/services/execution-core/src/code_interpreter.rs:1-34,462-540,575-600 (persistent hydrated root reused across calls; output is stdout, stderr, exit_code, files)
apps/Model Plane/rust/services/execution-core/src/workspace_hydrate.rs:1-130 (safe_relative_path, hydrate baseline, diff_and_upload with redaction)
apps/Model Plane/rust/services/execution-core/src/permission/mod.rs:229-275 (is_risky_tool is a substring match; no 'edit' keyword)
apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/shared/chat-nodes/diff.ts:1-40 (diff producer; its header states no file-editing tool exists)
reuse: sandbox_lease::ensure_hydrated_workspace (the hydrated per-run Space workspace directory the tools would operate on)
workspace_hydrate::safe_relative_path, hash baseline and diff_and_upload for path safety and change detection
sandbox-manager UpsertOverlay and Promote (base_hash compare-and-swap) as the durable merge path
capability_policy::trusted_capability_id and permission::is_risky_tool for governance of the new ids
process_tools authorize_in_space pattern for Space checks
frontend diff.ts and the tool-presentation diff card for before/after hunks
verevon.constraints: Only Space-scoped runs with a Control-signed sandbox decision hydrate a persistent workspace; non-Space calls get an ephemeral per-call directory, so durable file tools have nothing to edit in personal threads until F-t3-009's thread workspace exists. Path safety must reuse safe_relative_path (rejects absolute and .. components; symlinks are skipped). diff_and_upload hashes and uploads REDACTED bytes (secret patterns scrubbed), so a written file with secret-shaped strings is altered on upload and the read hash must be in the same hash domain as the CAS baseline or the guard will false-conflict. permission::is_risky_tool matches substrings such as write, update, patch, create; an id like fs.edit matches none, so new ids need explicit entries plus capability ids in trusted_capability_id. Durable mutation under ZDR is refused (workspace_promote), so ZDR runs must keep writing nothing durable. Chat-mode artifact patching was already adjudicated no-go (patch-revision critic verdict); this item is Do-mode workspace files only.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Implement reads first as stated, but inside execution-core over the hydrated workspace root (no new sandbox-manager RPC) rather than as MCP tools. Keep the existing release path (diff_and_upload, SnapshotSandbox, Promote CAS) as the only durable path and derive the per-file stale-read token from the CAS baseline hash so the tool-level and promote-level guards agree. Add edit and the read names deliberately to the risk classifier and capability mapping instead of relying on substring matches, and fix the redaction hash-domain issue before exposing content hashes to the model.
verevon.effortNote: Unchanged: read, grep, glob are S; the edit engine with guards is M. Grows if personal-thread workspaces are put in scope, which depends on F-t3-009.
verevon.verdictReason: Confirmed absent in code, and the persistent hydrated Space workspace plus CAS merge it relies on are real, so it is buildable now for Space-scoped Do runs. Only the constraints need adjusting (redacted hash domain, risky-tool name matching, Space-only durability).

items.title: Artifact canvas: server-side versions with restore, user editing, selection comments and selection-scoped AI edits, annotation, then collaborative documents
items.summary: Give Model Plane a session-scoped artifact store with revision ids and editor attribution (agent, owner), add an editor to the Output panel (Markdown and code first) that saves with an expected revision and locks while a run targets the same artifact, and let users restore versions. Add selection comments and 'rewrite this selection' bound to artifact version, a translate action, an annotation overlay for previews, and later collaborative documents on Application Plane realtime projections.
items.whyItMatters: Canvas-style editing is how claude.ai, ChatGPT and Manus let users finish work with the agent; Verevon renders artifacts with a version stepper but versions are client-side and users cannot edit, restore or point at a part. 'Save to knowledge' must promote into Data Plane documents rather than duplicate storage.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Manus (SRC) for versions, restore and editor attribution; claude.ai (DOC) for typed artifacts ; T3 Code (serialised <review_comment> block with path, range, text, diff excerpt and fence language that round-trips into a comment card; one annotation component for diffs, files and PRs) ; Claude (SRC: Rust-to-WASM yrs and pulldown-cmark engine) and claude.ai Docs (DOC: @AI in comments); T3 Code (SRC) for the annotation payload
others: Cursor (Cmd+K StreamCmdK selection rewrite with a streamed inline diff and a terminal variant)
claude desktop (SRC, annotation with element context)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: R-t3-01-04: 4 of 12 sources; common | R-t3-07-05: 2 of 9 sources for comments (differentiator); selection rewrite is unique to Cursor in this category's records | R-t3-02-07: Collaborative documents: 2 of 11 (one vendor), differentiator. Annotation: 2 of 11 (claude, t3code), differentiator. Translate action: 1 of 11, unique
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: A server-side file/artifact store keeps a version list with restore and editor attribution (AI, owner, collaborator). An annotatable wrapper over the diff, code or document renderer turns a selection into a draft annotation (Cmd/Ctrl+Enter submits, Esc cancels) and then a composer chip kept in the draft store. Markdown document model in a yrs CRDT shared by server (Rust) and browser (WASM);

verevonToday.gap: R-t3-01-04: The Output panel (document, code, sandboxed HTML, image, PDF, files) with a version stepper and diff ships, but users cannot edit, restore a version or edit a selection, version history is held client-side, and there is no editor attribution or conflict guard. | R-t3-07-05: A grep of features/chat for getSelection, selectionchange and annotation finds nothing: there is no comment-on-selection or select-and-rewrite in the artifact panel or in DiffView. | R-t3-02-07: No editor, no selection-scoped edit and no restore in the artifact panel (artifacts change only through model revisions);

items.approach: Phase 1 (plan I17): server versions, editor, restore, selection edit. Phase 2: annotation overlay with a typed annotation part. Phase 3: yrs-based collaborative documents owned by Application Plane with Data Plane storage.
items.planeOwner: Model Plane (version store) with Frontend Plane (editor), Application Plane (realtime) and Data Plane v2 (promotion)
items.risks: Concurrency with running agents; ZDR forbids durable versions; whose token runs AI edits in collaborative documents; Markdown/CRDT round-trip fidelity.

alreadyPlanned.where: R-t3-01-04: Partly: plan I17 canvas phase 1 (highlight-to-edit, restore this version) (apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/apps/verevon-web/plans/system-audits/CHAT_GAP_CLOSURE_PLAN_2026-10-01.md:253); the server-side version store itself is not named in the plan | R-t3-02-07: Partly. Plan I17 (canvas phase 1: highlight-to-edit, shortcut presets, restore this version, about a week) is in apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/apps/verevon-web/plans/system-audits/CHAT_GAP_CLOSURE_PLAN_2026-10-01.md:253, with the selection-edit scope ruling in OD19 at :507. Annotation, translate action and collaborative documents are not in the plan (INF, not found there).

verevon.exactGap: The gateway already owns the artifact version counter and current text (artifacts.rs ArtifactVersionStore, process-local and rehydrated from each assistant turn's metadata.artifacts by sse.rs rehydrate_persisted_artifacts) and serialises run-versus-run commits with lock_commit and unchanged_from, but there is no artifact store with its own revision ids, no HTTP route to read, write or restore an artifact, no editor attribution, and ZDR turns are not persisted at all. The panel (ChatArtifactPanel.tsx) has a read-only version stepper built from client-merged history (chat-artifacts.ts mergeArtifactVersion), a diff, copy and browser-side export, but no edit, restore or selection capability (no getSelection or selectionchange anywhere in verevonv3/src). Annotation overlay and collaborative documents are absent: Application Plane has only plannerDocuments metadata and presence, and no yrs or yjs dependency was found in any Cargo.toml, package.json or go.mod.
reuse: ArtifactVersionStore (counter, content, kind, title index) and its per-thread commit lock plus base-comparison guard (lock_commit, unchanged_from) as the concurrency model for a user save
sse.rs rehydrate_persisted_artifacts and metadata.artifacts as the existing durable representation of versions
revision_preservation.rs section parser (byte-for-byte preservation of untouched Markdown sections) for selection or section scoped rewrites
update_artifact and read_artifact tools for the model-side revision path
ChatArtifactPanel version stepper and diffText, chat-artifacts.ts mergeArtifactVersion
POST /v1/chat/documents (create_document) as the existing path to promote text into Data Plane for save to knowledge
plan I17 and the artifact_revision_binding receipt already asserted in e2e tests
verevon.constraints: Under effective ZDR the gateway neither seeds nor persists artifacts (sse.rs:4047-4057), so a durable version store, restore or collaboration cannot exist for ZDR threads and editing there must stay client-session-only. Artifact content lives in session-core thread metadata (Model Plane owns it); save to knowledge must go through Data Plane document creation with the user's delegated token so owner=user, not a second copy of storage. Application Plane realtime projections must not become the source of truth for owner-plane content, and an AI edit inside a shared document needs an explicit whose-authority decision. OD19 ruled that selection edits stay at phase 1 and I18 (a server range patch) is cut, so Phase 1 must not introduce a server range-patch API.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Rewrite Phase 1 as plan I17: client-side highlight-to-edit through the normal model revision path and restore this version by re-emitting an old revision as a new version. Drop the 'expected revision plus lock while a run targets the same artifact' server design from Phase 1; the gateway already has a per-thread commit lock and base comparison for run races, so a later user-save RPC should go through the same lock_commit/unchanged_from path and append a new version with an editor attribute. Treat Phase 2 (annotation) and Phase 3 (yrs collaborative documents) as separate, later bets: Phase 3 duplicates ground Data Plane and Application Plane would own.
verevon.effortNote: XL stands only for all three phases together. Phase 1 alone is M (plan I17, about a week); Phase 2 annotation M; Phase 3 collaborative documents XL.
verevon.verdictReason: Phase 1 is already planned (I17, Wave 5) and the item mis-states the baseline (the gateway already owns counter, content and a run concurrency guard; only the history assembly is client-side); Phases 2 and 3 are genuinely absent and should be separated.

items.title: Org agent policy registry: named agent modes, setting locks, a lockdown profile, extension allow-lists, frozen tool snapshots, durable hooks and one Customize hub
items.summary: Add a typed AgentMode (ask every time, allow reads, workspace write, full access) that resolves to the existing posture and autonomy rung, persisted per thread or Space and clamped to min(org cap, user choice). Back it with a schema-as-source org policy registry in Control Plane with locks and tighten-only remote config, a lockdown (anti-exfiltration) profile, org allow-lists for MCP servers and tools with frozen tool snapshots after approval, durable hooks stored in capability-core and passed to Do runs (plan B4), and one Customize hub for skills, connectors, hooks and modes.
items.whyItMatters: Named modes are common (8 of 12) and admin policy registries with locks are common (7 of 12). Verevon has the enforcement core (signed gate, hook engine, rollout and scopes) but the hook rules are in memory and only reach browser runs, and admins have no product surface. Codex, Claude and ChatGPT show the shape.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Codex (typed mode vocabulary with a granular per-effect approval config, full-access confirmation listing risks) for modes and friction; Claude (schema-as-source registry with a fail-closed value per key, tighten-only remote config) for the registry; ChatGPT for Lockdown mode and Requirements-versus-Defaults admin framing ; Claude desktop (33 hook events with command, HTTP, prompt and agent handlers; per-surface plugin-only lock; per-feature egress list; SRC) plus ChatGPT web (a custom app's tool list is frozen after admin approval; DOC) and Codex (hook runs and MCP calls as typed thread items with resource-activity chips; SRC)
others: antigravity (presets map to settings bundles, Strict mode)
deepseek (policy meaning injected into the prompt)
Hermes (observers, transforms, vetoes and middleware with schema-versioned payloads)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: R-t3-11-08: named modes 8 of 12 and admin registry 7 of 12 (table-stakes); elevated-risk labels 6 of 12 (common); lockdown 3 of 12 (differentiator) | R-t3-05-09: Admin governance 4 of 12, common; hooks 4 of 12, common; unified hub 5 of 12, common; extension observability 2 of 12, differentiator
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Enum of modes, each resolving to {sandbox, approval policy per effect class, reviewer}; Org policy document {allowedMcpServers (URL patterns), allowedTools, pluginOnly surfaces, allowed catalogues, network mode};

verevonToday.gap: R-t3-11-08: Posture is server-resolved per profile (chat=auto with read-only tools, Do and deployed_agent=ask) and the user can only tighten it; | R-t3-05-09: The Pre/PostToolUse hook engine is real (allow, deny, ask with glob matching) and sits inside the capability pipeline, but rules live in an in-memory HookRegistry fed by gRPC RegisterHook and are passed only to browser runs;

items.approach: Control Plane owns the registry and signs policy bundles; capability-core enforces at the gate; model-gateway clamps the mode. Hooks get a durable store and are passed to execute_step in Do runs.
items.planeOwner: Control Plane (policy registry) with Model Plane (capability-core enforcement, model-gateway mode clamp) and Frontend Plane (hub)
items.risks: Policy sprawl; remote config must only tighten; lockdown must be testable end to end.

alreadyPlanned.where: R-t3-11-08: claude-hermes-deepseek.md section 13.3 status note (2026-08-24): the autonomy ladder and plan-approval control are built; the durable hook store is a listed known gap in the planned-decisions baseline | R-t3-05-09: Partly: apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/apps/verevon-web/plans/system-audits/CHAT_GAP_CLOSURE_PLAN_2026-10-01.md:110 (task B4, Wave 1: feed org hook_context into agentic runs) and OD6 (hooks on the governed agentic loop only). The durable store, handler types, org policy, snapshots and hub are not in the plan.

verevon.exactGap: Named modes do not exist as a product concept: only PermissionMode Auto/Ask/Deny (execution-core permission/mod.rs:6-20, whose from_wire maps any unknown string to Auto), a server-floored ApprovalPosture per profile (model-gateway profile.rs:95-125) and a plan-approval AutonomyRung grant (mp-contracts autonomy.rs:45-59, ChatMessages.tsx:2536-2542) exist, with no per-thread or Space persistence and no org cap. The hook engine is real (execution-core hook/mod.rs:113) but HookRegistry is in-memory (runtime_registries.rs:2003), RegisterHook has no gateway or UI caller (grpc.rs:2052), hook_context reaches only browser runs and the chat code_interpreter call (browser_run.rs:418, tools.rs:211) while the Do loop passes an empty string (agent.rs:1927); a durable hook_configs table already exists in session-core (migration 0004:165) but nothing reads or writes it except GDPR erasure. There is no org policy registry, setting lock, lockdown profile, frozen tool snapshot or unified Customize hub; a per-server exact-name MCP tool_allowlist (fail-closed) and admin Settings sections for MCP servers, plugins, skills and org instructions do exist, but tool schemas are re-discovered live (runtime_registries.rs:797) and plugin manifests are inert.
reuse: AutonomyRung ladder, strictly-wider escalation and per-call permits() check (mp-contracts autonomy.rs)
resolve_posture / floor_from_scopes tighten-only clamp (model-gateway profile.rs) as the model for min(org cap, user choice)
execution-core hook engine (allow/deny/ask, glob match, Pre/PostToolUse) and model-gateway hook_context_json serialiser
session-core hook_configs schema (migration 0004) as a ready durable store, or capability-core as owner per the ownership matrix
capability-core plugin_packages (enabled, pinned, rollout_state, risk_level) and capability scope grant/revoke/resolve routes
MCP per-server tool_allowlist and org/private/shared scope (McpServersSection.tsx, runtime_registries.rs filter_allowlist)
Existing Settings sections (mcp, skills, plugins, org-instructions, persona, integrations) as the hub backbone
Control-signed decision key distribution (CONTROL_SPACE_DECISION_KEY_ID / public key env) for signed policy bundles
verevon.constraints: Control Plane owns org identity and policy, so the registry and its signing belong there; Model Plane only enforces and must verify signed bundles (no cross-plane DB reads). Policy may only tighten: copy the resolve_posture rule that a client request can raise strictness but never fall below the server floor. Owner-plane effects are never auto-approved (permission/mod.rs:53-58), so a "full access" mode cannot lower that durable-approval requirement. PermissionMode::from_wire currently fails open to Auto for unknown strings, so new modes must not ride that parser until it fails closed. ZDR turns run a persistence-free path that already refuses tool lists and plan mode (model-gateway zdr_features.rs), so modes and hooks have nothing to govern there and lockdown must not become a ZDR bypass. Org policy must never widen Space access.
verevon.approachAdjustment: The item bundles seven independent workstreams across three planes; split it. (1) Plan B4 (S): pass hook_context into the Do loop (agent.rs:1927 passes an empty string). (2) Durable hooks: do not invent a table; session-core hook_configs already has the schema, so decide owner (session-core vs capability-core per CR-04), add an admin API and a gateway/UI caller. (3) AgentMode: map each named mode onto the existing PermissionMode plus AutonomyRung server-side, clamped by an org cap. (4) Org policy registry, locks and lockdown: Control Plane, signed, tighten-only, with a fail-closed value per key. (5) Frozen tool snapshots: pin tool name plus description hash plus schema hash at admin approval (today only names are allow-listed). (6) Hub: extend the existing Settings sections; the premise that admins have no product surface is wrong for MCP, plugins, skills and org instructions, and the real gap is hooks, modes and locks. Also correct "hooks only reach browser runs": they also reach the chat code_interpreter call.
verevon.effortNote: As one item this spans Control (registry, signing), Model Plane (clamp, hooks, snapshots) and Frontend (hub, mode picker), so L understates it. Split as S (Do-run hook_context, already plan B4), M (durable hooks plus admin API), M (AgentMode), L (policy registry, locks, lockdown), M (hub and frozen snapshots).
verevon.verdictReason: The enforcement core and several admin surfaces already exist, so the item must stop implying an empty product surface and must be split; the true gaps are named modes, durable hooks wired to Do runs, org locks and lockdown, snapshot pinning and a unified hub.

items.title: Content-safety hardening: an injection normaliser, enforcing semantic screening for web and browser content, one policy check on every memory and skill write, and safe links
items.summary: Add a normaliser before scan_injection (NFKC, strip tag-block and zero-width characters, confusable folding, neutralise forged envelope tags), promote the semantic ContentSafety pass from shadow to enforcing for ExternalWeb and Browser trust classes after a false-positive eval, run one deterministic memory policy (identifiers, account and card numbers, credentials, special-category data) on every memory write path including manual and imported memory, govern skill writes, and add safe-link handling and safety UX.
items.whyItMatters: Trust-class provenance and a fail-closed scan are already ahead of most references, but the scanner is evadable by Unicode tricks and memory writes outside the extractor bypass the sensitive-data rule. As browser and connector reads arrive (F-t3-008, F-t3-010) injection exposure grows sharply. Perplexity's layered stack and Claude's homoglyph-aware scrubber are the references.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Perplexity (most layered documented stack: intent anchoring, screening classifier, containment, runtime monitoring) and Claude (homoglyph-aware scrubber neutralising forged envelope tags) for injection; Hermes for memory and skill write governance (staged entry-pinned writes, review fork limited to an allowlist, install-scan trust matrix) ; claude (import flow); web-claudeai (sensitive policy); hermes (write-tool mechanics)
