items.title: Trajectory ledger with exact model-visible request capture and timing waterfall
items.summary: Add a complete second view of every run next to the chat: a virtualised, grouped ledger (turn, step, request, tool call, sub-call) with a per-record inspector (raw record, payload, result, tool schema, request options, system prompt in effect, usage, timing) and an Inspect action on each chat tool card. Back it with request_snapshot events written at the model call site (parameters, adapter defaults, content-addressed system-prompt and tool-catalogue blobs, auxiliary calls labelled by purpose) and step-level timing events drawn as a waterfall that shows 'unavailable' instead of estimates.
items.whyItMatters: DeepSeek's 'maximum information, very transparent' is an explicit Verevon reference, and long Do-mode and browser runs cannot be explained from a flat event list. This is the strongest single transparency gap: users, support and engineers cannot see what the model was actually sent, which also blocks replay tests (R-t3-10-11) and trustworthy audit.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: deepseek
others: antigravity (DEBUG/FULL verbosity stream, queue and hook/approval time in timing)
t3code (native and canonical provider streams logged side by side)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: Ledger: 2 of 12 (differentiator); request capture: 4 of 12 (common); timing waterfall: 3 of 12 (differentiator)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: DeepSeek keeps the invariant 'model-visible implies logged': one append-only per-session log; a request header event {config, adapterDefaults, tools} is appended only when it differs from the previous one; the system prompt is a diffable event; auxiliary requests are logged before dispatch. The ledger is a projection grouped by turn, step and request with request numbers and cumulative usage, 13 inspector tabs, and an Inspect action on each chat tool card. The waterfall is drawn from recorded timestamps only, with time-to-first-token split from decoding and in-flight records showing only a start marker.

verevonToday.gap: The Trace tab is a flat durable run-event list capped at 5,000 with proof and receipts. There is no turn/step/request grouping, no inspector tabs, no Inspect link from a tool card. The context inspector (GET /v1/threads/:id/context, GetContextAssembly) shows assembled segments and token counts, but no per-request snapshot of effective parameters, the exact system prompt or the tool catalogue is persisted or served, and auxiliary calls (title, follow-ups, verification pass) are not shown as requests. Timing is per turn (turn_timing phases plus provider intervals), not per step or tool; no copyable trace/request id was found in the chat UI (INF from grep).

items.approach: Deliver in three slices. (1) Projection and UI: session-core exposes GET /v1/runs/:id/trajectory that groups stored events by turn, step and request (browser actions grouped by action_id); verevonv3 upgrades the Trace tab to a virtualised grouped ledger with an inspector drawer, and tool-presentation carries the event id so tool cards get Inspect. (2) Request capture: at the model-gateway/execution-core call site write request_snapshot events to session-core (provider, model, effort, params, adapter default flags, tool schema list) only when changed, with system prompt and tool catalogue stored as hash-addressed blobs in MinIO (deduplicated), and purpose-labelled auxiliary calls; under ZDR persist only hashes and parameter metadata and render 'not retained (ZDR)'. Decide which Verevon persona/policy prompt text is shown versus hashed. (3) Timing: emit step_timing {step_id, queued_at, started_at, first_token_at, ended_at} from the existing OTEL spans (including approval wait and hooks), expose trace id on usage, draw the waterfall strip, add a copy-trace-id action. Owner-only access as today; never widen Space ACLs.
items.planeOwner: Model Plane (session-core, model-gateway, execution-core) and Frontend Plane (Trace tab)
items.risks: Prompt and payload tabs can expose tenant secrets or other users' content in shared Spaces, so they stay owner-only with redaction and no ACL widening; ZDR must propagate (no prompt content persisted); persona/policy prompt IP visibility needs a decision; storage growth and virtualisation for very large runs; clock skew across services must never be papered over by synthesised timings.

verevon.exactGap: SRC: the Trace tab (TracePanel) is a flat, user-safe projection of durable run events capped at 5,000 plus the proof bundle; the context inspector (GET /v1/threads/:id/context to GetContextAssembly) already shows assembled segments with content and token estimates; per-turn timing (turn_timing phases and provider intervals) reaches the UI only as model-time and system-time totals and is not persisted per step; the per-message popover lists tool names. No request_snapshot exists: the exact system prompt, tool catalogue, effective parameters and auxiliary calls (title, follow-ups, verification) are neither persisted nor served, and there is no turn/step/request grouping, inspector drawer, waterfall, Inspect link on tool cards or copyable trace id. The model-gateway trajectory store is an in-memory 200-per-org ring buffer for training export, not a user surface.

turn_timing phase spans and provider timing as the data source for step timing (extend, persist as content-free events)

RunProofPanel and the proof bundle for receipts

verevon.constraints: Request capture adds a new durable copy of customer content (prompts carry recalled memory, retrieved documents and org/Space instructions), so it must sit inside retention, erasure and ZDR: thread delete, Space deletion reconciler, GDPR purge and memory erasure must reach it, ZDR runs keep hashes and parameter metadata only (turn timing and provider timing are explicitly content-free for that reason), and content-hash dedup must be tenant-keyed so a shared hash cannot reveal another tenant's content. Owner-only access and no ACL widening. The Trace panel today promises no hidden reasoning or credentials and which platform or policy prompt text is shown is a product decision. verevon.approachAdjustment: Order the slices by risk: (1) projection and UI first (group existing run events by turn, step and action_id, an inspector drawer, event id on tool cards, copy trace id), which needs no new storage; (2) persisted step timing as content-free events extending turn_timing; (3) request capture last, short-retention and tenant-keyed, hashes only under ZDR, wired into the erasure paths, and not stored in full by default.
verevon.effortNote: Unchanged; slice 1 is roughly L, slice 2 M, slice 3 L because of the erasure and tenancy requirements.
verevon.verdictReason: The gap statement is accurate (flat trace list, no request capture, no step timing) and the item is a real transparency gap versus the DeepSeek reference; only additive constraints are needed.

items.title: Wide research: user entry point, honest estimate and spend gate, per-item retry, replay after reload
items.summary: Give the existing subagent.research_fan_out engine a product surface. Add a 'Bred forskning' control with item-count presets, a start card that states the expected scale before anything is spawned (items x rounds x minutes, plus cost on metered routes), a status grid of per-item cards with retry for failed or refused items, a mid-run progress and spend check after the first N items (Continue or Wrap up now), and durable per-item results so the grid survives a reload. Under ZDR the grid stays live-only.
items.whyItMatters: Wide research is Manus's signature feature and serves Verevon's B2B lists (suppliers, competitors, leads). The engine is already paid for; without an entry point, a cost statement and retry it is unusable and unsafe, and a cost gate fits Verevon's honest-cost stance.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Manus (manus-product-ux-038 SRC UX, web-manus-web-product-023 DOC architecture)
others: Manus web (DOC): plan limits on concurrency and task count
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 2 of 11 sources (both Manus); differentiator
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Controller decomposes into independent items -> estimate a cost range from per-item budget x item count -> start card with Start or 'Always auto-start' -> spawn up to K concurrent isolated sub-runs, each in its own context -> stream per-item status into a 3-column grid with replay link and retry -> after the first N items compute actual spend and show a Skip or Continue card -> 'Wrap up now' -> controller merges structured per-item results. Sub-agents never talk to each other.

verevonToday.gap: SRC: engine exists (one tool call, N parallel items, structured per-item results merged in order, kill switch WIDE_RESEARCH_FAN_OUT_ENABLED, default concurrency 4) and live cards by batchId exist. Missing: a composer entry point (planned C6), a pre-run estimate and accept gate, a mid-run spend check, per-item retry, durable replay (cards come back empty after reload, planned C7), and scale (default 4 rounds and 2 subagents on the subscription route; 12/24/48 presets wait on owner decision OD7). Do mode only. DOC: on the subscription route cost-core meters nothing (CostBasis::Subscription), so a USD budget is a no-op there.

items.approach: Model Plane execution-core: add an estimate step before spawning that is computed from item count, round budget and observed per-item p50 time, and expressed in items, rounds and minutes (USD only when the route is metered, via a run-scoped cost-core check such as the planned cost_guard.rs). Emit an awaiting-approval style start card that the user can set to 'always auto-start', and after the first N completed items emit a progress and spend card with Continue or Wrap up now. Persist the batch and per-item results in session-core so replay works after reload, and add a retry action per item that re-spawns only that child (research-only toolset, C8). Long batches run through the existing WideResearch Temporal workflow (apps/Model Plane/go/services/orchestrator-core/cmd/workflows/wide_research.go). Frontend: 'Bred forskning' control, estimate card, grid with retry, spend card. Under ZDR skip persistence and degrade to a live-only grid.
items.planeOwner: Model Plane
items.risks: Spend blowouts and provider rate limits at scale. OD7 recommends no confirm gate in v1; the estimate card should therefore default to informational for small runs and gate only above an org-set size. Credential lifetime caps wide research at about 6 to 8 items on Terra without C9. ZDR forbids durable replay.

Retry means re-spawning one child with the original item text, so store the full item goal or re-read the parent tool input. items.title: Persistent goals with a token budget, a completion judge and auto-continuation
items.summary: Add a Goal record in session-core {objective, success_criteria, token_budget, used, status active|completed|blocked|cancelled} and a continuation driver, hosted as a Temporal workflow in orchestrator-core, that starts budgeted Do runs until a cheap judge model (verevon-balance) confirms the criteria with evidence, or a budget or blocker is hit, then notifies the user. The Agent Run Console's goal launcher is the natural UI host, with a goal bar showing budget used and compare-and-set edits.
items.whyItMatters: Outcome agents that work for a long time are the core of the Manus and ChatGPT Work vision, and goals are present in 6 of 12 references. Verevon has no goal primitive, and long autonomous work is also capped by the 300 s delegated bearer and a default of 4 rounds, so a user cannot hand over a multi-step objective and come back to a result.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Codex (persisted ThreadGoal with token budget and an audited completion check)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 6 of 12 sources (common)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Goal{objective, success_criteria, token_budget, used, status}. When the run goes idle, a continuation driver re-prompts with the goal state; a cheap judge checks completion against the criteria with evidence; stop on budget exhaustion or a blocker and notify. Completion is audited, not self-declared by the worker model.

verevonToday.gap: No durable goal, budget accounting, completion judge or continuation driver. A Do run ends when its rounds end, and delegated authority lapses after 300 s.

items.approach: Model Plane. Goal rows and budget accounting in session-core; a GoalContinuation workflow in orchestrator-core that starts budgeted Do runs (same start path as scheduled runs), calls a judge through inference-core with the success criteria and the run's proof bundle and postcondition results, and updates the goal; renewable delegated credential so each continuation re-checks authority through the Control reauthorizer; goal bar and budget display in the Agent Run Console and the Work panel; cost reservation per continuation.
items.planeOwner: Model Plane
items.risks: Runaway cost (hard budget, per-continuation reservation); each continuation must re-verify authority; judge model can be gamed, so tie it to deterministic postconditions and the proof bundle where available; do not auto-continue across approval-required effects without a human.

verevon.exactGap: No Goal record, budget accounting, completion judge or continuation driver exists. The nearest primitives are an in-memory TeamWorker (objective, context, success_criteria, no budget or judge) in coordinator.rs, a run's plain goal string, deterministic postcondition verifiers for effects, and the scheduled-step lane, which is one tool-less, 1,024-token, tool_choice none inference per step (execution-core grpc.rs:498-523) and so cannot continue a Do run. A run ends when its rounds end (DEFAULT_MAX_ROUNDS 12) and its credentials lapse at the delegated bearer lifetime.
reuse: ScheduledRunSupervision and the per-fire Control authorization pattern (reauthorizeScheduleFire, AuthorizeScheduledStep) as the model for per-continuation authority
scheduled_inference_auth.rs service credential minting (narrow inference:invoke scope) if the judge runs service-side
postcondition.rs, verified_outcome.proto and proof_bundle.proto as deterministic completion evidence for effectful goals
RunDeadline in run_budget.rs and cost-core GetRunUsage for budget accounting
session-core Plan and Todo records and the Work panel for goal progress display
AgentRunConsole goal launcher and schedule-from-chat for the UI entry and "continue later"
verevon.constraints: Each continuation is unattended work, so it needs fresh Control-owned authorization; the only unattended lane today (model.schedule.step) is tool-less single-step and the workflow is marked DeniesZDR, and an unattended governed Do-run lane does not exist (plan D10 is an L, OD8 is the credential decision). A durable Goal row persists content, so ZDR threads must be refused (the item omits ZDR). Go workflow step responses carry no usage (the AutoresearchWorkflow exclusion in workflowreg.go says so), so token budget must come from cost-core run usage, and on the Subscription route nothing is metered so a token budget is a no-op. Never auto-continue across approval-required effects (ScheduledRunSupervision already fails on NeedsApproval). The judge call must inherit the turn privacy-tier floor.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Do not describe the driver as starting Do runs on "the same start path as scheduled runs": that lane executes one tool-less inference. Reframe as (1) a Goal record and budget ledger in session-core, non-ZDR only; (2) a continuation workflow modelled on ScheduledRunSupervision that obtains fresh Control authorization per continuation and starts a governed RunAgent, which requires the unattended Do-run lane (D10 and OD8) first; (3) a judge that prefers the proof bundle and postcondition results and falls back to a rubric judge through inference-core. A smaller attended first slice is possible: a goal bar in the Agent Run Console that auto-continues while the user session still holds delegated authority, with no new credential class.
verevon.effortNote: Raised from L: new durable record, a new unattended governed-run authority lane across Control and Model Plane, a judge, budget accounting from cost-core and the UI. L only for the attended first slice.
verevon.verdictReason: The gap is real and fully absent, but the premise that the scheduled lane can start budgeted Do runs is wrong and ZDR is missing from the constraints, so approach, dependencies and effort must change before it is planned.

items.title: Deck pipeline with brand templates: tool-owned slide manifest, per-slide validation, present mode, research-to-deck, and an org template library
items.summary: Add a slides tool family over a versioned deck manifest (per-slide state planned, authored, valid; layout, content, notes) that generates native editable PPTX slide by slide in the sandbox, validates each slide through the render step of F-t3-014 and refuses delivery until every slide is valid. Add a slide strip and present mode, chain deep-research reports into decks, and introduce a template skill kind (reference file, preview, brand tokens) scoped to org or Space with a picker card.
items.whyItMatters: Decks are a common deliverable (4 of 11) and Manus Slides shows the most robust mechanism; Codex's template skills show how to carry brand. Verevon has only browser-side PPTX export of chat text.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Manus Slides (DOC and SRC): an MCP slides server with a tool-owned project manifest, per-slide state, XML validation hooks and a present gate ; Codex (SRC): artifact-template-<slug> skill folders with a manifest, a picker tool using form elicitation with thumbnails, and a gallery with view, edit, share and uninstall
others: claude desktop (SRC, design-system restyle, authorship labels)
Perplexity web (DOC, research hands off to asset skills)
claude desktop (SRC) and claude.ai (DOC) for design-system tokens and self-check
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: R-t3-02-05: Decks: 4 of 11 sources (2 distinct vendors), common. Research-to-deliverable chaining: 1 of 11, unique | R-t3-02-08: Templates: 1 of 11, unique. Design systems and canvas: 2 of 11 (one vendor), differentiator
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Manifest {deck_id, template_id, slides[{id, state: planned|edit_pending|authored|valid, layout, content, notes}]} owned by the tool and never hand-edited. Template = skill folder {SKILL.md instructions, manifest {kind document|presentation|spreadsheet, reference asset, preview image}}.

items.approach: Plan H8 (deck v1) after H4 (native charts); templates as skill bundles on F-t3-014's format.
items.planeOwner: Model Plane (slides tool, capability-core templates) with Frontend Plane (slide strip, present mode) and Data Plane (reference assets)

alreadyPlanned.where: R-t3-02-05: Plan H8 (deck path v1: research report to a designed .pptx with notes and charts, Wave 5, depends on H4) is in apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/apps/verevon-web/plans/system-audits/CHAT_GAP_CLOSURE_PLAN_2026-10-01.md:206,249 with a COM open check as exit criterion at :255. The per-slide manifest, validation gate, present mode and slide strip are not in the plan (INF, not found there). | R-t3-02-08: Only a seam: a neutral deck theme with a DeckTheme seam is the plan recommendation at apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/apps/verevon-web/plans/system-audits/CHAT_GAP_CLOSURE_PLAN_2026-10-01.md:504 (owner ruling OD18). A template library is not in the plan (INF, not found there).

verevon.exactGap: Decks are already producible two ways: the model writes python-pptx inside code_interpreter (advertised at tool_loop.rs:4320, python-pptx 1.0.2 baked into the execution-core image) and the browser turns one answer into a PPTX (chat-export/pptx.ts planSlides, one slide per level-1/2 heading with a bullet and character budget). What does not exist is any tool-owned deck manifest or per-slide state, any render or validation step (the sandbox image installs no renderer such as LibreOffice and the per-call workspace is deleted when the call returns), a slide strip or present mode (no hits in the frontend or Model Plane), and any template or brand-token skill kind (AgentSkill is text content plus triggers and tool restrictions only). Plan H8 (research report to designed PPTX, Wave 5, depends on H4 native charts) is the planned seed and OD18 recommends a neutral theme with a DeckTheme seam, but H8 has no manifest, validation gate, present mode or template library.
reuse: code_interpreter (python-pptx, matplotlib PNG charts, files_in staging up to 8 MiB per file and 16 MiB total, generated files returned as download cards)
chat-export/pptx.ts planSlides and layout constants as the in-browser fallback and for a manifest-driven preview
session-core agent_skills plus capability-core skill promotion (scope org|user, shared_with) as the delivery vehicle for template skills
durable Space workspace design (workspace_hydrate.rs, sandbox.rs extra_ro_binds read-only layers) for mounting template files into the sandbox; hydrate is still standalone per its own header
artifacts pipeline (ArtifactKind::File) for delivery; plan items H4 (native charts) and H8 (deck path v1)
verevon.constraints: The sandbox is MpNetworkPolicy::Disabled with a ~30 s timeout and a workspace deleted after every call, so the manifest must be owned by the tool or gateway (not the sandbox) and brand templates must be staged through files_in or read-only workspace layers, never fetched. Under ZDR the gateway does not seed or persist artifacts (sse.rs:4047-4057), so a durable manifest and org template library must be refused or kept client-session-only for ZDR threads. Brand and template files are org or Space content owned by Data Plane (document is the only ownable resource type in user-core's taxonomy), and Space access never widens that ACL. The per-slide render gate depends on a renderer that does not exist in the sandbox image (F-t3-014), which adds image size and attack surface.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Do not frame it as a new slides tool family on top of nothing: first deliver plan H4/H8 on the existing code_interpreter path, then add the manifest as a small validated JSON schema that a deck-build helper renders with python-pptx, and have the SPA draw the slide strip and present mode from the manifest JSON rather than from the PPTX. Make per-slide validation structural (shape bounds, overflow heuristics, notes present) unless F-t3-014 lands a real renderer. Ship templates as org-authored skills first and brand tokens through the DeckTheme seam, which is what OD18 and OD19 ('templates are user-authored first') already recommend; the reference file and preview parts of a template skill need Data Plane storage, not the agent_skills text column.
verevon.effortNote: Kept at L on the assumption that the F-t3-014 render step and plan H4 charts land separately; without a renderer the validation gate is structural only, and adding a renderer to the sandbox image would push this to XL.
verevon.verdictReason: Not shipped, but the item's premise that only a browser-side export exists is wrong (code_interpreter python-pptx is advertised and baked into the image) and plan H8 already plans the base deck path; the real delta is manifest, validation gate, present mode and template library, so the recommendation should be rewritten as that delta on top of H8.

items.title: Runtime release safety: signed candidate and separate rollback artifact, rehearsed rollback, deployed audit fix and a release gate
items.summary: Finish artifact format v3 end to end: build a signed candidate per release (image digests, migration set, compatibility gates) and a separate accepted rollback artifact, rehearse restoring it against a database snapshot, deploy the already-built audit publisher fix and replay the stuck rows, and gate deploys on a release-evidence check in coresystem-conformance.sh with numeric canary and rollback thresholds.
items.whyItMatters: Verevon cannot claim production readiness, or defend a ZDR and audit promise to enterprise buyers, without a reproducible signed release and a proven rollback. Postmortem 0002 shows the failure mode: a built fix sat undeployed while 4,992 audit events stayed stuck.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: T3 Code
others: Claude desktop app (signed manifest, staged rollout)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 4 of 12 (common)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: T3 installs the new version beside the old, preflights it, starts a trial child against a database snapshot and rolls back on failure. Claude ships a signed manifest {version, artifacts[sha256, size], compat} with staged rollout; Hermes restarts drain-first and keeps receipts for interrupted steps.

verevonToday.gap: SRC/DOC: artifact v3 tooling (11 services, pinned infrastructure images, refuses a dirty tree) and graceful drain exist, and the evidence register defines candidate and rollback evidence classes. The roadmap states no signed candidate or rollback artifact has been built, and postmortem 0002 (2026-10-06) records the audit publisher fix as built but not deployed. These docs are dated (the roadmap text also describes the approval dispatcher as missing although the worker now exists), so the current state needs a code-level re-check.

items.approach: Run artifact v3 in release mode with signing and verification keys; produce a separate rollback artifact from the prior revision; script a rollback rehearsal that restores the retained digest and runs the migration revert scripts against a snapshot; add a release-evidence check to coresystem-conformance.sh that fails when candidate or rollback evidence is missing; require forward-compatible (expand/contract) migrations; define canary thresholds and observation windows; deploy the session-core audit publisher fix and requeue the stuck rows.
items.planeOwner: Model Plane (release tooling), Infra Plane for deploy
items.risks: Rolling back Postgres migrations that changed data requires forward-compatible schemas; a rehearsal on production-shaped data is needed. Release gates can block urgent fixes without an emergency path.

alreadyPlanned.where: MODEL_PLANE_ROADMAP.md next steps 5-9 (signed artifact-v3 candidate, separate rollback artifact, canary thresholds); postmortem 0002 (publisher fix built, not deployed)

verevon.exactGap: SRC: most of the tooling is built. scripts/release-artifact.sh (1,917 lines, format v3, 11 services plus pinned infrastructure images) has dry-run/build/verify/restore/compose/deploy subcommands, signed root-manifest verification, an external rollback-artifact locator that must resolve to a distinct trusted-signed root, rollback runtime-evidence binding and release-mode gates, and coresystem-conformance.sh already adds blockers candidate_artifact_missing, rollback_artifact_missing and unapproved acceptance thresholds. Still open: no signed candidate or rollback artifact has been produced (evidence register row reads absent | absent), the thresholds file holds nine proposed operational values and no canary error-rate or latency thresholds, only two session-core migrations (0044, 0045) have revert scripts and no rehearsal restores a database snapshot, and per DOC postmortem 0002 the audit-publisher fix (commit b9ed9197, 2026-10-08) and requeue function (migration 0043) are built but not deployed with 4,992 rows unreplayed.

verevon.constraints: This is operator and Infra work around Model Plane release tooling, not a product surface. Secrets stay out of the artifact (RUNTIME_SECRET_KEYS partition), the rollback artifact must be an independently signed external root, and rolling back Postgres schema changes needs forward-compatible expand/contract migrations. The evidence register is dated (2026-08-17 status) and the conformance script reads a markdown table row, so state claims must be re-verified live and a machine-verifiable signal is preferable. Release gates need an emergency path.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Reword as 'run and prove' rather than 'finish artifact v3': replace the grep of the evidence-register row in coresystem-conformance.sh with a check of the signed manifest and rollback evidence files; add canary thresholds (error rate, p95 latency, ZDR residual bytes) to the thresholds TSV and obtain owner approval; add a rehearsal script that restores the rollback artifact and applies revert scripts to a snapshot, with an explicit expand/contract or forward-only policy for the migrations that lack revert scripts; deploy the publisher fix, run the requeue function and confirm the rows in audit_events (operator action).
verevon.effortNote: Unchanged: most tooling exists, so remaining effort is thresholds, a rehearsal script, the migration policy and operator deployment with signing keys.
verevon.verdictReason: The recommendation understates what is built (signing, rollback artifact validation, conformance gate) and overstates what is code work; the remaining gaps are canary thresholds, a rehearsal, migration revert policy and actually deploying the audit fix.

items.title: Eval and replay release gates for prompts, tools and routing: recorded-session replay in CI, required eval stages and an eval gate on RoutingPolicy edits
items.summary: Add a replay inference provider that serves recorded completions so committed session logs replay through model-gateway in CI, make eval-lab a required stage for prompt and tool-schema changes, require a passing task-suite comparison (quality, cost, latency per role and model) before a production org's RoutingPolicy edit is accepted, stamp experiment ids on runs, and add user-path budgets.
items.whyItMatters: Verevon edits routing tables at runtime and changes prompts often, but live evals do not run in CI and routing edits are not gated. DeepSeek, Antigravity and Codex show replay and eval gates as the way to change agent behaviour safely.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: deepseek ; codexagent (codexagent-agent-runtime-and-models-091 model-migration playbook); antigravity (091 best-of-N battle mode, 090 experiment overrides)
others: hermes (compaction scored by what a fresh model can still answer; A/B runs with seeded data and programmatic oracles; 36 eval directories)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: R-t3-10-11: Replay tests 2 of 12; behavioural evals 3 of 12 (differentiator); generated docs 1 of 12; user-path budgets 1 of 12 (unique) | R-t3-09-11: 3 of 12 for evals (differentiator); 2 of 12 for remote config; 1 of 12 for best-of-N (unique)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: DeepSeek commits 600 session logs across 227 scenarios and replays them through shipped profiles with an llm-replay provider, tokenises volatile ids, and requires every model- or user-visible change to update a scenario in the same PR; An embedded skill inventories every model usage site, classifies it, maps flagship, balanced and fast roles and validates against a matrix rather than blind string replacement;

verevonToday.gap: R-t3-10-11: SRC: a compaction-recall eval harness ships, and eval-lab CI runs only the credential-free selftest (live evals are deliberately not run in CI); | R-t3-09-11: Only the routing table is runtime-editable;

items.approach: Replay provider in inference-core; corpus captured via the request capture of F-t3-034; eval job in the Go durable tier.
items.planeOwner: Model Plane (inference-core, eval-lab, orchestrator-core)
items.risks: CI cost and flakiness; recorded sessions must be scrubbed of customer content.

alreadyPlanned.where: R-t3-09-11: Eval architecture proposed in docs/MODEL_PLANE_IMPROVEMENTS_2026.md section 19 (v-modelplane baseline line 329)

verevon.exactGap: Shipped: eval-lab-py (12 baseline plus 2 compaction YAML cases, metrics.py runners, optional LLM judge, report.py) with a CI job that runs only the credential-free selftest and only on changes under eval-lab-py, an SSE-taxonomy gate, contract-golden checks, and in-process mock inference servers in Rust tests. Missing: a recorded-completion replay provider (the only 'replay' in code is session-core event-fold determinism and SSE Last-Event-ID buffering), any CI stage triggered by prompt or tool-schema changes, any comparison or promotion code (the README claims A/B and promotion reports, src has none), experiment-id stamping and user-path budgets (mp-slo is a performance harness). RoutingPolicy edits are not gated: it is one platform-global JSONB row (session-core routing_policy_grpc.rs set_policy, admin scope, version bump) that inference-core's PUT hot-swaps after serde validation only.
evidence: apps/Model Plane/python/eval-lab-py/src/eval_lab (cases, client, judge, metrics, report, runner, types; no compare or promote code)
reuse: eval-lab-py cases, runner and report writer
mp-slo harness
existing in-process inference doubles (MockInference in execution-core runtime_loop/agent.rs:5546, MockInferenceOk in model-gateway grpc.rs:2932) as the seam for a replay fake
sse-taxonomy.yml as the precedent for a path-triggered required check
orchestrator-core SkillPromotion workflow (candidate, gate, promote) as the pattern for policy promotion
RoutingPolicy serde-default pattern for adding fields without breaking stored rows
the dataplane-v2-eval-nightly.yml scheduled eval job (listed, not opened) as a precedent
verevon.constraints: RoutingPolicy is platform-global (id=1 singleton), not per-org, so 'a production org's RoutingPolicy edit' is a misdescription: the gate protects every tenant's routing and belongs at the store owner (session-core set_policy) or at inference-core put_policy, which also hard-codes updated_by to inference-core-admin and so loses the admin identity for audit. Live evals need provider credentials and spend, so they cannot be a synchronous gate on a PUT; they must be an async candidate, evaluate, promote flow or a scheduled job, as eval-lab.yml itself argues. Recorded sessions must be synthetic or scrubbed: customer content and ZDR turns must never be committed or replayed (ZDR must propagate). No cross-plane DB access: replay goes through gRPC or HTTP surfaces.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Do not make F-t3-034 request capture a prerequisite for the first slice. Start with synthetic, hand-authored recorded completions served by a replay fake at the InferenceCore gRPC boundary (the pattern the existing Mock servers use), keeping a replay provider out of the production inference-core binary; capture-based corpora can follow. Re-target the routing gate to the platform-global policy as a candidate state with an async eval-lab comparison (quality, cost, latency per role and model) before promote, instead of rejecting a PUT. Widen eval-lab.yml path filters to model-gateway prompt and tool-schema files so a required stage can trigger at all. Either build the A/B code or correct the README before citing it.
verevon.effortNote: Unchanged as a bundle. Replay fake plus a path-filtered CI stage is about M, the routing candidate and promote workflow is M to L, and experiment ids and user-path budgets should be split out as separate S or M items.
verevon.verdictReason: Core claims verified (selftest-only CI, no replay provider, no routing gate), but the routing target is platform-global, the replay seam should not depend on F-t3-034, and the item must not imply the eval harness itself is missing.

items.title: Model record v2 and role table: one inference-core model record (context, modalities, effort ladder, lifecycle, price, privacy, residency) rendered by a searchable picker, and purpose-tagged role routing for every inference call
items.summary: Replace the thin ModelDescriptor with a versioned ModelRecord owned by inference-core and validated at admission, render it in a searchable picker with locked-model reasons, and add a role dimension to RoutingPolicy (chat, planner, worker, title, compaction, memory_extract, vision, scheduled) that replaces hard-coded side-task models, with a purpose tag on every inference call and multimodal input routing.
items.whyItMatters: The SPA cannot gate controls per model because ListModels lacks context window, modalities and effort ladder; side tasks use constants. Codex, T3 Code, Hermes and DeepSeek show the record, picker and role table.

PrivacyTier and residency already on ModelInfo

verevon.constraints: inference-core owns capability, cost-core owns pricing and session-core stores the routing policy, so the record must join by id rather than copy prices or policies across planes (no cross-plane DB access). Role routing must respect ZDR and privacy tier: today title, follow-up and judge calls pin a model regardless of the caller's min privacy tier, so a role resolver has to filter by the caller's posture. The pinned side-task models exist for a documented reason (a reasoning-tier model returned empty output at tiny budgets), so a role entry must carry a non-reasoning and small-budget constraint, not just a model id. The SPA must render no claim for fields the server omits (the existing privacyTier rule).
verevon.approachAdjustment: Correct two premises: the browser planner already resolves through the intent tier (verevon-balance) with an env override, so it is not a hard-coded constant, and per-model gating by features[] and provider already exists. Split: (1) S-M extend ModelInfo and ModelDescriptor with context window, max output and effort ladder (from ProviderCapabilities, per-model overrides only where they differ), join price from cost-core, and add a search box to both pickers; (2) M role table as a new serde-default field on RoutingPolicy (title, follow_ups, judge, planner, compaction, memory_extract, vision) replacing the gpt-4o-mini constants through a resolver that honours the reasoning-tier constraint and rejects role model ids not in the deployed catalogue; (3) S-M purpose tag as a new InferRequest field feeding metrics and cost attribution (none exists today).
verevon.effortNote: Unchanged as a bundle: a proto change across inference-core, gateway and SPA, a routing-policy schema change and picker work. Part (1) alone is M.
verevon.verdictReason: Partial status confirmed (thin record, constants, no role table, no picker search); fix the planner premise, name cost-core as price owner, and add the reasoning-tier and ZDR constraints on role routing.

items.title: Sandbox egress tiers and a credential-injecting egress proxy, with per-call enforcement reports and shell-grammar approvals
items.summary: Add an org and user network tier (off, package registries, allowlisted domains, all) stamped on the sandbox lease and mapped to the existing fail-closed MpNetworkPolicy, backed by a deployed egress proxy that injects vaulted credentials so sandboxes only ever see sentinels. Surface the per-call 'sandboxed' result and enforcement level in the Do loop and tool cards, add shell-grammar-aware approvals and versioned file writes.
items.whyItMatters: Sandboxes currently have no network, which blocks package installs and API work; references (claude.ai, Manus) use egress tiers, and Claude's credential masking is the safe way to give sandboxes authenticated access. Verevon's fail-closed proxy design is already strict; it needs deploying and exposing.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Claude.ai (four egress tiers with plan-dependent defaults) and Manus (admin policy sets with glob and CIDR applied to sandbox and browser) for egress; DeepSeek (enforcement reported as full or partial per call, denial signatures matched only after runner-failure rules) for transparency; Antigravity (TLS-intercepting proxy with fine-grained resource grants) for credential injection ; Claude (credential masking with sentinel values, per-host injection and SigV4 re-signing) plus DeepSeek (per-call enforcement report: full, partial or none) plus Antigravity (shell-grammar parsing with 'allow always' suggestions) plus Hermes and DeepSeek (version-token guarded file writes)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: R-t3-11-10: egress tiers 3 of 12 and denial transparency 2 of 12 (differentiator); credential isolation 5 of 12 (common) | R-t3-06-07: 1 of 12 each for enforcement report, credential masking and shell-grammar approvals (unique); 3 of 12 for guarded file writes (differentiator)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Policy set {mode allowlist|blocklist, patterns[], cidrs[]} per org, a tier enum on the sandbox lease enforced by a proxy (domains) plus a net namespace (off), changes applying to new leases. Enforcement: the launcher returns {enforcement, mechanisms[], denied, denial_detail} and the card shows a badge.

verevonToday.gap: R-t3-11-10: MpNetworkPolicy has Disabled and AllowDomains variants and the code requires fail-closed behaviour without an egress proxy; | R-t3-06-07: Enforcement: ExecOutcome already carries sandboxed, and a measured capability profile is exposed and pinned by a Control decision, but nothing in the Do-mode loop or the UI reads it per call.

items.approach: Deploy the proxy, add the tier key to the policy registry of F-t3-032, report enforcement per call (DeepSeek's full/partial vocabulary is an open ledger decision).
items.planeOwner: Model Plane (execution-core, capability-core) with Control Plane (secret store)
items.risks: Network access widens exfiltration paths; tiers must default to off for ZDR and high-risk runs.

alreadyPlanned.where: R-t3-11-10: Model Plane/docs/decisions/ledger.md (2026-08-26) records the sandbox full/partial vocabulary as an open design call: the probe exists but no Go consumer reads it

verevon.exactGap: Shipped: MpNetworkPolicy has Disabled, AllowAll and AllowDomains (policy.rs:23-32), executor.rs refuses AllowDomains when no HTTPS_PROXY/ALL_PROXY is set, bwrap unshares the network namespace only for Disabled (sandbox.rs:210-222), code_interpreter hard-codes Disabled (code_interpreter.rs:575-583), and Control already signs a Space capability decision whose egress claim (default disabled_by_default) adds a space:egress permission that sandbox-manager's verifier enforces. Missing: a tier vocabulary (the egress claim is a free-form string and Control has no separate egress entitlement), any deployed sandbox egress proxy (none in deploy or code; the only egress proxy is Quarry's loopback-only DNS-pinned Chromium proxy), any credential store or injection (credential_mode is credential_free), any per-call enforcement field (CodeResult is stdout, stderr, exit_code, files; ExecOutcome.sandboxed is not surfaced; the full/partial vocabulary is an open ledger item with no Go consumer) and shell-grammar approvals. With AllowDomains the network namespace stays shared with the host, so a proxy env var is advisory and a child process can bypass it.
evidence: apps/Model Plane/rust/services/execution-core/src/sandbox.rs:170-230,255-296 (net unshared only for Disabled; SECURITY note; capability profile egress)
apps/Control Plane/user-core/internal/spaces/space_capability_decision.go:64-82,100-175 (space:egress permission when egress != disabled_by_default; Validate checks only presence)
apps/Model Plane/proto/model_plane/v1/sandboxes.proto:15-40 (ActivateLease SCRATCH to ACTIVE for network permission)
apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/docs/S3_2_SANDBOX_LEASE_CLOSEOUT_DESIGN_2026-09-10.md:105-121 (design says non-default egress needs an org entitlement)
apps/Model Plane/docs/decisions/ledger.md:2925-2945 (sandbox full/partial vocabulary open; no Go consumer)
reuse: Control IssueSpaceCapabilityDecision plus sandbox-manager authz capability_verifier: the already-signed egress claim and space:egress permission are the place to stamp a tier
MpNetworkPolicy and executor::require_requested_isolation (fail-closed gate)
SandboxCapabilityProfile.egress and the /capability-profile endpoint (measured side of the claim)
Quarry dns_guard::resolve_public_url and the BrowserEgressReceipt shape for SSRF-safe DNS pinning and per-request receipts
execution-core scrub.rs for output redaction
ActivateLease (SCRATCH to ACTIVE) as the existing lease transition for network permission
verevon.constraints: Egress tiers are Control-owned policy (org and user level, tied to the F-t3-032 registry) carried in the Control-signed Space decision; Model Plane enforces and must stay fail-closed (unknown tier means Disabled). Today Control grants space:egress for any non-default egress claim with no org egress entitlement, contrary to its own design doc, so that must be fixed before tiers. ZDR: the capability decision is ZDR-compatible only because scratch is credential-free and egress-less; any tier above off must be refused or separately gated for ZDR and high-risk runs. Outbound fetching and the SSRF guard belong to Quarry (Ingestion Plane), so a sandbox proxy must reuse that guard instead of re-implementing it. A credential-injecting proxy needs a Control-held secret store; execution-core must never hold plaintext service credentials, and credential_mode is part of the signed claim, so a credentialed backend is a new claim and a new attested backend. Real enforcement needs a dedicated netns or firewall (or the F-t3-009 VM): bwrap with a shared network namespace plus HTTPS_PROXY only constrains cooperative clients.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Reword 'stamp the tier on the sandbox lease': the stamping path exists as the egress claim in the Control-signed Space capability decision (space_capability_decision.go:157, capability_verifier.go:179), so extend that claim with a closed tier enum plus an allowlist digest, add an explicit Control egress entitlement, then map the tier to MpNetworkPolicy in execution-core. Do not deploy a proxy and call AllowDomains enforced; add netns/firewall enforcement or defer to the VM backend, and reuse Quarry's dns_guard. Split: (a) S: add sandboxed/enforcement fields to CodeResult and process_* results from ExecOutcome and the measured profile, shown as a tool-card badge (useful now, while network is simply off); (b) L: tiers, allowlist proxy and namespace enforcement; (c) XL, demote: credential-injecting proxy (TLS interception CA in the sandbox, Control secret store, per-host re-signing); (d) M, separate: shell-grammar approvals; (e) versioned file writes belong to F-t3-030.
verevon.effortNote: As written (tiers, deployed proxy, credential injection, per-call report, shell-grammar approvals, versioned writes) it is XL. Parts (a) and (b) alone are about L; the credential-injecting proxy is the largest separable piece.
verevon.verdictReason: The fail-closed policy, signed egress claim and space:egress gating already exist, so the item should extend them instead of adding a lease key; the proxy as described is advisory under a shared network namespace; and the bundle should be split with the credential proxy demoted.

items.title: Inline interactive outputs: sandboxed generative-UI widgets with a host-validated prompt bridge, selection-to-agent actions and attributed image results
items.summary: Render model-written HTML or SVG widgets inline in the transcript using the existing opaque-origin sandbox, with host theme tokens, a small widget-state store and a narrow postMessage bridge (sendPrompt, resize) whose follow-ups appear as visible, rate-limited user turns. Selecting transcript text or an artifact region produces a typed context item for the agent. Show Quarry image results as an attributed thumbnail strip.
items.whyItMatters: Inline widgets and point-and-edit are common (6 of 12); claude.ai and ChatGPT show the mechanism. Verevon's sandboxed HTML is limited to the Output panel and has no bridge.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Antigravity (SRC), Codex (DOC) and Claude desktop (SRC) for widgets; Manus (SRC) and T3 Code (SRC) for point-and-edit ; claude.ai (DOC) for the general widget mechanism; ChatGPT web (DOC) for curated widget components
others: claude.ai (DOC, Bing image results in the web search tool)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: R-t3-01-11: 6 of 12 for widgets and for point-and-edit (common); 4 of 12 for result cells; 2 of 12 for selection actions | R-t3-02-09: Widgets: 2 of 11, differentiator, documentation-only. Image results in answers: 1 of 11, unique
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Widgets: a show_widget tool returns an HTML fragment rendered in a sandboxed iframe (scripts allowed, no same-origin) under a strict CSP, with semantic CSS variables for light and dark, a postMessage bridge with getState/setState (small JSON snapshot persisted with the message, up to 16 KiB in Codex), sendFollowUp(prompt) gated by a confirmation dialog, and readContext. The model writes HTML or SVG into a sandboxed iframe inline in the message;

verevonToday.gap: R-t3-01-11: Sandboxed HTML (allow-scripts without same-origin) renders only in the Output panel, not inline; | R-t3-02-09: Generated HTML renders in the Output panel in a sandboxed srcdoc iframe (allow-scripts, no same-origin), not inline, and has no bridge back to the chat;

items.approach: Widget chat-node, bridge with strict CSP and no network, confirmation of model-triggered follow-ups.
items.planeOwner: Frontend Plane (widget frame, bridge) with Model Plane (widget artifact kind) and Ingestion Plane (image results)
items.risks: XSS and exfiltration from model code; prompt injection through widget-sent prompts; image copyright (thumbnails with links only).

alreadyPlanned.where: R-t3-01-11: Partly: plan I17 highlight-to-edit (apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/apps/verevon-web/plans/system-audits/CHAT_GAP_CLOSURE_PLAN_2026-10-01.md:253, scope per OD19); inline widgets and result cells are not in the plan

verevon.exactGap: Model-written HTML already renders in a sandboxed iframe (allow-scripts, no allow-same-origin, CSP with default-src none and connect-src none via sandboxHtmlDocument) but only as an html artifact in the Output panel; inline in the transcript there is a ```chart SVG block (ChatChart), a generated-image strip node and a plain artifact chip, and no widget node kind. There is no chat postMessage bridge (a grep of src finds postMessage only in the demo bridge, WorkspaceSettingsPage and the OAuth popup helper), no selection-to-agent context item (plan I17 covers canvas highlight-to-edit only), and Quarry image results (gateway POST /api/v1/search/images) are consumed only by the dashboard search panel, not by chat answers. Artifact kinds are limited to document, code and html (sse_events.rs:880).
reuse: ArtifactHtmlPreview and sandboxHtmlDocument (opaque origin plus strict CSP) as the widget frame
ConversationNode exhaustive registry (add a widget kind; the compiler then forces a renderer)
ChatChart module-level keyed view-state map as the pattern for surviving node remounts
the existing html ChatEvent::Artifact path instead of a new Model Plane artifact kind
GeneratedImagePreviews node and gateway search/images route plus search-client loadSearchImages for the image strip
plan I17 highlight-to-edit for the selection capture instead of a parallel mechanism
verevon.constraints: The widget frame and bridge are Frontend Plane. The bridge must not widen authority: a widget-sent prompt has to go through the normal composer submit path as a visible user turn so ZDR, privacy-tier floor and run policy still apply; the opaque origin and connect-src none must stay (the allow-scripts without allow-same-origin rule is pinned by a test). Widget state snapshots and persisted artifacts must not be stored for ZDR threads. Image results originate in Quarry via the gateway (Ingestion Plane executes); thumbnails with links only, and ZDR turns already refuse web search so they must not show image results either.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Split into three items. Widget core (M): chat nodes are re-derived on every streamed token, so an iframe mounted inside a derived node would reload each time; mount it only when the artifact is complete and keep it in a keyed cache like ChatChart does. Bridge check must compare event.source with the iframe contentWindow because an opaque-origin frame posts with origin "null". Selection-to-context (S to M) belongs with plan I17/OD19. Image strip (S) should be a BFF fetch for web-search turns using the existing /api/v1/search/images, not a new model tool, unless the model proposes the search.
verevon.effortNote: The widget core is M because the sandbox, CSP, artifact event and node registry all exist; the whole three-part bundle stays L only if selection actions and the image strip are kept inside this item.
verevon.verdictReason: Sandboxed HTML and an inline chart already exist, so the item should be reduced to the missing inline node plus bridge and split from the selection and image parts, which have different owners and sizes.

items.title: MCP Apps, elicitation forms and a hosted artifact runtime on a dedicated user-content origin
items.summary: Render tool-supplied UI (MCP ext-apps: ui:// resources) and MCP elicitation forms inside a sandboxed frame served from a dedicated user-content origin by the Rust gateway, with JSON-RPC over postMessage whose tools/call passes the capability gate and approvals. Give interactive artifacts a narrow host bridge (call the model, connectors and a small viewer-scoped key-value store) with viewer identity issued by Control.
items.whyItMatters: MCP Apps are common (6 of 12) and the artifact-as-app pattern (claude.ai, ChatGPT Sites) turns outputs into working tools. Nothing in Verevon implements ui://, elicitation or a host bridge today (absence grep).

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Codex (full ext-apps implementation including a pull-request review workspace; SRC) plus ChatGPT web (postMessage JSON-RPC and CSP model; DOC); Claude desktop and claude.ai for the artifact bridge (SRI-pinned libraries, frame shell on a separate origin, callTool/complete/kv, viewer billed; SRC and DOC); Codex for form elicitation (SRC) ; ChatGPT Sites (DOC)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: R-t3-05-10: MCP Apps 6 of 12, common; elicitation and sampling 2 of 12, differentiator; artifact host bridge 2 of 12, differentiator | R-t3-13-11: 3 of 12 (differentiator; documentation-level evidence only)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Tool metadata _meta.ui.resourceUri (ui:// scheme) -> the host fetches the text/html;profile=mcp-app resource -> renders it in an iframe on a separate origin with sandbox=allow-scripts (no same-origin) and a CSP from _meta. Artifacts are served from a user-content origin and talk to the host through a postMessage bridge;

verevonToday.gap: R-t3-05-10: No baseline record covers MCP Apps, elicitation or an artifact bridge. | R-t3-13-11: SRC: HTML artifacts render through srcdoc in an iframe with sandbox=allow-scripts and no allow-same-origin (opaque origin, cannot reach cookies or the BFF), which is the correct baseline.

items.approach: Dedicated origin and frame shell first; MCP Apps after F-t3-003 makes MCP callable; artifact bridge with viewer-billed completions later.
dependencies: ADR: user-content origin and viewer-bound connectors
items.planeOwner: Frontend Plane (frame, origin) with Model Plane (MCP host, gate) and Application Plane (storage) and Control Plane (viewer identity)
items.risks: Connectors called from a shared artifact must run with the viewer's own credentials, never the author's; a new origin is a new attack surface; ADR needed.

verevon.exactGap: No MCP Apps, elicitation or artifact host bridge exists: an absence grep for ui://, resourceUri, ext-apps, elicitation/create and sampling/createMessage across Model Plane Rust and Go, the frontend and the gateway returned nothing, and the MCP client declares empty capabilities and opens a fresh session per call (mcp_jsonrpc.rs:37-39, mcp_http.rs:50-55) with no resources/read. The only substrate is the HTML artifact preview: ArtifactHtmlPreview renders srcdoc with sandbox="allow-scripts" and no allow-same-origin under a CSP of default-src none, connect-src none and inline scripts only (ChatArtifactPanel.tsx:512-523, sandbox-html.ts:10-30); no postMessage handler or dedicated origin exists. The "elicitation" in tool_loop.rs:652 is prompt guidance for missing tool arguments, not MCP forms.
reuse: ArtifactHtmlPreview and sandboxHtmlDocument (opaque-origin srcdoc iframe plus CSP) as the frame
model-gateway artifacts.rs (artifact ids, versions and SSE events)
mcp_http.rs and mcp_jsonrpc.rs client, to be extended with client capabilities and resources/read
mcp_call and mcp_catalog staged tools (already callable in the tool loop) and the approval/HITL card path for elicitation
F-t3-044 sandboxed widget and host-validated prompt bridge, to avoid building the bridge twice
verevon.constraints: Every app-initiated tools/call must pass the capability gate and org MCP allow-list and be attributed to the viewing user, never the artifact author. ZDR: no artifact persistence and no viewer key-value store under ZDR. A new user-content origin is a new attack surface and needs an ADR. The MCP client currently opens one short session per call, so server-initiated elicitation must be handled inside the tools/call SSE stream and routed into the existing human-approval pause. The preview CSP blocks remote scripts and connections, so a per-app CSP from declared metadata would have to be built and org-restricted.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Do not make the dedicated user-content origin a prerequisite. The existing opaque-origin srcdoc frame can host a postMessage bridge that authenticates by event.source equal to iframe.contentWindow; a separate-origin frame shell is needed only if apps require same-origin web APIs, SRI-loaded libraries or shareable URLs, which is an ADR decision (inference, medium confidence). Merge the artifact host bridge with F-t3-044 and split elicitation (MCP client plus HITL card, smaller) from MCP Apps. The dependency note that F-t3-003 "makes MCP callable" is inaccurate: MCP tools are already callable through mcp_call; F-t3-003 supplies side-effect classes and the signed gate.
verevon.effortNote: Holds for elicitation plus MCP Apps on the existing sandboxed frame; the dedicated origin, viewer-bound connectors and viewer key-value store push it to XL and should be a separate later item.
verevon.verdictReason: The capability is genuinely absent, but the dedicated origin is not required for a first bridge and the bridge overlaps F-t3-044; reword to MCP elicitation and MCP Apps on the existing sandbox, with origin and viewer storage deferred.

items.title: Sharing, replay, export and import: governed snapshot links, org-only default, and conversation export and import
items.summary: Add a session-core snapshot entity (owner, visibility org or named people, created_from_message) whose grants are checked through Control Plane and audited, with public links only behind admin policy and refused for ZDR threads and threads that used private connectors unless redacted. Viewers read it read-only and a follow-up creates a fork under the viewer; a replay view is built from the durable run event log. In parallel add an owner-only audited whole-conversation export and an importer that maps ChatGPT and Claude export JSON into origin=import threads.
items.whyItMatters: Teams share answers and agent runs constantly and org-only sharing is expected in B2B (8 of 12 sources). A replay of an agent run is also a strong trust and transparency artefact. Importing history lowers switching cost, and reports must leave Verevon as Office files and PDFs.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Manus (SRC) for visibility, roles, replay and admin policy; claude.ai and Perplexity (DOC) for snapshot hygiene and fork-on-follow-up; Manus (SRC) and Claude desktop (SRC) for conversion and import
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 8 of 12 for sharing (table-stakes); 6 of 12 for export and import (common)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Share is an immutable snapshot of the thread up to a message (artifacts included, raw tool and connector payloads and files excluded unless in-org) with a visibility enum and an audit entry. Viewers load read-only, a follow-up forks under the viewer, replay plays recorded steps with a countdown and skip-to-result, and admin policy can disable public or replay sharing (strictest wins). Export uses server-side conversion jobs with PENDING, CONVERTING, SUCCESS and FAILED states, session export as a zip (rate-limited, policy-gated), and importers that enumerate sources and can remove an import run.

verevonToday.gap: No chat share link exists (status absent; deferred pending the owner's share-model ruling). Export is partly shipped: answers export to Word, Excel and PowerPoint and print-to-PDF in the browser with pure in-browser OOXML builders (no network, good for ZDR), but without images, charts or math, PDF goes through the print dialog, there is no whole-conversation or account export endpoint, and no importer from ChatGPT or Claude exports.

items.approach: session-core: a snapshot entity with a visibility enum and Control Plane grant and audit checks; the viewer follow-up reuses ForkThread from R-t3-01-02. sessions.proto already stores recipient_audience_revision and hash so share, replay and fork can detect a participant-set change. Replay is built from the durable run event log. Client builders stay and gain chart and image embedding (plan H3/H4); add a session-core export (owner-only, audited) and an importer that marks imported turns untrusted. Refuse sharing and import for ZDR threads, and honour admin policy.
items.planeOwner: Model Plane (snapshots, export, import), Control Plane (grants, audit, admin policy)
items.risks: Leakage of connector content, ZDR and residency violations, and legal retention of public snapshots. Imported content may carry prompt injections.

alreadyPlanned.where: Partly: plan I19 read-only share link (deferred to Wave 6, owner-gated, apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/apps/verevon-web/plans/system-audits/CHAT_GAP_CLOSURE_PLAN_2026-10-01.md:271) and I20 copy a chat into a Space (:272); H3 direct PDF and H4 native charts in Office exports (Wave 4); backlog item #22 governed share and replay (apps/Model Plane/docs/verevon_CHAT_PARITY_BACKLOG.md:176); import and whole-conversation export are not planned

verevon.exactGap: Share link is absent: there is no chat share route, gateway shares.rs and user-core grants cover documents only, and user-core's taxonomy lists 'document' as the only ownable type and rejects any other type for a per-user grant, so a snapshot or thread grant needs a new classified type in Control Plane. Replay primitives exist (session-core ReplayThread, gateway GET /v1/threads/:id/events and /v1/runs/:id/events/replay) but are envelope-only or browser-agent projections by deliberate design, so a content-bearing replay needs a new redacted projection, and there is no ForkThread RPC (artifacts.rs fork_thread only forks artifact counters) and no 'import' value in session-core THREAD_ORIGINS. Export is partly shipped (per-answer Word, Excel, PowerPoint and print-to-PDF built in the browser via ChatMessages.tsx exportMenuItems) but there is no whole-conversation export (the DSAR export is Control-Plane-only by its own disclosure) and no ChatGPT or Claude importer.
reuse: session-core ReplayThread and the replay_run_events pattern (GetRun ownership proof first, then filter payloads before they leave the boundary)
sessions.proto recipient_audience_revision and recipient_audience_hash on threads, already documented as the share/replay/fork drift detector
user-core resource_grants facade plus authztaxonomy (extend with a new type) and the gateway shares.rs / ShareDialog pattern
chat-export docx/xlsx/pptx/zip builders and chatThreadHref deep-link helper
session audit outbox pattern (audit_publisher) for an audited export event
plan I19 (read-only share link), I20 (copy chat into a Space), I8 (server-owned branch conversation)
verevon.constraints: Threads are owned by session-core, so the snapshot entity belongs in Model Plane, but grants and admin policy must be Control Plane authority: add a new resource type to user-core's resource_taxonomy.json (the Go embed, the retrieval-engine-rs mirror and the lint script must stay in parity) rather than any Model Plane-local ACL; Space access never widens an owner-plane ACL. ZDR threads have no durable transcript (persistence-free execution) so sharing, replay and export must refuse them, and connector or private-connector content must be redacted or refused. The existing replay routes are deliberately not browser-safe (gateway comment: payloads may carry prompt, provider or connector data), so replay must be a new redacted projection, not a pass-through of the event log. Import needs a new origin value in THREAD_ORIGINS and the DB CHECK constraint, and imported turns must be marked untrusted because they can carry prompt injections.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Drop the claim that the viewer follow-up reuses ForkThread: no such RPC exists, so either land plan I8/I20 first or ship the first release view-only. Build the share as an immutable redacted snapshot copy (OD19 recommends an org-internal sign-in link, 30-day expiry, revocable, redacted text view) rather than a live view of the thread, and do not describe replay as 'built from the durable run event log' because that log is envelope-only today. Split export and import into an owner-only track that needs no share-model ruling.
verevon.effortNote: Bundles a snapshot entity with Control grants and redaction, a new redacted replay projection, whole-conversation export, an importer and a fork dependency. Recommend splitting: share snapshot L (owner-gated by OD19, plan Wave 6 says do not start), export M, import M.
verevon.verdictReason: Share is correctly missing but already planned and owner-gated (I19), the replay premise is wrong as stated (event logs are envelope-only by design), ForkThread does not exist, and export is partly shipped; the item should be split and its dependencies corrected.

items.title: Event-triggered automations: normalised connector events from Ingestion wake budgeted runs, with wake gates, dry runs, blueprints and consent-first suggestions
items.summary: Add trigger records in capability-core (provider event, structured filter plus optional LLM predicate, prompt template, run target, revision, dry-run) subscribed to normalised events that integration-corev2 publishes on NATS, starting budgeted Do runs through the scheduled-run path with wake gates (source-hash, silent sentinel), per-automation notes, blueprints and capped, de-duplicated suggestions.
items.whyItMatters: Event triggers are common (5 of 12): Cursor's automations service and Hermes's wake gates are the references, ChatGPT MCP Events the DOC-level variant. They turn Verevon agents from on-demand into proactive, which is the natural next step after scheduled runs.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Cursor (automations service with event triggers, LLM filtering and dry runs) for triggers; Hermes (source-hash wake gate, silent sentinel, per-job notepad, blueprints, suggestions with a dedup latch and cap of 5) for state and authoring ; ChatGPT MCP Events (web-chatgpt-web-product-044, DOC)
others: Manus (trigger catalog with revisions, dry runs and execution history; AI triage of failed runs)
web ChatGPT (task definitions shared as independent copies)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: R-t3-04-07: event triggers 5 of 12 (common); wake gates 3 of 12; authoring and sharing 3 of 12; proactive suggestions 3 of 12 | R-t3-03-12: 1 of 11 sources; unique (DOC only)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Trigger{source, filter, prompt template, run_target, revision}; The server declares an events capability, the client subscribes with a callback URL and signing secret, the provider posts signed webhooks (Standard Webhooks HMAC, 256 KiB cap), the receiver verifies, batches events and starts a task run in the bound conversation.

evidence: apps/Model Plane/go/services/capability-core/internal/watch (S4.3 Watch primitive, cursor-bearing, authority re-checked at disclosure; only a process-output adapter)
apps/Model Plane/go/services/bridge-core/internal/channel/adapter.go:1-20 (webhook channel adapter, not a trigger system)

apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/features/chat/components/ScheduleDialog.tsx:56 and src/shared/api/schedule-from-chat.ts:21-65 ('Schedule this' dialog and /schedule only: no blueprints, triage or sharing)
verevonToday.gap: R-t3-04-07: No event trigger, filter, run history for triggers, per-automation state or probe, blueprint, failure triage, sharing or suggestion surface; | R-t3-03-12: run_watchers only notifies a user when a run finishes.

items.approach: Ingestion owns provider webhooks and normalisation; Model Plane owns triggers and runs; reuse the unattended contract of F-t3-018.
items.planeOwner: Model Plane (capability-core triggers) with Ingestion Plane (integration-corev2 events)
items.risks: Event storms and cost; unattended authority; prompt injection through event payloads.

verevon.exactGap: No connector-event trigger exists: integration-corev2 publishes verevon.ingestion.integration.webhook_received (server.go:1080) carrying only eventType, webhookEventId and normalizedBy while the payload stays in its own store, and the only consumer found is Application Plane conversation-core; Model Plane has no consumer for it. capability-core has time-based cron_schedules with a per-fire FireAuthorizer, a Watch primitive with a single process_output adapter and an explicit one-resource-one-Space-one-member authority model, and a run-finished notifier, but no trigger records, structured or LLM filters, wake gates, dry runs or blueprints; chat only offers a time-based "Schedule this" dialog. The webhook normaliser derives just an event type, ids and a replay key, so filters would run over raw provider JSON.
evidence: apps/Ingestion Plane/integration-corev2/internal/api/server.go:1050-1100 (publishes webhook_received after storing the payload; data = eventType, webhookEventId, normalizedBy)
apps/Ingestion Plane/integration-corev2/services/webhook-normalizer-rs/src/lib.rs:55-110 (event type from headers or payload fields, default provider.webhook; no semantic event schema)
apps/Ingestion Plane/integration-corev2/internal/events/publisher.go:55-110 (NATS publisher, subject from event type)
apps/Application Plane/conversation-core/conversation-core-go/internal/consumers/webhook_received_consumer.go:1-60 (durable JetStream consumer + FetchWebhookEvent: the reference pattern)

apps/Model Plane/go/services/capability-core/internal/watch/watch.go:1-140 (Watch: one resource, one Space, one member; not a topic subscription; continuous mode unimplemented; process_output only; TrustUnscreened for source payload)
apps/Model Plane/go/services/capability-core/internal/cron/sweeper.go:14-47 (FireIntent with SpaceRef, SubjectID, TemplateDigest; FireAuthorizer: a schedule record is not authority by itself)
apps/Model Plane/go/services/capability-core/internal/runwatch/consumer.go:1-60 (JetStream durable consumer pattern, nats-provisioner binding pitfall)
apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/shared/api/schedule-from-chat.ts:30-47 (createScheduleFromChat: cron expression + goal text only)
apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/apps/gateway/src/domains/run_watchers.rs:1-14 (notify when a run finishes; not a trigger)
apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/apps/gateway/src/domains/mail_task.rs:1-60 (event-to-run pipeline stubbed 503; doc states no unattended precedent outside Space-scoped scheduled-run machinery)
reuse: cron_schedules + Sweeper + FireAuthorizer/FireIntent + cron_fires as the template for a trigger row, per-fire reauthorization and run history
Watch primitive (cursor, dedupe, expiry, trust column, summary bound) as the home of a new connector-event source kind
conversation-core webhook_received consumer (durable JetStream + FetchWebhookEvent by webhookEventId) as the consumption pattern
runwatch / sessionreview JetStream consumers in capability-core for ack and redelivery behaviour
Scheduled-run path (PrepareScheduledRunThread, orchestrator StartScheduledRunActivity) for starting the budgeted Do run
Run budget and org quota machinery (run_budget.rs, org_quota.rs) for the per-automation cap
verevon.constraints: Ingestion owns provider webhooks and normalisation; Model Plane owns triggers and runs; no cross-plane DB access, so the payload must be fetched through integration-corev2 API (as conversation-core does), not read from its tables. Authority: a trigger must be bound to one connection, Space and acting member and reauthorized with a fresh Control decision on every fire, because the Watch primitive deliberately refuses org-wide subscriptions and a stored record is not authority. Event payloads are attacker-influenced untrusted content (prompt injection) and must be classified untrusted before any LLM predicate or run. ZDR must come from policy because there is no user turn, and unattended runs have no precedent outside Space-scoped scheduled runs (mail_task.rs). A new JetStream durable needs a nats-provisioner binding; event storms need rate limits and budgets.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Model a trigger as a new Watch source kind or a cron_schedules-like row keyed by (connection_id, Space, member) that implements FireAuthorizer, not as free-standing org-wide subscriptions in capability-core. Consume webhook_received through a durable JetStream consumer, fetch the payload by webhookEventId, dedupe on it as the fire key, and treat the payload as untrusted_source_payload. State honestly that integration-corev2 publishes only three event types in code (webhook_received, scim_event_received, sync_cancelled; INF by pattern search) and no mail-received event, so useful mail triggers need an Ingestion-side change first.
verevon.effortNote: As written (trigger store, consumer, filters plus LLM predicate, wake gates, dry run, blueprints, suggestions, unattended Space-authority runs, UI) it is XL; trimmed to trigger + consumer + wake gate + budgeted run it is L, with blueprints and suggestions deferred.
verevon.verdictReason: Confirmed absent in code, with a clear existing pattern to build on. Keep, but reshape around the Watch and FireAuthorizer authority model, flag the missing event types, and trim scope.

items.title: Readable long runs: transcript view and density levels, settled-turn folding, a docked plan strip, activity narration, reasoning summaries and find in collapsed content
items.summary: Add a per-user transcript view preference (compact to verbose) applied at turn, group and row level, fold settled turns behind a 'Worked for Xm' row, show tool rows as soon as the name streams, dock a 'Step N/M' plan strip, and emit a fixed localised activity vocabulary with per-action narration templates from capability and integration metadata. Add provider-neutral collapsed reasoning summaries, retained research history and hidden=until-found so collapsed content stays searchable.
items.whyItMatters: Long agent transcripts are where readability decides whether users trust the agent. DeepSeek (density levels), T3 Code (folding), Claude (view modes, recap) and Codex (narration) each solve part of it; Verevon has the raw events and a strong Work panel.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: T3 Code (SRC) for settled-turn folding; Claude desktop (SRC) for view modes, plan pin and recap; Manus (SRC) for the docked Step N/M planner ; DeepSeek (four work-detail levels applied turn, group, row; fixed activity vocabulary; hidden="until-found" for collapsed rows; server-side turn-outline projection so the rail works before history loads) ; codexagent
others: DeepSeek harness (SRC, early tool rows from partial JSON)
Antigravity (SRC, thinking duration and render hints)
web-chatgpt (reasoning summaries and adjustable upfront plan; activity history and sources kept with the report)
web-perplexity (sources read and learnings shown live)
deepseek (per-turn changed-files card from private snapshots)
web-claudeai (edit attribution in artifacts; show-the-query chart metadata)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: R-t3-01-08: 4 of 12 (view modes, common); 3 of 12 each for folding and the plan dock (differentiators) | R-t3-12-09: Density: 3 of 12; turn rail: 3 of 12; find across collapsed content: 2 of 12 (differentiators). | R-t3-10-08: Narration 1 of 12 (unique); reasoning visibility 1 of 12 (unique, DOC only); research history 2 of 12 (differentiator, DOC only); per-turn changes 1 of 12 (unique); attribution and query provenance 1 of 12 each (DOC only)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Folding: derive one fold row per settled turn that keeps the first and terminal assistant messages, measure duration from the triggering user message, never fold a running turn, keep expanded ids in UI state. Each tool maps to a category with preparing, running and closed labels; Codex keeps about 900 localisable templates keyed connector.tool.state (active, completed, withContext, withName, withRecipient) with slots filled from arguments and results, plus a command parser that maps shell to a small set of semantic verbs;

verevonToday.gap: R-t3-01-08: reasoning_delta renders as a collapsible ReasoningTrace and the Work panel shows raw events, plans and todos, and tool cards carry intent, hit count, truncation and diff. | R-t3-12-09: One fixed detail level in the transcript; | R-t3-10-08: Tool presentation derives an intent icon and label but has no per-connector, per-state sentence templates (the verb/object/outcome activity grammar is planned, not built).
