items.title: Enterprise compliance posture: retention windows and legal hold, data-use disclosure, regime tags, sharing policy, telemetry scrub, signed releases
items.summary: Add a Control Plane retention policy per org and surface with a legal-hold flag that a session-core sweeper obeys (dry-run and audited), propagating deletes to Data Plane indexes and derived memory, and finish Temporary chat once ZDR is attested. Show each provider's training and data-use posture in the model picker from capability-core provider metadata, generalise the ZDR feature-gate pattern into org regime tags in the Control-signed posture, design share links with an org-only default, an admin policy key and a ZDR refusal, scrub telemetry through a typed event registry at the OTel exporter, and build and sign a release artifact in CI with SHA-pinned actions and cargo-deny/govulncheck gates.
items.whyItMatters: Enterprises require retention windows and legal hold before deploying chat broadly, and a signed reproducible release is a prerequisite for credible security claims to enterprise buyers. Most pieces reuse designs Verevon already has (ZDR gate matrix, erasure consumers, privacy-tier routing, hash-only security events).

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Claude (policy-driven retention per surface with legal hold and a headless sweep; sticky HIPAA verdict gate; telemetry scrub framework); Cursor (purpose-by-classification privacy matrix); Hermes (SHA-pinned dependencies, release-age check)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: retention 4 of 12, telemetry privacy 5 of 12, release integrity 5 of 12 (common); data-use controls 3 of 12 (differentiator); regime tags and sharing governance 1 of 12 each (unique)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Retention policy per org and surface, a sweep deleting inactive sessions past the window unless on hold, deletions propagating to search indexes and derived memory. Org taints from the server latch a restricted verdict and a gate throws a typed error for listed surfaces. Typed telemetry events with scrubbers per sink. Lockfiles with exact pins, CI actions by SHA, minimum release age, signed artifacts with rollback.

verevonToday.gap: GDPR org and user erasure and Space deletion reconciliation are shipped, and privacy tiers route by residency and contract with ZDR as a non-downgradable claim. Missing or unverified: org-configurable retention windows and legal hold for threads and runs; a user-visible per-provider training and data-use statement; regime tags beyond ZDR and residency; share links (not built, and Space access must never widen an owner-plane ACL); an audit of product analytics and frontend telemetry (only hash-only security events verified); and a signed release candidate with rollback (artifact v3 tooling exists but none has been built; dependency pinning not audited).

items.approach: Control Plane: retention policy schema and legal-hold flag; session-core retention sweeper (extend gdpr.rs and the deletion reconciler) with dry-run, audit and propagation to Data Plane and memory consumers. capability-core provider metadata for the data-use label; regime tags added to the Control-signed org posture and checked with the zdr_features gate pattern. Share links designed in session-core (org-only default, admin policy key, ZDR refusal). Support Plane: typed telemetry event registry scrubbed at the OTel exporter; CI builds and signs the release artifact, pins Actions by SHA and adds dependency gates.
items.planeOwner: Control Plane (retention policy, regime tags); Model Plane (sweeper, provider metadata, share links); Support Plane (telemetry, release pipeline)
items.risks: Accidental mass deletion: dry-run and audit. Do not claim signed releases before a signed candidate with rollback exists. Share links must never widen an owner-plane ACL. Several sub-workstreams are independent and can be sequenced separately, retention and legal hold first.

alreadyPlanned.where: Temporary chat is built but gated by ZDR attestation (Z-40); Model Plane/scripts/release-artifact.sh exists without a signed candidate; an external audit is listed as owner-only and planned

verevon.exactGap: Shipped: org and user GDPR erasure fan-out (session-core gdpr.rs), Space deletion reconciliation, a Control-only Space-scoped legal hold with a hold_ref pointer (user-core spaces.go:410, deletion_authorization.go:25-31), a global env-driven audit and usage retention sweeper (audit-core main.go:93-172), privacy tiers by residency and ZDR contract shown as model badges (privacy-tier.ts), temporary chat via a ZDR body flag (gateway zdr.rs:43), and signed release-artifact v3 tooling with a rollback artifact (scripts/release-artifact.sh) that no CI workflow invokes. Missing: per-org retention windows and a sweeper for threads and runs (org-core Compliance.DataRetentionDays at types.go:66 is a vestigial unused field), an org or thread level legal hold, any training or data-use statement, regime tags beyond ZDR and residency, share links, a typed telemetry registry with scrub (mp-telemetry only wires OTLP), SHA-pinned actions (none of 107 uses lines are SHA-pinned; Model Plane CI has no audit step; govulncheck and cargo-audit run only in quarry-v2-ci.yml), and a CI-built signed candidate.
reuse: Control Space legal-hold shape (Control-only fence carrying an external hold_ref) generalised from Space scope to org or thread scope
session-core gdpr.rs erasure fan-out (verevon.gdpr.erasure.requested) and the Space deletion receipt plus reconciler pattern for propagating deletes to Data Plane and memory
audit-core runRetention loop as the sweeper template
Run retention_class receipt (zdr, persistent, zdr_waived) in session-core migration 0044 to skip ZDR rows and mark waived runs
privacy-tier.ts badges plus capability-core provider metadata for the data-use label
zdr_features.rs typed-refusal gate matrix as the template for regime tags
scripts/release-artifact.sh v3 build/verify/deploy with signed root and rollback artifact
verevon.constraints: Control owns the retention policy and legal hold (identity/orgs/audit); session-core sweeps only its own rows and must propagate to Data Plane indexes and Letta memory through events and receipts, never by cross-plane DB access (gdpr.rs itself notes cost-core is unreachable). A legal hold must outrank the sweeper but interacts with GDPR erasure (Space deletion already has a blocked_legal_hold status), so precedence needs a Control decision. ZDR runs persist no content, so a hold cannot apply to them and the sweeper has nothing to delete; return a typed refusal rather than silence. Share links are authority-bearing: Space access must never widen an owner-plane ACL, ZDR threads must be refused, and the grant belongs in Control rather than only in session-core.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Place the share-link grant in Control (issue and verify, like Space read decisions) with session-core enforcing it, instead of designing it in session-core alone. Reuse the existing Space legal-hold contract rather than adding a new flag shape, and either wire or delete the unused org-core Compliance struct (DataRetentionDays, HIPAACompliant) so there is one retention field. Split the item into independent workstreams: retention window plus org/thread hold with dry-run and audit (L), data-use label (S), regime tags (M), share-link ADR then build (L), typed telemetry registry (M), and release pipeline (M: invoke release-artifact.sh from CI, pin actions by SHA, add cargo-audit/cargo-deny and govulncheck to the Model Plane workflows). Do not claim signed releases until a candidate with rollback has actually been built.
verevon.effortNote: Six sub-workstreams across Control, Model Plane and Support Plane; sequence retention and hold first. Individually S to L.
verevon.verdictReason: Several pieces already exist (Space legal hold, audit retention sweeper, privacy tiers, temporary chat, release-artifact tooling), so the item should be reworded to say exactly which parts are missing and split so retention/hold, share links and the release pipeline can ship independently.

items.title: Loop guard, durable org hooks and universal tool-output handles in both loops
items.summary: (1) A LoopGuard in mp-contracts used by both loops: a rolling window of (tool, args hash, result class) with an escalating reminder at 3, 5 and 8 identical failing calls, a stop with a typed loop_detected end reason, a repetition detector for streamed text (code-fence aware) and bounded retry on empty or length-stopped responses. (2) Persist org and Space hook rules in capability-core and pass hook_context into Do runs, which today receive none; handlers stay declarative rules plus HTTP webhooks (no shell) and hooks may only narrow authority. (3) Generalise ToolResultHandle from MCP results to every built-in tool result above a token threshold (fetch_url, knowledge, provider actions), run-scoped and never stored on ZDR turns.
items.whyItMatters: A stuck run that keeps repeating a failing call wastes tokens and is exactly what users describe as "it keeps doing the same thing". Hooks let org admins enforce policy (for example block mail outside the domain) without code changes, and result handles protect the context window in Do runs that read large documents. All three are small wiring jobs on existing primitives.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Hermes (side-effect-free loop controller for repeat, cycle and no-progress detection with stop gates) for the guard; Cursor (generic and tool-specific pre/post hooks) for hooks; DeepSeek (private spill files with opaque locators inside a shared token budget) for output handles
others: Antigravity (hook JSON contract with step injection)
Codex (command, MCP-tool and agent hook handlers)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: loop hygiene 3 of 12 (differentiator); hooks 3 of 12 (differentiator); output spill 3 of 12 (differentiator)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Guard: rolling window of (tool, args hash, result class); on N identical failing calls or no new information inject an escalating reminder, then stop with a loop reason. Hooks: registry {event, matcher, handler(command|http|prompt), timeout}; pre-hooks return allow|deny|ask plus optional rewritten input and context; durable store with per-org admin rules. Spill: if output exceeds max_inline_tokens store the full text as a run-scoped blob and return {preview_head, marker, preview_tail, handle, size}; a read tool fetches ranges; blobs expire with the run.

grep of apps/Model Plane/rust/services/*.rs for LoopGuard, loop_guard, no_progress, repeated_call: no matches

verevonToday.gap: No repetition, cycle or no-progress detection in either loop. The hook engine is real but its rules are in memory, are not passed to Do runs, have no UI or durable store and cannot rewrite input. Result handles exist only for large MCP results, not for built-in tools.

items.approach: Model Plane. Add LoopGuard to mp-contracts and call it from model-gateway tool_loop.rs and execution-core agent.rs, emitting a typed loop_detected terminal reason. Persist hook rules in capability-core per org and Space, add a hook_context field to RunAgentRequest, and add a settings UI. Generalise ToolResultHandle to every tool result above a threshold in both loops with a ZDR bypass (no handle persisted).
items.planeOwner: Model Plane
items.risks: False positives on legitimate polling (allow-list idempotent poll tools and require identical result class); hooks must never widen authority; ZDR turns must not persist handles; hook webhooks are an egress path and need allow-listing.

verevon.exactGap: Neither loop has repetition, cycle or no-progress detection: only exact duplicate read-only calls are suppressed (tool_loop.rs duplicate_call_signature; agent.rs knowledge_search retrieval_signature), there is no loop_detected end reason, and neither an empty nor a length-stopped model round is retried (an empty stream is detected and reported as inference_stream_error at sse.rs:3347-3385, only a truncated final tool call is refused, and transient tool failures are retried by retry.rs). The hook engine is real but rules live only in the gateway in-memory HookRegistry, are forwarded only on browser and code_interpreter steps, and the agent loop passes an empty hook_context (agent.rs:1923-1927) because RunAgentRequest has no hook field; a session-core hook_configs table exists but nothing reads it. ToolResultHandle already parks oversized built-in Verevon reads in the inline loop (verevon_read_outcome), but not fetch_url, web_search, knowledge_search or provider results; MCP calls are denied in the inline loop, so the premise that handles serve MCP results is stale, and execution-core has no handle store (8,000-character truncation only).
evidence: apps/Model Plane/rust/services/model-gateway/src/tool_loop.rs:40-62 (12 default rounds, ceiling 32) and :2320-2345 (exact-repeat suppression) and :7185-7200 (same-round duplicates)

apps/Model Plane/rust/services/model-gateway/src/sse.rs:3347-3385 (empty assistant stream reported as an error, not retried) and apps/Model Plane/rust/services/model-gateway/src/tool_loop.rs:145-155,6892 (length-stop makes the last tool call truncated and refused)
apps/Model Plane/rust/services/model-gateway/src/tool_loop.rs:2188-2214 and :3805-3841 (handles park built-in Verevon reads; ZDR returns raw output)
apps/Model Plane/rust/services/model-gateway/src/tool_loop.rs:3676-3692 (mcp__ tools denied in the inline loop)
reuse: duplicate_call_signature (model-gateway) and retrieval_signature (execution-core), which already mirror each other and are the natural base for a shared LoopGuard in mp-contracts
retry.rs risky-call classifier (is_risky_call) so loop-guard reminders and retries never replay side effects
Hook engine (hook/mod.rs) and hook_context_json wire format unchanged; only the rule source and the RunAgentRequest plumbing are new
Unused session-core hook_configs schema (or a capability-core table) as the durable store instead of a third schema
ToolResultStore plus unwrap/apply_query for the handle generalisation, shared with the text-page kind of F-t3-054
verevon.constraints: Hooks may only narrow authority: Allow defers to the permission engine and first matching rule wins, so rule order must be validated so an early allow-all cannot mask a later deny; Space or org hook scope must never widen an owner-plane ACL. ZDR: handles are never created under ZDR (tool_loop.rs:3805-3815), so universal handles keep the inline-truncation fallback on ZDR turns and a durable hook store must not persist event content. Hook webhooks are an egress path and need allow-listing. The two loops are separate processes, so a handle store used by the Do loop needs its own process-local store or a shared crate; gateway handle memory is not durable (900 s TTL).
verevon.approachAdjustment: Re-scope part 3: handles already cover built-in Verevon reads in the inline loop; the work is extending them to fetch_url, knowledge_search and provider results and adding a store to execution-core, not generalising from MCP. For part 2, pick one owner for durable rules (the existing session-core hook_configs table or a new capability-core table, since the hook engine doc names capability-core), add a REST and settings route (the frontend gateway has no hooks domain), add hook_context to RunAgentRequest and replace the "" at agent.rs:1927. Ship the LoopGuard (part 1) first and independently; it needs no schema or proto change.
verevon.effortNote: Raised from M because the three parts are independent workstreams: LoopGuard alone is S-M, durable hooks need a store, REST route, UI and a proto field, and universal handles need an execution-core store.
verevon.verdictReason: The LoopGuard gap and the Do-run hook gap are real and absent, but the handle premise is outdated (handles already serve built-in reads and MCP is denied inline) and a dormant hook_configs table and the engine doc change the persistence approach. Reword and split.

items.title: Public, versioned Agent API with origin-tagged runs as the one entry for every surface (SPA, API keys, schedules, mail, later channels)
items.summary: Expose a versioned /v1/agent API on model-gateway (create run, stream, resume, cancel, answer an interaction) behind Control-issued API keys exchanged for audience-bound delegated bearers, generate an SDK from the same contract, and make every run carry an origin and parent id (chat, console, api, schedule, mail, channel, subagent). Route scheduled and mail-triggered runs through the same governed pipeline, and treat future Channel Plane adapters (Teams, Slack) and a thin CLI as clients of this API.
items.whyItMatters: Enterprise customers and internal surfaces (Office add-ins, mail tasks, cron) can reuse the governed Do-mode pipeline instead of re-implementing it, and agents reachable from Teams or Slack raise daily use. Today Model Plane has one real front door, the SPA through the BFF, plus a hollow scheduled path.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Codex (one runtime, many thin surfaces); Manus (everything is a task with an id and URL)
others: Hermes Agent (messaging gateway with about 25 adapters)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: C-001: 6 of 12 (table-stakes). C-037: 3 of 12 (differentiator). C-038: 1 of 12 (unique)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Codex: one Rust binary exposes exec, review, resume and fork by id, queue, sandbox, execpolicy and an app-server daemon, so each surface is a thin client of the same runtime. Manus: a task.* API where chats, API tasks, schedules and sub-tasks are all tasks with a task_url. Hermes: channel adapters are plugins that connect, normalise, authorise, resolve a canonical session key (agent:{ns}:{platform}:{chat_type}:{chat_id}), queue busy sessions and stream replies.

verevonToday.gap: SRC: the gateway already serves a rich /v1 surface (invoke, stream, resume, runs, orchestration, tasks, cron) but only the BFF consumes it; there is no public Agent API, SDK, CLI or OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Threads carry a stored origin and system runs are listed, but a scheduled step is a single no-tool 1,024-token call with a receipt and no result delivery, and the daily-brief route has no SPA caller. auth-core has an optional API-key plugin (API_KEY_ENABLED) and a model-plane token controller that mints audience-bound RS256 bearers, so key-to-bearer exchange is feasible. The Channel Plane is docs-only and bridge-core is scaffolding.

items.approach: (1) Versioned /v1/agent routes in model-gateway that wrap the existing managed-run start, events, resume, cancel, plan-approval and interaction answers, with an OpenAPI spec generated from the Rust types (shares tooling with R-t3-13-07) and a generated SDK. (2) API keys from auth-core exchanged at the edge for audience-bound delegated bearers; the API must never bypass the BFF's bearer minting, ZDR propagation or per-org rate limits. (3) Extend the thread and run origin enum (api, schedule, mail, channel, subagent) and parent run id; run ScheduledRunSupervision through the full governed Do-mode loop with an unattended identity and deliver results to the thread plus notification-core (agent-runtime item R-t3-04-05 owns the loop semantics). (4) Later: stand up the Channel Plane with a Teams then Slack adapter calling this API, with per-channel identity mapping through Control, and a thin CLI.
items.planeOwner: Model Plane (model-gateway); Control Plane for keys; Channel Plane (not yet built) for adapters
items.risks: Widening the edge enlarges attack surface; unattended runs need always-ask or pre-approved plans; channel identity linking and per-platform data residency; the Channel Plane does not exist yet.

verevon.exactGap: SRC: model-gateway already serves the run lifecycle (invoke, stream, resume, cancel, queue, plan-approval, run events, runs list, cron) and an OpenAPI spec with generated TypeScript and Python SDKs exists, but only the BFF consumes it: the BFF authenticates by session cookie only, auth-core's API-key plugin (API_KEY_ENABLED, orpc verifyApiKey) has no consumer that exchanges a key for a model-gateway bearer, and there is no /v1/agent surface, CLI or OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Thread origin is a closed six-value CHECK list (chat, space, agent_run, support, system, mail_task; session-core grpc.rs THREAD_ORIGINS, migrations 0034/0041) with no api/schedule/channel/subagent value, the mail-task pipeline is wired to None in gateway config.rs:269 (every call answers 503), and a scheduled step is one no-tool 1,024-token inference (execution-core grpc.rs:498-531) with no result delivery.
evidence: apps/Model Plane/rust/services/model-gateway/src/http_routes.rs:132-236 (route table: invoke, stream, resume, cancel, queue, runs, plan-approval, events, browser, ai, proxies)

apps/Model Plane/api/generate-sdk.sh:1-30 (openapi-generator TS and Python SDKs already scripted)

apps/Control Plane/auth-core/src/auth/auth.ts:1112-1160 (apiKey plugin, user-keys and org-keys, x-api-key header, rate limit)
