auth-core model-plane-token controller (audience-bound RS256 bearers; interactive retention/ZDR posture resolved at mint)
session-core PrepareUserOwnedThread and USER_OWNED_THREAD_CALLERS seam for unattended user-owned threads
StartScheduledRun / PrepareScheduledRunThread Control-decision machinery and runs.parent_run_id lineage plus runs.metadata.source
BFF normalization (normalized_model_body, apply_org_zdr_posture, inject_persona_instructions, audience token minting, rate_limit.rs)
verevon.constraints: Control Plane owns keys and identity; Model Plane must only ever see audience-bound delegated bearers that carry the retention (ZDR) posture minted by auth-core. SRC: org, Space and persona instruction layers and the org ZDR raise are applied by the BFF (chat/streams.rs:82, shared.rs:95) while model-gateway only reads what the request carries, so a client that calls model-gateway directly skips them. Unattended runs need a system or service owner under Control-signed decisions (the scheduled path already requires a Space decision) and always-ask or pre-approved plans; Space access must never widen an owner-plane ACL; channel adapters belong to the Channel Plane, which is docs-only; API-started browser runs still need broker grants (Model proposes, Quarry executes).
verevon.approachAdjustment: Do not expose /v1/agent directly on model-gateway: host the versioned public surface at the Frontend Plane gateway (or a thin API edge that reuses its normalization and instruction injection) and authenticate API keys there through auth-core verifyApiKey and a delegated-bearer exchange, or first move instruction-layer resolution server-side. Drop 'generate an SDK' as a new step (SDKs are already generated from a hand-written spec) and instead cover the missing routes and generate the spec from route types. Record origin on the run (runs.metadata.source or a column) instead of widening the thread-origin CHECK for each surface; start with api and schedule, and defer channel and CLI until the Channel Plane exists. Split into (1) API-key edge plus facade, (2) governed unattended scheduled loop (owned by the agent-runtime items), (3) mail-task pipeline wiring, (4) channel adapters and CLI.
verevon.effortNote: Unchanged at L for slices 1 to 3 together; channel adapters and CLI are excluded and blocked on a Channel Plane that does not exist. Scaffolding (SDK spec, API-key issuance, origin enum) lowers slice 1 but the BFF-governance placement question adds design work.
verevon.verdictReason: The need is real, but the item misstates the starting point (an OpenAPI spec with generated SDKs and API-key issuance already exist) and places the public surface on model-gateway, which would bypass BFF-owned instruction layers and org ZDR raise; the scheduled and mail paths are hollow and should be named as separate prerequisites.

items.title: Declarative provider registry and bring-your-own connections
items.summary: Turn provider registration from environment configuration into data: a ProviderProfile (wire protocol, base and models URL, auth kind, compat switches, retry and timeout budgets, residency, privacy tier) stored by inference-core, added through a schema-generated admin form, with model discovery that proposes entries without mutating config until saved and an admin overlay (custom model ids, hide, reorder, unverified capability overrides). Then generalise the ChatGPT-subscription pattern into BYO connections held by Integration Core (API key, cloud role or helper command for Bedrock, Vertex, Azure Foundry, or a customer gateway), referenced by opaque connection id, with per-connection routing so a user or org can hold several connections of one provider.
items.whyItMatters: Enterprise and sovereign customers can add their own gateway, on-prem endpoint or cloud tenancy without a Verevon release, and heavy users can bring their own keys. It also covers the local-model need in a form appropriate for a cloud product.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: hermes (hermes-architecture-and-surfaces-091, 41 overridable provider profiles); claude desktop (claude-product-ux-107, claude-runtime-architecture-072 for BYO cloud accounts and helper credentials with TTL)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: registry 5 of 12 (common); BYO 6 of 12 (table-stakes); multi-instance 1 of 12; curation 2 of 12
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: A ProviderProfile dataclass per provider with api mode, auth type, base and models URLs and error classification, overridable by a user profile of the same name; BYO credentials come from key, cloud role or a helper script with TTL and silent refresh, with health probes on save, and platform and customer credentials never fall back to each other. [SRC]

verevonToday.gap: Providers come from environment configuration (INFERENCE_PROVIDER_ORDER plus fixed adapters). Only the user-owned ChatGPT subscription route exists as a connection; there is no admin-defined provider record, compat switches, discovery, add-provider UI, API-key BYOK, customer cloud account or customer gateway. Whether a user or org can hold several connections of one provider, and any per-org model visibility beyond the router-policy table, have no baseline record (unknown).

items.approach: inference-core: provider-profile table with secrets referenced, never stored; discovery calls GET /models; profiles flow into the same fallback chain, privacy-tier gate and metered decorator. Customer-declared profiles default to the lowest privacy tier and no ZDR claim until attested. Integration Core: new credential kinds and short-lived token minting per call; Model Plane receives only an opaque connection id. cost-core: customer-billed flag. Frontend Plane: schema-annotated settings form. Phase 1 registry plus curation, phase 2 BYO.
items.planeOwner: Model Plane (registry) with Integration Core (credentials)
items.risks: Unverified endpoints can claim residency or ZDR they do not have; customer endpoints may log prompts; confusing which account paid (show the connection on the served-by line); wrong capability overrides cause failures (mark unverified and log).

verevon.exactGap: SRC: provider registration is environment-only (inference-core config.rs from_env: INFERENCE_PROVIDER_ORDER plus fixed Anthropic, OpenAI-compatible base URL, Azure OpenAI, Azure Foundry Anthropic, Azure Cohere and ChatGPT-subscription adapters; ZDR attestation is an evidence-bound env block in provider/zdr.rs), and no Bedrock, Vertex, Gemini, Mistral or Ollama adapter exists. The only per-user connection is the ChatGPT-subscription route where Integration Core owns auth, inference-core receives an opaque subscription_connection_id, and a connection-level ZDR assessment runs at connect time; there is no provider-profile table, model discovery, compat switches, admin overlay, API-key BYOK or customer-gateway route. The only DB-backed precedent is the routing-policy JSONB singleton in session-core that inference-core polls (policy_client.rs).
evidence: apps/Model Plane/rust/services/inference-core/src/config.rs:200-335 (from_env: INFERENCE_PROVIDER_ORDER, Azure blocks, ZDR attestation resolution, deny-by-default residency opt-ins)
apps/Model Plane/rust/services/inference-core/src/provider/zdr.rs:1-50 (evidence-bound ZDR attestation with effective and review-by dates)
apps/Model Plane/rust/services/inference-core/src/provider/codex_subscription.rs:1-70 and :100-130 (opaque connection id; no token held)
apps/Model Plane/rust/services/inference-core/src/provider/policy_client.rs:1-60 (routing policy read from session-core, fail-soft)
apps/Model Plane/rust/services/inference-core/src/provider/routing_policy.rs:1-50 (RoutingPolicy schema, default equals compile-time values)
apps/Ingestion Plane/integration-corev2/internal/api/codex_subscription.go:30-140 (connection create with new conn_ id, applyConnectionZDR in the same transaction, audit events)
apps/Model Plane/rust/services/model-gateway/src/http_routes.rs:7603-7642 (list_models passes through inference-core's catalogue with privacy tier and residency)
apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/apps/gateway/src/domains/router_policy.rs:1-40 (admin routing policy, mode to model table only)
reuse: Integration Core connection records and the opaque-connection-id pattern (codex_subscription.rs plus codex_subscription.go) for BYO credentials
Integration Core's applyConnectionZDR capability assessment at connect time
session-core routing-policy singleton and inference-core's poll client as the store and refresh pattern for an admin overlay
provider/zdr.rs evidence-bound attestation instead of a free-form zdr flag
served-by stamp and /v1/models descriptor (privacy_tier, residency) to show which connection served an answer
cost-core metering decorator and the intent-layer fallback chain
verevon.constraints: Model Plane must not store provider secrets: reference an opaque connection id held by Integration Core (existing pattern). A customer-declared provider must default to the lowest privacy tier with no ZDR or residency claim; ZDR today requires an attestation with resource id, approval reference, effective and review-by dates and a digest, and global residency opt-ins are deny-by-default flags, so an admin form must not be able to type 'zdr: true'. Customer-billed routes need cost-core attribution and the served-by line must name the connection. Entitlement ownership between Control and Model Plane is an open decision (ADR dependency).
verevon.approachAdjustment: Phase it differently: (1) an admin overlay over the env-defined providers (hide, reorder, custom model ids), stored in session-core like the routing-policy singleton; (2) one new OpenAI-compatible customer-gateway profile with a secret reference and lowest privacy tier; (3) cloud-role BYO (Bedrock, Vertex, Foundry) last. Do not start with a generic registry that replaces env wiring: ZDR and residency attestation and provider-specific adapters (the Anthropic cache planner, Azure deployment names) cannot be expressed as compat switches. Schema-generated admin form is optional polish.
verevon.effortNote: Unchanged for the full registry plus BYO; phase 1 overlay alone is M.
verevon.verdictReason: The capability is genuinely absent beyond the single subscription connection, so it stays, but the approach should start from an overlay on existing providers and preserve evidence-bound ZDR and residency rather than introduce a generic registry.

items.title: UI quality gates: remove Norwegian-only controls and enforce i18n and design tokens in CI
items.summary: Route the remaining Norwegian-only strings (approval buttons, plan rung labels, tool status words, trace copy) through i18n.tr, then add CI gates so they cannot come back: an ESLint rule against bare string literals in JSX under features/chat and features/agents, a dictionary-parity test, and a raw-colour ban outside tokens for new files. Write the per-surface state checklist (empty, loading, reconnecting, degraded, exhausted, error) into the design doc, and move toward namespace catalogs instead of inline tr(no, en) pairs so a third locale is feasible.
items.whyItMatters: Language leaks in the most important controls (approvals) are visible to every English user and to screen readers. A fast-growing SolidJS UI with a roughly 16k-line global.css needs automated guards to stay consistent across chat, agents and Spaces, and the Nordic market makes a clean Norwegian, English and later Swedish or Danish setup a real differentiator.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: DeepSeek (typed dictionaries, a gate against hard-coded copy, a parity test; semantic-token specs) plus Hermes Agent (layered locale packs, 34 KB DESIGN.md with a state checklist)
others: Claude desktop (34k ICU strings in 11 locales)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: i18n: 7 of 12 (table-stakes); design contract and token enforcement: 4 of 12 (common).
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Message keys in typed catalogs per feature namespace with ICU plural/select; a CI script fails on string literals in JSX outside the i18n call; a parity test asserts every key exists in every locale; typed failure causes select localised guidance. Tokens in three layers (scale, semantic alias, component) with a lint gate rejecting raw colours and literal spacing in feature code, one primitives catalog, and motion tokens with reduced-motion fallbacks.

verevonToday.gap: Norwegian and English are handled with inline i18n.tr(no, en) pairs, and several controls are Norwegian-only (the Godkjenn and Avvis approval buttons were verified as bare literals); there is no gate or parity test and only two locales. eslint.config.js (116 lines) has a no-restricted-syntax block (a fabricated-security-posture rule) but no raw-colour or JSX-string rule that I found; a single primitives catalog was not located. The design spec is marked stale against code.

items.approach: Frontend Plane: fix the leaks first. Then extend the existing no-restricted-syntax array in eslint.config.js (a second key would replace the existing A8 rule, per the comment in that file) with a JSX bare-literal selector scoped to features/chat and features/agents, add a Vitest parity test over the dictionaries, and add a stylelint or ESLint raw-colour rule for new files only (legacy global.css is too large for a big-bang gate). Add the state checklist and motion tokens to the design doc. Introduce namespace catalogs gradually, starting with approvals and tool status.
items.planeOwner: Frontend Plane
items.risks: Gate noise on legacy CSS and inline pairs, so scope new rules to new or touched files. Inline tr(no, en) pairs make a third locale costly until migrated. Needs verification of the token-gate half (check for an existing primitives kit under src/shared/ui).

verevon.exactGap: Confirmed bare or single-language literals in the most important controls: Godkjenn and Avvis approval buttons (ChatMessages.tsx:1917,1924), plan approve button (2523), rung labels (2538-2542), Tenker (3672), Last ned (ChatArtifactPanel.tsx:397,581), Stopp svar (ChatPage.tsx:947), run receipt labels and effect names (ChatPanels.tsx:1285-1306) and English-only Pause fleet (FleetRunConsole.tsx:155), while roughly 984 other strings in chat and agents use i18n.tr. eslint.config.js has one no-restricted-syntax array (fabricated-posture plus web-speech selectors, lines 93-108) and no JSX-literal or raw-colour rule, and no stylelint exists. The dictionaries en.ts and no.ts are about 40 lines each and en.ts documents inline tr(no, en) as the preferred pattern, so a parity test and namespace catalogs would add little.
reuse: eslint.config.js no-restricted-syntax array and the existing pnpm verify step that CI already runs (verevonv3-ci.yml)
useI18n().tr(no, en) pairs already used about 984 times in chat and agents
The AgentRunConsole approve control, which already uses an i18n.tr pair, as the model for the fix
shared/ui primitives (Button, Badge, MetricCard) and shared/ui/verevon (20 files)
node:test contract-test pattern in apps/gateway/scripts/*.test.mjs for repo-level text gates
verevon.constraints: Frontend Plane only; no plane, ZDR or Space-authority conflict. The one engineering constraint is ESLint flat config: a second block that matches the same files and sets no-restricted-syntax replaces the first, as the comment at eslint.config.js:104-105 warns.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Fix the roughly 15 to 20 leaking sites first. Then add JSXText and JSXAttribute (title, aria-label, placeholder, alt) literal selectors in a second config block scoped to features/chat and features/agents that re-spreads the existing A8 and web-speech selectors; extending the existing array would apply the rule to all of src. Drop the dictionary-parity test and the namespace-catalog migration: inline tr(no, en) is the documented convention and gives parity at each call site, and en.ts holds one feature. Scope the raw-colour rule to features/chat only (about 1 hex literal) or use a baseline, because features/agents has about 537 hex literals in Chatbot Studio Tailwind classes. apps/verevon-web/DESIGN.md is the marketing-site spec, so the state checklist needs its own document. global.css is about 49k lines with about 389 custom properties, not 16k.
verevon.effortNote: Lowered from M: leak fixes plus one or two lint selectors plus a short checklist doc; the parity test and catalog migration are dropped.
verevon.verdictReason: The leaks are real and the lint gate is absent, but the parity test and namespace-catalog parts contradict the documented inline-pair convention and have little to check, and the raw-colour gate needs scoping; reword to a small leak-fix plus JSX-literal gate.

items.title: Contract and architecture guardrails in CI: generated SPA types from Rust, plane-boundary and logging gates, and a size ratchet
items.summary: Generate TypeScript types for SSE payloads and BFF JSON from the Rust contracts (ts-rs or schemars into json-schema-to-ts, or from proto) with a CI diff failure, and add a test-mode payload validator in the SPA stream client that rejects unknown keys. Add syntax-aware fitness gates: no cross-plane DB access, no raw user content in logs, and a baselined file and function size ratchet whose enforcement level is read from the base branch.
items.whyItMatters: It removes the recurring class of bug where the backend emits an event the SPA silently drops, and it turns the plane-ownership and ZDR rules, which are enforced today by review and by docs that go stale, into durable checks that still hold when AI agents write most of the code.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Hermes Agent (schema codegen); DeepSeek harness (AST fitness gates)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: C-007: 4 of 12 (common). C-046: 3 of 12 (differentiator)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Hermes: one Pydantic model per method, server request and event; a generator renders TypeScript types and an OpenRPC document; extra keys are rejected and test isolation raises ContractViolation on a mismatched payload. DeepSeek: AST-based repository checks that cannot be dodged by renamed imports, with SHA-256 baselines for retiring legacy violations; Hermes reads the ratchet level from main so a PR cannot relax its own check.

verevonToday.gap: SRC: CI guards SSE event-name taxonomy freshness, vendored contract goldens with sha256 pins, buf breaking changes, a resource-taxonomy lint and secret scanning. Not found: generated SPA payload types (chat-client.ts is hand-written; no ts-rs, specta, schemars or utoipa in the verevonv3 manifests), an automated check of the no-cross-plane-DB-access rule, a complexity ratchet (agent.rs is 13,521 lines, sse.rs 13,325 and http_routes.rs 11,681) or a stale-doc gate; the Model Plane CI job runs fmt, check and tests only.

items.approach: Types: derive schemars or ts-rs on the SSE event and BFF DTO structs in model-gateway and the verevonv3 gateway, emit committed .ts files under src/shared/api/generated, fail CI on diff, and add an assert-on-unknown-keys validator used in tests and dev builds of the SSE parser. Fitness: add a syn and go/ast based job that scans each service's DB URLs and migrations for foreign schemas, a lint gate that forbids logging prompt, message and tool-result fields (pairs with R-t3-13-09), a file and function size ratchet baselined by hash with the level read from the base branch, and a doc-freshness check tied to STALE_DOC_DELETION_REGISTER.md. This ratchet is also the answer to the oversized loop functions; do not add a contributor-registry abstraction for a single implementation (ledger.md:1358 rule).
items.planeOwner: Frontend Plane (types) and Support Plane (CI gates)
items.risks: Codegen churn in a fast-moving SPA and the BFF reshaping layer must also be covered; false positives slow development, so baseline existing violations.

verevon.exactGap: The item treats these guarantees as enforced only by review, but event-name coverage between sse_events.rs and chat-client.ts is already a CI gate (sse-taxonomy.yml running gen-sse-event-taxonomy.py --check, with a step proving the check can fail), contract goldens are sha256-pinned, buf lint/breaking runs, the gateway runs clippy -D warnings, and the SPA has AST-level no-restricted-syntax rules plus a grep-based fabrication-guard job (SRC). What is missing is payload-field-level contract types (ChatEvent::payload() builds json! by hand at sse_events.rs:490 and chat-client.ts is hand-written; no ts-rs/schemars/utoipa/specta in any Cargo.toml or package.json under apps), any automated no-cross-plane-DB or no-raw-content-in-logs gate, any size ratchet (agent.rs 13,521, sse.rs 13,325, http_routes.rs 11,681 lines by wc -l) and any Model Plane clippy (deliberately omitted, 304 pedantic warnings). A stale-doc gate exists only for the SSE taxonomy doc.
reuse: gen-sse-event-taxonomy.py --check plus the drift self-test step in sse-taxonomy.yml: extend from event names to payload keys instead of building a new generator
zdr-contract-sync.test.sh with --self-test and scripts/tests/*.test.mjs hermetic parity tests as the pattern for new fitness gates
ChatEvent::payload() match arms in sse_events.rs as the single source of field names
eslint no-restricted-syntax block in verevonv3/eslint.config.js for SPA-side syntactic rules
auth-core lint-ratchet.mjs with a reviewed baseline as the ratchet precedent
buf generate with protoc-gen-es for proto-backed contracts (currently pointed at the legacy verevon app, so re-point rather than add a tool)
verevon.constraints: Gates must stay hermetic (no live DB, no env values printed) like the existing scripts/tests. CI gates are repo-root .github/workflows and scripts/ owned by no plane, so naming Support Plane as owner is wrong (Support Plane is the RustDesk hbbs/hbbr backend per CLAUDE.md). The gateway reshapes BFF JSON, so SSE passthrough payloads and BFF DTOs are two separate contracts. The no-cross-plane-DB rule must be a static scan of compose DATABASE_URLs and migrations, not a runtime check.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Split into three. (1) Payload keys: ChatEvent::payload() is hand-built json!, so a ts-rs/schemars derive does not apply; either extend gen-sse-event-taxonomy.py to extract per-event field lists from the payload() arms and compare with chat-client.ts reads, or first convert payloads to serde structs, and add the unknown-key validator only in tests. (2) Hermetic syntactic gates modelled on scripts/tests with a self-test proving they fail: cross-plane DB scan first, log-content rule second. (3) Size ratchet last, baselined by hash like auth-core lint-ratchet; reading the level from the base branch needs a fetch step the current workflows do not have. Also verify buf.yml: it passes the unquoted path "apps/Model Plane/proto" (contains a space) to buf, so the job may not be checking what it appears to check (INF).
verevon.effortNote: Unchanged as a bundle, but the first slice (payload-key check extending the existing SSE gate) is S to M because the name-level gate, the parser and the CI wiring already exist.
verevon.verdictReason: Half of the stated benefit (backend event silently dropped by the SPA) is already guarded at event-name level; the item should say so, drop the derive approach that does not fit hand-built payloads, and fix the owner. The cross-plane DB, log and size gates are genuinely absent.

items.title: Policy and data-flow transparency: effective-policy origin view and declared egress catalogue
items.summary: Show the effective value of approval posture, ZDR, privacy tier, model routing and budgets for a Space or thread together with the layer that set it (org, workspace, Space, user, server default). Declare every outbound destination once per plane (destination, data classes, owning feature, ZDR behaviour, toggle) in an egress catalogue that drives the gateway CSP, a generated Trust Center 'what leaves the platform' table and a CI check that fails on undeclared hosts.
items.whyItMatters: Verevon's privacy positioning rests on ZDR, residency and one-way-tightening policy, but users and admins cannot see why a setting has its value or exactly which providers receive which data. This makes the authority model auditable and cheap to explain to buyers.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: claude
others: deepseek (--dump-config shows each field's origin and which layers patched it, warns when a patch matches nothing; plugin inventory with live phase)
web-chatgpt (what goes to search and app partners)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: Data-flow and egress disclosure 4 of 12 (common); effective configuration provenance 3 of 12 (differentiator)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Claude uses one declarative catalogue listing each destination with its disabling policy toggle, the process that contacts it, the required CSP directive and redirects; it generates the CSP, firewall allow-lists, admin toggles and local 503 fallbacks. DeepSeek applies configuration layers cumulatively, snapshots after each and compares per field to attribute origin and patchedBy.

verevonToday.gap: SRC: per-answer served-by provenance (provider, residency, strongest substantiated privacy tier), server-resolved one-way-tightening posture, a router-policy admin and a Trust Center with connected-app permissions, retention and workspace AI activity all exist. Missing: a view of effective policy values with their originating layer, a single declared egress catalogue per plane, a generated disclosure of what is sent to LLM providers, Quarry targets and integration providers, and any telemetry consent switch (SPA grep).

items.approach: Model Plane profile resolver returns {field, value, origin, patched_by[]} for posture, ZDR, privacy tier, routing and budgets (hiding other tenants' and admin-only details from members); Frontend Settings gets an 'Effective policy' panel per Space and thread. Support Plane tooling: egress.yaml per plane generating gateway CSP and a Trust Center disclosure table, plus a CI check against outbound client hosts; Control Plane exposes the org toggles. Reuse the approval cause taxonomy (R-t3-10-01) for the 'why' wording.
items.planeOwner: Model Plane (profile resolver) with Support Plane (egress catalogue tooling), Control Plane (org toggles) and Frontend Plane (Trust Center)
items.risks: Catalogue drift unless CI enforces it; the view must not reveal other tenants' or admin-only policy details; a disclosure page is a public claim, so it must be generated from the catalogue and not hand-edited.

verevon.exactGap: SRC: per-answer served-by provenance (SSE usage frame; session-only in the SPA), BFF and Model one-way ratchets for ZDR, privacy tier, approval posture and budgets, an admin router-policy read of the live routing policy, a context inspector whose segment kinds include policy, workspace and persona, and a Trust Center for connected apps and AI activity all exist. Missing: any view that shows an effective value with the layer that set it, any declared egress catalogue (the only CSP is nginx.conf:70 with connect-src 'self' https:, which governs the browser, not plane-to-provider traffic), and a generated 'what leaves the platform' disclosure or CI check for undeclared hosts.
evidence: apps/Model Plane/rust/services/model-gateway/src/profile.rs:1-110 (approval posture resolution: server floor from JWT scopes, client may only ratchet stricter)
apps/Model Plane/rust/services/model-gateway/src/sse_events.rs:15-60 and :262-296 (ServedBy stamp on the usage frame)
apps/Model Plane/rust/services/model-gateway/src/budget.rs:300-315 (tests: caller may tighten own budget, org ceiling still applies)
apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/apps/gateway/src/zdr.rs:1-50 (org ZDR read from org-core, OR-ed with request)
apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/apps/gateway/src/domains/router_policy.rs:1-40 (GET returns inference-core effective routing policy)
apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/features/settings/components/TrustCenterSection.tsx:26-60 and :170-210 (connected-app transparency, workspace AI activity)
apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/features/chat/components/ChatPanels.tsx:575-640 (context segment kinds incl. policy, workspace, persona)
apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/nginx.conf:66-71 (the SPA CSP lives at nginx; connect-src 'self' https:)
apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/apps/gateway/src/main.rs:150-157 (gateway sets only nosniff and referrer policy; CSP is at nginx)
apps/Control Plane/user-core/internal/spaces/repository.go:1210-1225 (Control-owned effect policy floor, fences Spaces on change)
apps/Support Plane/README.md:1-20 (Support Plane is the RustDesk relay stack, not build tooling)
reuse: ServedBy stamp and processing note for the per-answer 'who processed this' line
Context inspector segment kinds (policy, workspace, persona, agent) as the instruction-layer 'why'
router-policy GET as the routing leg of the effective-policy view
WorkspaceSettingsPage ZDR attestation check and TrustCenterSection as the host surfaces
provider/zdr.rs attestation fields (resource, approval ref, effective and review dates) for the disclosure
scripts/coresystem-conformance.sh and the cross-plane preflight as the home for a CI check
verevon.constraints: No cross-plane DB access: org ZDR lives in org-core (read by the BFF), Space effect policy in Control user-core, instruction layers in Convex via the BFF, routing in inference-core, budgets in model-gateway/cost-core, and the approval-posture floor comes from JWT scopes in model-gateway profile.rs, so no single Model Plane resolver can see every layer. Each owner plane must expose its own {value, origin} and the BFF aggregates. Members must not see admin-only or other-tenant policy; Space access never widens an owner-plane ACL. The egress catalogue is a public claim and must be generated and CI-checked, never hand-edited. Support Plane hosts the RustDesk relay and is not tooling.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Put the aggregation at the Frontend Plane BFF (a read-only effective-policy route that asks each owner plane for its own resolved fields; Model Plane returns only approval posture and floor, privacy-tier floor, routing and budgets). Put the egress catalogue and its CI check in repo-level scripts next to coresystem-conformance.sh with per-plane declaration files, not in Support Plane. Treat browser CSP as a separate small tightening (nginx.conf connect-src is currently any https) generated from the browser-facing subset; server-side egress to LLM providers, Quarry targets and integrations is not controlled by CSP at all.
verevon.effortNote: M to L: needs read endpoints in three or four owner planes plus the catalogue, disclosure and CI check. Slice (a) effective-policy panel is M; slice (b) catalogue plus CI is M.
verevon.verdictReason: Transparency pieces already exist for provenance and routing; the genuine gaps are the origin-layer view and the egress catalogue. The item places the resolver in Model Plane and the tooling in Support Plane, both wrong, and assumes CSP covers server egress.

items.title: Rewind with undo preview, read-only side chat and spin-off tasks, built on the message tree
items.summary: Once the server message tree exists, add three tree operations. Rewind moves the active leaf to before an earlier message and restores the artifact version pointer, with a preview and an undo of the rewind. Side chat is an ephemeral child thread seeded with a read-only snapshot of the parent's context, with inline read-only tools only, usable while the run continues. Spin-off lets the assistant propose a draft thread chip with a seeded prompt that the user must accept.
items.whyItMatters: Rewind is a differentiator for safe experimentation in Do mode, side chat (6 of 12 sources) lets users ask 'why did it do X?' mid-run without redirecting the run, which serves the transparency goal, and spin-off keeps threads focused. All three are cheap once forks exist.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Claude desktop (SRC) for rewind and spin-off; Claude desktop plus Codex (SRC) for side chat, with Codex's ephemeral read-only fork as the safest model
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 6 of 12 (side chat, common), 2 of 12 each (rewind, spin-off; differentiators)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Rewind: a checkpoint per user turn (conversation cursor plus artifact version ids); rewinding moves the cursor, restores versions and keeps the rewound tail recoverable until a new message is sent; a preview lists the per-artifact diffs that would be undone and warns about external effects. Side chat: an ephemeral child session seeded with a read-only snapshot of parent context, no effectful tools and no user prompts, not appended to the main transcript, stoppable independently, discarded or merged back as one message. Spin-off: a plan scope value or spawn_task tool creates a backlog chip with a self-contained prompt.

verevonToday.gap: Run checkpoints exist (SaveCheckpoint, auto-checkpoint compaction) but there is no user-facing rewind or restore. A grep for side chat in the chat feature found no hits, so there is no side-chat surface or ephemeral fork primitive. There is no user-facing spin-off or backlog; the nearest thing is wide-research fan-out inside Do runs.

items.approach: Rewind: move the active leaf of the R-t3-01-02 tree plus an artifact version pointer; scope per OD19 is conversation and artifact versions only, and effectful turns are marked non-rewindable with an explicit preview. Side chat: a model-gateway ephemeral invocation using the parent thread's assembled context snapshot (GetContextAssembly exists), the inline_tool_allowed read-only tool gate, no persistence under ZDR and an origin=side tag otherwise; SPA resizable side pane. Spin-off last: a spawn_task builtin that creates a draft thread in session-core.
items.planeOwner: Model Plane (tree operations, ephemeral invocation), Frontend Plane (side pane, rewind preview)
items.risks: Users may assume rewind reverts external effects (emails, tickets), so the preview must be explicit. A second context costs tokens and must carry the parent's ACL and ZDR posture. Spin-off must never auto-start effectful work.

alreadyPlanned.where: Partly: plan I11 checkpoint and rewind with non-rewindable marking (apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/apps/verevon-web/plans/system-audits/CHAT_GAP_CLOSURE_PLAN_2026-10-01.md:252, owner decision OD19); side chat and spin-off are not in the plan

verevon.exactGap: No rewind, side chat or spin-off exists in code: messages are a linear table with a sequence identity and no parent pointer (session-core 0001_init.sql:14-24), InvokeRequest.parent_message_id (gateway.proto:250) has no handler, checkpoints are run step watermarks (compaction.rs:1-12, save_checkpoint) with no restore RPC, and regenerate and edit versions are client-only (chat-versions.ts:1-12). Rewind is already planned as I10 then I11 in CHAT_GAP_CLOSURE_PLAN (lines 236, 252) with the owner recommendation of conversation plus artifact versions and effectful turns non-rewindable (OD19, line 509); side chat and spin-off appear in no plan, and today a message sent mid-run is queued into the running agent (QueuedInputStrip) instead of being answered separately.
reuse: CHAT_GAP_CLOSURE_PLAN I10 and I11 plus the OD19 rewind ruling (reference them, do not re-specify)
session-core GetContextAssembly for the parent's context, noting it re-assembles memory and retrieval rather than snapshotting the exact prompt that was sent
model-gateway builtin_tool_defs as the catalogue for an explicit read-only allowlist
threads.origin and its CHECK constraint for tagging a persisted side thread
ArtifactVersionStore::fork_thread as a pattern for a read-only artifact snapshot
the plan.propose draft pattern for a spin-off chip
verevon.constraints: ZDR: a side chat under a ZDR parent must not persist; threads.origin allows only chat, space, agent_run, support and system, so a persisted 'side' thread needs a migration, while an unpersisted ephemeral invocation avoids both problems. Space authority: a side chat inherits the parent's Space read decision and audience context and must never widen them. inline_tool_allowed is a denylist (save_memory, browser_agent, mcp tools) and still admits create_artifact, update_artifact, code_interpreter and reattach_skill, so it cannot serve as the read-only gate the item assumes. Rewind cannot undo provider writes or sandbox effects, so effectful turns stay non-rewindable per OD19; spin-off may only create a draft chip that a person accepts, never start effectful work.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Remove rewind from this item and reference I10 and I11 (planned, M, dependent on the server message tree). Keep side chat as the new recommendation, implemented in model-gateway as an ephemeral invocation with an explicit read-only tool allowlist (for example web_search, fetch_url, knowledge_search and its siblings, read_artifact, count_words, result_query) over a snapshot of the parent thread, with no persistence under ZDR; build spin-off last as a plan-gate-style draft chip.
verevon.effortNote: Rewind (M) is already in the plan; the remaining side chat (M) plus spin-off (S to M) is M overall.
verevon.verdictReason: All three are absent in code, but rewind is already planned and should be referenced rather than re-recommended; side chat is a genuine gap but its approach reuses an inline tool gate that is not read-only.

items.title: Tool efficiency at scale: a deferred tool index, typed tool outputs, code mode through a gated sandbox bridge, background jobs and WebMCP page tools
items.summary: Extend the mcp_catalog/mcp_call staged-disclosure pattern into one deferred tool index over built-ins, provider actions and MCP tools; add optional typed output schemas; then let sandboxed code call Verevon tools as async functions where every call re-enters capability-core EvaluatePolicy, with per-cell limits; add background jobs with await and notify, and later WebMCP site tools proposed by the Model and executed by Quarry.
items.whyItMatters: Codex, Hermes, Manus and DeepSeek use code mode or tool search to cut round trips and context; Verevon's built-in catalogue is unbounded (about 16k characters). Valuable, but it should follow MCP enablement and the sandbox computer.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Hermes (tool_search / tool_describe / tool_call bridge with core tools never deferred, BM25 gated on the query's rarest token and a coverage floor; SRC) for the index; Codex (JavaScript in a V8 isolate with injected async tools and bounded output; SRC) with DeepSeek PTC (every sub-call re-enters the full guarded pipeline; SRC) for code mode; DeepSeek (validated, frozen tool outputs rendered purely) for the output contract ; Codex (model-written JS in a fresh V8 isolate with tools as async functions) and Manus (per-cell budgets and resumable state) for code mode; Cursor (background commands with output-pattern notifications; tee on the model stream dispatching completed tool calls) for jobs and early dispatch ; Manus and DeepSeek for code mode (QuickJS-WASM with no fs or network; a host-child protocol with declared bindings, resource ceilings and an eight-way typed failure taxonomy); Antigravity for WebMCP
others: Cursor (MCP descriptors as files; spills results over 40 KB to files)
DeepSeek (jobs scoped to the starting agent with a wake budget; PTC routes sub-calls through the policy pipeline)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: R-t3-05-11: Tool search 4 of 12, common; code mode 2 of 12, differentiator; tool-result contract 3 of 12, differentiator | R-t3-04-11: code mode 3 of 12 (differentiator); background jobs 4 of 12 (common); streaming dispatch 1 of 12 (unique to Cursor) | R-t3-06-11: 3 of 12 for code mode (differentiator); WebMCP 1 of 12 (unique)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Classify tools as visible (core, direct-only) or deferrable; exec(source) runs in an isolate with no filesystem or network; run_cell{code} starts a fresh confined runtime;

evidence: apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/apps/verevon-web/plans/system-audits/CHAT_PARITY_AUDIT_2026-10-01.md:43 (code mode listed as BKL #11, not built; code_interpreter cannot call Verevon tools)
apps/Model Plane/rust/services/execution-core/src/process_tools.rs:1-8 and process_host.rs:1-8 (process_* tools for Space-scoped runs under a space:processes lease, bwrap isolation)
apps/Model Plane/go/services/capability-core/cmd/main.go:298-376 and internal/watch/watch.go (Watch primitive, process adapter)
verevonToday.gap: R-t3-05-11: MCP staged disclosure (mcp_catalog and mcp_call, threshold 40, ceiling 200) is shipped. | R-t3-04-11: Code mode is not built. | R-t3-06-11: Code mode is recorded as greenfield (sections 23.4 and 23.5 of the Model Plane improvements doc): code_interpreter has no tool-RPC bridge and no network.

items.approach: Deferred index first (resolve the purpose-lock collision recorded in the ledger), code mode (BKL #11) second with DeepSeek's rule that each sub-call passes the full guarded pipeline.
items.planeOwner: Model Plane (model-gateway catalogue, execution-core, sandbox-manager)
items.risks: Code mode can bypass per-call approvals if the bridge is not routed through the gate; deferred tools can hide needed tools from the model.

alreadyPlanned.where: R-t3-05-11: Partly: code mode is scheduled and not built (BKL #11, MODEL_PLANE_IMPROVEMENTS_2026.md section 23.4); the unbounded tool-catalogue budget is a recognised gap that collides with the purpose-lock (decision ledger, Needle entry). | R-t3-04-11: BKL #11 in CHAT_PARITY_AUDIT_2026-10-01.md:43 (code mode), per the cluster evidence | R-t3-06-11: apps/Model Plane/docs/MODEL_PLANE_IMPROVEMENTS_2026.md sections 23.4 and 23.5 (MCP code mode, confirmed greenfield); WebMCP is not planned.

verevon.exactGap: The MCP baseline is overstated: stage_mcp_tool_defs builds the mcp_catalog/mcp_call definitions (threshold 40, ceiling 200), but tool_loop.rs returns an error for both names and every mcp__ call, execution-core has no mcp_call handler, and trusted_capability_id returns None for dynamic MCP names so the signed gate fails closed, so registered MCP tools cannot run. Present: tool-result handles with result_query (inline loop), argument validation in both loops, process_* background processes and the Watch primitive with a process-output adapter. Absent: a deferred index over built-in tools, per-tool output schemas (ToolDefinition has only parameters_json), code mode (greenfield, no tool-RPC bridge), an agent-side wake on job completion, and WebMCP.
reuse: stage_mcp_tool_defs and the 60-second MCP catalogue cache as the staging mechanism once MCP execution is unblocked
tool_result_handles and result_query as the bounded-output and large-result contract (extend to execution-core)
mp_contracts tool_arguments validation as the input half of a typed tool contract
process_* tools, sandbox-manager leases and the capability-core Watch primitive for background jobs
capability-core EvaluatePolicy as the per-call gate every code-mode sub-call must re-enter
Quarry browser grants for any WebMCP-style page tool (the Model proposes, Quarry executes)
verevon.constraints: Both loops refuse MCP execution by design until capability-core provides a durable per-tool binding (F-t3-003), so a deferred index over MCP tools cannot ship first. The decision ledger records that offered_tool_defs() is the purpose-lock allowlist: hiding a tool from the rendered set forbids it, so a deferred index first needs the allowlist decoupled from the rendered set. Code mode must route every sub-call through EvaluatePolicy and approvals, keep the sandbox network-off except the bridge, and keep intermediate data out of persisted history under ZDR. WebMCP page tools must be proposed by the Model and executed or rejected by Quarry, never by a Model Plane browser.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Reorder: (1) MCP enablement via F-t3-003 is the prerequisite, not "shipped"; (2) deferred index only after decoupling the purpose-lock allowlist, starting with description and schema budgeting with degrade-before-drop as the ledger advises; (3) typed outputs as an optional output schema on ToolDefinition, building on result handles; (4) code mode as its own XL item on top of F-t3-009, read-only tools first; (5) agent wake on process completion on the existing Watch primitive; (6) WebMCP last and optional.
verevon.effortNote: Raised from L because the bundle includes greenfield code mode and an MCP execution path that does not run yet; the deferred index and typed outputs alone would be M to L.
verevon.verdictReason: The item is correctly partial and correctly sequenced late, but its premise that MCP staged disclosure is shipped is wrong (definitions only, execution blocked), the purpose-lock constraint is missing, and process_* plus Watch already cover part of the background-job idea.

items.title: Coordinator-mode orchestration on Temporal with typed child results, a fleet panel and gated fan-out
items.summary: Replace the in-memory coordinator and team-worker stub with a coordinator workflow in orchestrator-core (Temporal WideResearch and DeepTask workflows already exist but chat and Do do not use them). The coordinator run has no effect tools, writes a plan, spawns workers through the existing subagent.task (bounded concurrency, shared atomic budget), collects typed results ({status, summary, evidence, next_steps, blocker} through an optional output_schema or structured_output tool), runs a verifier pass and synthesises. Show a fan-out and cost confirmation card above a threshold, add a fleet section to the Work panel fed by child-run events, and add the missing gateway route for /v1/fleets. Later phases: best-of-N fan-out across models with a synthesis step, and model-authored deterministic workflow scripts compiled to Temporal.
items.whyItMatters: Research-heavy and wide tasks are where Manus Wide Research and Perplexity Computer beat single-agent chat, and Verevon already has the hard parts (durable subagent lineage, atomic budgets, Temporal workflows). Without typed child results and a visible, stoppable fleet, parallel work is both invisible and unusable by code that must branch on outcomes.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Cursor (Project mode: non-editing orchestrator with phase gates and a single-writer progress record); Manus (deterministic Workflow Composer with confirmation above about 20 agent calls); T3 Code (task rows, fleet banner with Stop) for the UI
others: DeepSeek (structured_output child tool with a guard)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: orchestration patterns 6 of 12 (common); fleet panel 4 of 12; model-authored workflows 3 of 12; best-of-N 3 of 12; structured child results 2 of 12
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: A coordinator run with no effect tools writes a plan, spawns a worker per item with bounded concurrency, collects structured results, runs a verifier pass and synthesises; progress lives in one single-writer record and a fresh successor coordinator per milestone avoids context rot. Child tasks may declare output_schema; the child concludes by calling structured_output. The UI maps run, child-run and process events to task rows with a banner (3 agents working, Stop all).

evidence: apps/Model Plane/rust/services/model-gateway/src/coordinator.rs:1-25 and 401 (TeamWorkerStore is in-memory by design; coordinator mode is a gRPC stub)
apps/Model Plane/go/services/orchestrator-core/internal/orchestration/workflowreg.go:98-160 and cmd/main.go:146-175 (WideResearch and DeepTask workflows registered but not used by chat or Do)
apps/Model Plane/rust/services/execution-core/src/subagent/mod.rs:1-8 and 29 (durable subagent lineage, atomic budget, leaf restriction: keep)
apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/features/agents/components/FleetRunConsole.tsx:9-35 (calls GET /v1/fleets; a grep of apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/apps/gateway/src found no matching route)
apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/features/chat/components/ChatPanels.tsx:1041 (lineage fetched only for the plan panel)
verevonToday.gap: Coordinator and team mode is an in-memory stub; Temporal orchestration workflows exist but are not wired to chat or Do; the typed subagent handoff report is deferred by decision; the fleet console calls a route that does not exist; chat shows no fleet panel; no best-of-N or model-authored workflow path.

items.approach: Model Plane (orchestrator-core, execution-core subagent, model-gateway) plus Frontend. Build the coordinator as a Temporal workflow reusing subagent.task for workers; add output_schema validated with the existing mp-contracts tool_arguments machinery; expose it as a Do-mode option behind a fan-out and cost confirmation; add the /v1/fleets gateway route and a Work-panel fleet section fed by child-run events. Treat best-of-N and model-authored workflows as follow-ups that need an owner decision on whether model-authored fan-out is wanted.
items.planeOwner: Model Plane (orchestrator-core) with Frontend Plane for the fleet panel
items.risks: Cost blow-up (confirmation above a call-count threshold, shared budget); non-determinism if workflow scripts are model-authored; delegated authority must never widen across children; coordinator effect tools must stay empty.

alreadyPlanned.where: The typed subagent handoff report is deferred by decision until code must branch on outcomes (cluster C-t3-04-036 baseline, status planned); the model-authored workflow question is an open owner decision.

verevon.exactGap: The coordinator-mode TeamCreate, TeamDelete and TeamList RPCs are an in-memory DashMap tracker with no caller (coordinator.rs:1-25, 401; gateway.proto:83), but parallel delegation already ships in-loop: subagent.task and subagent.research_fan_out (research_fan_out.rs) give a shared atomic round pool, a per-run child ceiling, bounded concurrency, per-item ok/failed/refused status with extracted sources, a merged digest, durable lineage with a batch_id, and a fan-out card grid (ChatWideResearchPanel.tsx) in the chat run rail. Missing are validated typed child results (only a free-text result_schema_hint exists), a fan-out and cost confirmation card, fleet-level Stop all and cost in the panel, durable replay of subagent lifecycle events after reload, and any wiring of the Temporal WideResearch and DeepTask workflows (a query-list fan-out through ExecuteStepLoopActivity, not subagent.task) to chat or Do. The '/v1/fleets gateway route' is the wrong target: /v1/fleets and FleetRunConsole belong to Quarry's browser-agent fleets (quarry_fleets table, quarry-edge fleet_routes.rs), not Model Plane subagents.
reuse: subagent.research_fan_out and LoopSubagentDispatch as the worker primitive instead of a new Temporal coordinator
GET /v1/orchestration/threads/:thread_id/lineage and the SubagentAttached/Stopped events for the fleet panel
ChatWideResearchPanel and the ChatLiveRunPanel wideResearch slot as the fleet UI base
the plan.propose plan gate (execution-core plan.rs) and approval cards for the fan-out and cost confirmation
resolve_child_ceiling with the org ceiling and the shared round pool for budget bounds
structured_output_schema on InvokeRequest and InferRequest for provider-enforced typed results
verevon.constraints: ZDR must propagate: DeepTaskWorkflow and WideResearchWorkflow are not marked DeniesZDR (workflowreg.go:120-131) and the WideResearch input stamps only org and user ids (workflowreg.go:369-385), so a ZDR caller could start it and Temporal history would persist queries and results; a Temporal coordinator needs ZDR denial or propagation first. Plane ownership: Quarry fleets stay in the Ingestion Plane, so a Model Plane fleet view must read session-core lineage and run events, not Quarry's /v1/fleets, and the nginx config proxies only /api/ (nginx.conf:74). Delegated authority must not widen: children are blocked from risky tools by the leaf rule and MAX_DEPTH is 1. Unverified (INF, low confidence): whether cancelling the parent run stops in-flight children; I found no cancel check in the agent loop's round loop.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Do not rebuild the coordinator as a Temporal workflow first. Extend the shipped fan-out: add a validated output contract per item (provider-enforced structured_output_schema or a deeper validator, since mp-contracts tool_arguments ignores nested schema constructs), a confirmation card through the existing plan gate above a call-count or cost threshold, Stop all and cost in ChatWideResearchPanel, and persist subagent lifecycle events in session-core so the panel survives reload. Keep the Temporal coordinator, best-of-N and model-authored workflows as owner-decision follow-ups, and do not add a /v1/fleets gateway route for this feature.
verevon.effortNote: The reduced scope (typed results, confirmation card, fleet header with Stop and cost, event replay) is M; the Temporal coordinator plus the ZDR fix, best-of-N and model-authored scripts remain L to XL follow-ups.
verevon.verdictReason: Status is partial rather than stub: in-loop fan-out, lineage and a chat fan-out card grid already ship, and the proposed /v1/fleets route confuses Quarry fleets with Model Plane subagents. Reword to extend the shipped fan-out and drop the Temporal-first framing.

items.title: Resilient routing: failure vocabulary, credential pools, benching, usage-limit and refusal fallbacks, provider health
items.summary: Extend the shipped fallback chain in inference-core with a closed failure code set (auth, quota, rate limit, context too long, server, timeout, refusal, empty response) carrying retry_after, per-route retry policy, pooled deployments or credentials with model-scoped cooldowns, and benching of a failed primary until its declared reset. Add declared fallback models for usage-limit exhaustion with a switch-back at reset_at (opt-in when it crosses from a user subscription to platform billing), a policy-owned refusal fallback that records the original model and is undone on rewind or edit, and a per-provider health map exposed through ListModels so the picker greys unavailable routes with the reason.
items.whyItMatters: Fewer failed answers and stalled agent runs during provider incidents or quota exhaustion, which matters most for unattended scheduled agents and Azure deployment quotas. The subscription route currently stops at its limit with a typed message but no alternative.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: hermes (hermes-architecture-and-surfaces-095, 094 failover and credential pools); codexagent (036 usage-limit fallback and switch-back); claude (112 reversible refusal fallback); t3code (002, 050 provider health snapshot)
others: deepseek (126, 095 closed failure vocabulary and per-route retry modes)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 2 to 3 of 12 per facet; differentiator
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: try_activate_fallback() rebuilds the client in place; cooldowns follow the provider-declared reset (exponential 60 s to 4 h when absent); credential pools rotate on plan-limit 429s before switching provider; limit errors carry reset_at, blocked model and fallback models, and the client announces switches and switch-backs; a model_refusal_fallback message switches the model and remembers the original. [SRC]

verevonToday.gap: A fallback chain with bounded retries and retry-after, typed context overflow, and typed subscription refusals with a reset time exist. Missing: credential pool, reset-aware benching, failover on the subscription route, automatic fallback model and switch-back at limit, org-quota fallback. Refusal-driven rerouting and whether provider health or quota state reaches /v1/models have no baseline record (unknown).

items.approach: inference-core fallback.rs: add the failure enum and per-route retry policy, a cooldown map keyed by (credential, model), benching with reset_at, and reroute events written into the RoutingDecision (R-t3-09-07). Every hop is filtered through the privacy floor, entitlements and cost gates. subscription route: declared fallback models plus a user consent setting for platform billing. Provider health map feeds the model record availability field and the picker. Refusal fallback lists live in RoutingPolicy.
items.planeOwner: Model Plane
items.risks: Failover can silently cross privacy or cost lines (gate and display every hop); falling back from a user subscription to platform billing must be opt-in; stale health data can hide a working route (short-lived cheap probes); safety rerouting must always be disclosed.

alreadyPlanned.where: BKL #25 multi-provider auth-profile failover (docs/verevon_CHAT_PARITY_BACKLOG.md, v-modelplane baseline line 349)

verevon.exactGap: Exists: FallbackChain (fallback.rs) walks providers with per-provider max_retries, ThrottleState (retry-after, TooLong), typed ProviderError::SubscriptionRefused with resets_at, and ZDR/privacy/residency gates before every hop. Missing: a closed failure enum (auth, quota, timeout, server, empty and refusal collapse into Http/Unavailable), any cooldown, benching or credential-pool state, any refusal-driven reroute, and any health or availability field on ModelInfo, /v1/models or the picker. Failover off the subscription route is deliberately forbidden (fallback.rs tests at 2280-2330, rule 17), so the usage-limit fallback and switch-back half contradicts a recorded design choice.
evidence: apps/Model Plane/go/services/capability-core/internal/failover/failover.go:1-148 (shim-only; grep for importers outside tests found none)
reuse: FallbackChain::infer_one_model gate loop (ZDR, privacy tier, residency checks already run before each hop; a bench check slots in at the top of that loop)
ThrottleState and ProviderError::RateLimited/TooLong/SubscriptionRefused as the seed of the failure enum
ModelInfo proto and the /v1/models handler in http_routes.rs (add an availability field there)
The shape of go/.../failover.go (CircuitState, ProviderHealth, RetryPolicy) as a contract to port into Rust; it is unused and in the wrong plane to import
subscription_failure.rs typed reset timing for any user-facing text
RoutingPolicy.cheap_fallback in intent.rs for budget-triggered fallback
turn_timing and provider_used/residency stamps on responses for per-hop provenance
AiModelPicker disabled-with-title pattern for greying a route with its reason
verevon.constraints: Inference-core (Rust) owns the chain; the Go failover package in capability-core is an inert contract and the wrong plane for runtime state. Master ownership matrix rule 17 says enforcers honour a ZDR waiver only for the exact connection named and "never re-route"; fallback.rs tests assert a subscription outage never reaches an API provider and a ZDR turn pinned to the subscription never lands on Azure; the parity audit records "none on the subscription route by design". Every hop must keep passing ZDR, privacy-tier, residency and budget gates, and health probes must carry no user content and be metered. Config registers one key per provider today, so a credential pool has nothing to rotate until multiple keys or deployments per provider exist.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Keep only: a closed failure enum, per-(provider, model) cooldown and benching with reset_at in fallback.rs for API providers, and a health/availability field on ModelInfo surfaced in /v1/models and the picker. Remove the automatic usage-limit fallback and switch-back from the subscription route; if the owner wants continuity, offer an explicit per-turn "continue on a platform model" action with its own consent and ZDR/waiver check, never a silent reroute. Defer credential pools until multi-key config exists, and defer refusal fallback until adapters emit a typed refusal signal.
verevon.effortNote: Original L bundled credential pools, subscription fallback with switch-back and refusal rerouting. The keepable core (failure enum, cooldown/bench, health on ModelInfo and picker) is M.
verevon.verdictReason: The base chain, typed throttling and typed subscription refusals exist, and the rest is absent, so the item stands. But the subscription fallback and switch-back clash with rule 17 and the by-design no-failover decision, and the credential-pool part has no multi-key baseline, so the item must be narrowed.

items.title: Per-step routing decision and model continuity: resolver, lifecycle successors and a reasoning replay envelope
items.summary: Implement the planned step-level RoutingDecision {requested, resolved model, provider, effort, reason, complexity, budget posture} in inference-core, persist it on every run step in Session Core, and surface model and reason in the served-by line with an optional routing-feedback control. Build one resolve_model() with fixed precedence (explicit, thread last step, Space default, user last used, org default, intent default) that chat, Do, scheduled runs and subagents all call; add lifecycle states and successor ids so retired model ids resolve to successors with a model_switched event; insert a notice only when the provider family changes. Capture Anthropic signature and redacted thinking blocks (and later Gemini thought signatures) in a ReplayEnvelope stored with the step and replay them only to the matching adapter and model.
items.whyItMatters: Serves the DeepSeek-style transparency goal, gives the router-policy page real data to tune Budget/Balance/Genius, and protects saved threads, agents and scheduled runs from provider model retirements. Replay is required for correct multi-turn tool use with thinking models and is a blocker for Gemini.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: hermes (097 reasoning replay, 093 single resolver); cursor (073, 108 routed model); codexagent (035 lifecycle and upgrade target); deepseek (094, 134 mid-thread notice)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: replay 4 of 12 (common); routed-model stream 2 of 12, lifecycle 3 of 12, switching semantics 2 of 12, layered defaults 2 of 12 (differentiators)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: reasoning_carriers stores opaque reasoning as typed private records lifted back only for the matching route, with fingerprints of signature-rejected blocks excluded on retry; the agent stream emits routed_model with a display name; the catalogue declares upgrade {model, migration note, retirement_at} and a thread switches automatically after retirement; a durable notice tells the new model earlier turns came from another model. [SRC]

evidence: apps/Model Plane/rust/services/model-gateway/src/sse_events.rs:39-60 (ServedBy carries provider deployment, residency and privacy tier but no resolved model or reason)
apps/Model Plane/rust/services/inference-core/src/config.rs:83 (only a comment about a retired Cohere model name)
verevonToday.gap: Routing is request-level only (step-level RoutingDecision is planned), the served-by line has no model id or reason, signed thinking cannot be replayed, and there is no routing feedback. Lifecycle handling, per-message or per-thread model storage in Session Core, behaviour when a saved model is no longer routable, and a single resolver for chat, Do and scheduled runs have no baseline record (unknown); the Space default does not exist.

items.approach: inference-core: RoutingDecision per call plus a resolve_model(ctx) used by every surface; lifecycle {state, retire_at, successor_id} in the model record (R-t3-09-05). Session Core: extend the step schema with the route and an optional ReplayEnvelope {adapter, model, blocks}; skip persisting envelopes on ZDR turns. model-gateway: routed_model / model_switched SSE events, a small router-feedback endpoint, an org setting to show tier names only; strip replay state and add a notice on family change. Application Plane projection carries the Space default; it can only select among already-entitled models.
items.planeOwner: Model Plane (with Session Core)
items.risks: Reasoning content retention must follow ZDR; automatic successor mapping can change cost or behaviour (record it per run and show it); notices consume tokens and can break caches (insert only on family change); exposing model names may conflict with abstraction choices.

alreadyPlanned.where: Step-level RoutingDecision is planned in docs/MODEL_PLANE_IMPROVEMENTS_2026.md section 9 (v-modelplane baseline line 245)

verevon.exactGap: Request-level routing already exists: inference-core intent.rs resolve() returns a Decision{model,mode,complexity,posture} per request, but fallback.rs only logs it; the resolved model reaches the client as model_used on the done frame (shown as the Modell row in the Details popover) and in cost-core's USAGE_ENVELOPE, while ServedBy carries provider/residency/tier only (no reason) and nothing writes the model to Session Core message or run metadata, so a reopened thread shows none. Absent: step-level RoutingDecision, one resolver (chat uses the intent layer, agent runs use execution-core ModelRoute/EXECUTION_AGENT_MODEL, scheduled run_model is a null placeholder), model lifecycle/successors, model_switched or family-change notice, router feedback and a Space default. Also absent: any thinking-block replay (anthropic.rs discards signature_delta and ChatMessage is flat role/content), but replay is not a correctness blocker today because the gateway tool loop sends flat text messages rather than native tool_use blocks, and there is no Gemini adapter.

verevon.constraints: ZDR: a RoutingDecision is ids and enums only (content-free like turn_timing and the proof bundle) so it may be recorded on ZDR runs; a ReplayEnvelope holds provider-signed reasoning content and must never be persisted on ZDR turns (with_head_summary returns early on zdr as the precedent). Pinned models are never substituted today and a subscription-pinned agent route ends the run on a mismatch, so lifecycle successor mapping must not apply to pinned subscription routes or privacy-floored requests, and any successor use must be recorded per run.

(2) Resolver and lifecycle: one resolve_model() called by the inference-core intent layer and execution-core ModelRoute, with lifecycle fields on ModelInfo; Space and org defaults as inputs. (3) Replay envelope: defer until a native tool-block message type or a Gemini adapter exists, because ChatMessage must first carry content blocks. Drop 'persist on every run step in Session Core': there is no per-inference step table (plan_steps are plan items); use message/run metadata or the event log.
verevon.effortNote: Kept L for the whole item; the stamp plus display is M, resolver plus lifecycle is M to L, and the replay envelope (M) should be deferred, so the near-term slice is M.
verevon.verdictReason: Request-level routing, model_used on the done frame, the Details popover model row and the cost-ledger model all exist, so the item must be stated as extending them. Two parts are misdescribed: replay is not required for correct tool use under the current text-flattened tool loop, and per-step persistence in Session Core has no table to land on.

items.title: Editable permission rules, CEL policy and an MCP tool gate with consent receipts
items.summary: Add a rule store in capability-core (org, Space, user and thread scopes) over typed targets such as read_url(domain), send_mail(recipient) and command(prefix), resolved strictest-wins (deny > ask > ask-session > allow, with a wildcard allow surviving a merge only if both layers state it), so 'don't ask again' shows and edits the exact rule with its scope and org-scope rules are audited admin-gated changes. Optionally accept admin CEL expressions evaluated inside EvaluatePolicy (any deny wins, validated with dry-run), and when MCP tools are enabled add one execution-core gate that spends single-use consent receipts bound to the SHA-256 of the canonical arguments, reusing the approval descriptors.
items.whyItMatters: Editable 'don't ask again' rules are an acknowledged open item and the deterministic way to cut approval fatigue without an LLM in the permission path. Verevon already has the central decision point (capability-core EvaluatePolicy with signed Allow evidence and fail-closed unknown tools) that Claude is only now adding externally, and MCP is how users bring their own tools.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Antigravity (action(target) grant store with deny > ask > allow and per-conversation grants) with Claude (strictness lattice and strictest-wildcard folding, CEL rules and an external decision endpoint that fails closed, MCP gate with single-use consent receipts)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: declarative rules 2 of 12 (differentiator); CEL policy and MCP gate 1 of 12 each (unique)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Rule = {action, target-pattern, effect deny|ask|ask_session|allow, scope, source}; exact match first, else fold the strictest over matching wildcards; deny from any scope wins; grants recorded per conversation. CEL rules {id, condition over (tool, args, session, user), action, reason}, any deny wins. MCP: wrap the transport, reject malformed frames and unlisted tools, mint a short-lived receipt (session, tool, sha256(canonical args)) on approval and execute only by spending a live matching receipt; reserve internal server-name prefixes.

verevonToday.gap: capability-core EvaluatePolicy returns Allow/Ask/Deny per capability with Ed25519-signed Allow evidence and the hook engine supports allow/deny/ask globs, but there is no user- or admin-authored rule set over typed targets, no ask-session level and editable don't-ask-again is not built. MCP tool names are denied by the inline loop (tool_loop.rs:625-645, verified) and execution-core rejects dynamic MCP names until capability-core provides a durable binding, so none of the MCP gating exists yet; nine capabilities sit in an unattested quarantine baseline.

items.approach: capability-core: rules table keyed by capability id plus target pattern with strictest-wins resolution in Go; execution-core passes the target (domain, recipient, path) in EvaluatePolicy and surfaces the matched rule and reason on denials and cards; SPA Rules settings page (reusing R-t3-11-02 scoped grants as the producer of rules). Optional cel-go rules per org inside EvaluatePolicy. MCP gate after capability-core issues per-tool capability ids: execution-core spends argument-hash receipts built on the existing exact-effect descriptors, with reserved server-name prefixes in capability-core.
items.planeOwner: Model Plane
items.risks: Wildcard allows can silently widen authority: strictest-wins, audit every rule change and always show scope. Rule errors can lock users out, so validate and dry-run. Under master-ownership-matrix rule 12 an 'allow' rule for a provider write still needs a signed per-effect authorisation. MCP servers can return injected content, so combine with R-t3-11-07.

alreadyPlanned.where: claude-hermes-deepseek.md section 13.3 records editable don't-ask-again rules as an open item; no scheduled task found

verevon.exactGap: capability-core EvaluateCapability (engine.go) decides per capability id from a risk heuristic plus the org scope-grant table, EvaluatePolicyRequest carries no target or arguments, and execution-core permission::evaluate_call checks arguments only against fixed keyword lists; hook rules are tool-name globs, first-match-wins, fail-open and held in an in-memory HookRegistry. So there is no durable user or admin rule set over typed targets, no ask-session level, no strictest-wins merge and no CEL dependency. There is also no MCP gate, because both loops refuse MCP tools until capability-core issues a durable binding.
reuse: capability-core policy Engine and its signed Allow evidence (execution-core already verifies it and fails closed for unbound tools)
The execution-core hook matcher and the HookRegistry to hook_context_json wire, as the pattern for delivering rules to a run
permission::evaluate_call, which already receives tool_input, as the place to derive a server-side target
attestation.rs payload_sha256 and ticket_tools payload_digest as the pattern for argument-bound consent receipts
capability_scopes grant table and registry ScopeStore for durable per-org grants
SpaceApprovalPanel and the approvals queue UI for showing the rule that matched
verevon.constraints: capability-core IsSupportedScope accepts only org and global; agent, run, thread, workspace and user scopes are rejected until trusted identity bindings exist, so thread, user and Space rules cannot be evaluated in EvaluatePolicy yet. Owner-plane effects and consent-to-disclose tools are never auto-approved (permission/mod.rs), and ownership matrix rule 12 keeps provider writes behind a per-effect signed authorisation, so an allow rule can never relax those. Targets (domain, recipient) must be derived by execution-core from validated arguments, never taken from model text. Space-scoped rules may narrow but must not widen an owner-plane ACL.
verevon.approachAdjustment: First cut: add a server-derived typed target to EvaluatePolicyRequest (proto change in Go and Rust) and a durable rule table in capability-core (not the in-memory hook registry), org scope only, admin-authored and audited, resolved strictest-wins. Thread, user and Space "don't ask again" rules wait for F-t3-006 trusted bindings; until then keep them as per-run grants only. Treat CEL as a separate later increment, and add the MCP receipt gate only after F-t3-003 gives per-tool capability ids. Drop the claim about nine quarantined capabilities, which I did not verify.
verevon.effortNote: Unchanged: proto change, durable store, strictest-wins resolver and a settings page span three services plus the SPA; CEL and MCP receipts come on top.
verevon.verdictReason: Editable rules are genuinely absent (the Space approval panel and the chat design doc both record that no standing answer exists), but the proposed Space, user and thread scopes are not evaluable by capability-core today and the target must be a new proto field, so the approach needs rewording before it can be built.

items.title: Privacy by construction and a closed telemetry contract: user-content newtypes, allow-list scrubbing of telemetry, then org analytics and customer-owned telemetry export
items.summary: Introduce a UserContent (Redacted) newtype in mp-contracts so prompts, messages, tool results and memory cannot be logged or serialised except through an explicit privacy context carrying ZDR posture, add allow-list sanitising of telemetry names and labels, define a content-free telemetry contract (allowed event names, closed enums, buckets), and only then extend Insights with agent-run outcome analytics and customer export.
items.whyItMatters: Verevon's ZDR resolver and hash-only security events are strong; type-level wrappers (Cursor) and allow-list scrubbing (Claude) would make leaks a compile error instead of a review finding. Org analytics is common (5 of 12) but lower urgency.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Cursor (privacy-typed fields); Claude desktop app (allow-list telemetry scrubbing) ; claude
others: manus (mau-086 metadata-only streams with optional full-payload tiers)
cursor (cloud agent run lists and analytics)
hermes (hel-081 closed enums and count buckets, opt-in, recorder never raises)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: R-t3-13-09: C-017: 1 of 12 (unique). C-018: 3 of 12 (differentiator) | R-t3-10-09: Customer telemetry export 5 of 12 (common); workspace analytics 5 of 12 (common); closed-vocabulary telemetry 1 of 12 (unique)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Cursor marks user content in proto field options and wraps it in a RedactedString that refuses to serialize into logs unless privacy mode allows, with content-addressed AES-GCM blobs behind it. Claude's org policy holds the endpoint, protocol, headers (or a headers-helper script), resource attributes, trace toggle and content-capture categories (user prompts, assistant responses, tool details, tool content, raw API bodies) that fail closed to none;

verevonToday.gap: R-t3-13-09: SRC: a ZDR resolver with a golden matrix, encrypted approval continuation descriptors, pattern-based secret scrubbing, hash-only security events and Prometheus plus OTLP telemetry exist. | R-t3-10-09: SRC: cost analytics by user and entries exist (Insights page, cost dashboard) and audit-core has a usage summary route;

items.approach: Newtype and sanitizer first (M), contract next, analytics last (XL).
items.planeOwner: Model Plane (mp-contracts, mp-telemetry) with Control Plane (analytics, export)
items.risks: Refactoring cost across crates; export creates a new egress path.

verevon.exactGap: No UserContent or Redacted newtype exists (the only analogue is RedactedArgv, a plain struct with public fields at sandbox_manager_client.rs:98), mp-telemetry has no field or label allow-list (a JSON fmt layer plus an OTLP trace exporter read from env), and scrub.rs is a regex deny-list applied at the persistence boundary rather than at log or metric boundaries. gateway_metrics.rs labels every request counter and histogram with the raw URI path (lines 37-58), so path-embedded ids become label values. Usage and cost analytics for me and organization scope with a CSV export already ship (cost-client.ts:12, UsageAnalyticsSection.tsx:32, audit-core /usage/summary), so only agent-run outcome analytics and a customer-owned OTLP export are absent.
reuse: mp-telemetry::init as the single place to add a tracing field allow-list layer for every Rust service
mp_contracts::retention resolve_turn and its golden matrix as the privacy-context source
security_events.rs hash-only envelope as the content-free event precedent
scrub.rs scrub_string as defence in depth behind an allow-list
FE usageCsv and UsageAnalyticsSection, cost-client scope me/organization, audit-core /usage and /usage/summary routes
verevon.constraints: ZDR must propagate: any telemetry export or run analytics must be content-free and carry the ZDR posture, and a customer export is a new egress path that needs a Control Plane-owned org setting with explicit consent and audit rather than a Model Plane env var. No cross-plane DB access: outcome analytics must be built from audit-core, cost-core and session-core APIs or events, never another plane's tables. prost-generated message types carry plain String fields and the Go services have no Rust newtype equivalent, so type-level enforcement reaches only hand-written Rust boundaries.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Reorder: (1) change gateway_metrics.rs to label by matched route instead of the raw path and add a tracing field allow-list layer in mp-telemetry::init (S to M, immediate protection across all Rust services); (2) write the content-free telemetry contract as data (allowed event names, closed enums, buckets) enforced by that layer; (3) add the newtype only at hand-written boundaries and enforce the rest with a lint or CI check instead of a repo-wide type refactor; (4) remove 'org usage analytics and export' from this item because it ships, and keep agent-run outcome analytics and customer OTLP export as separate later items owned by Control Plane.
verevon.effortNote: Unchanged for the bundle, but it should be split: the metrics label fix plus telemetry allow-list layer is S to M, a repo-wide newtype is L to XL, and customer export is XL.
verevon.verdictReason: Partial stands. The real, cheap gap is the missing allow-list in mp-telemetry and the raw-path metric label, and usage analytics with CSV export already exist; a single-line grep of tracing macros for prompt, content, query or goal fields found no leak, so the newtype is preventive rather than remedial and the item stays nice-to-have.

items.title: Changed-files card per turn and a review gate before workspace promotion (accept or reject by file or hunk, with feedback to the agent)
