items.summary: At the end of each agent turn, diff the leased workspace against its baseline and show a compact changed-files card with line stats; hold the overlay as pending and let the owner accept or reject per file (later per hunk) with a written reason sent back to the run as steering, before PromoteWorkspace runs.
items.whyItMatters: Review before promotion is table-stakes among coding tools (5 of 9) and useful for document workspaces too, but Verevon is not an IDE and agents barely edit workspace files until F-t3-030 lands, so this follows demand.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: T3 Code (changed-files section with auto-expand thresholds, single-child directory chain collapse, aggregated stats, per-turn persisted expansion) ; Antigravity (accept/reject with FILE|HUNK|ALL scope, written_feedback returned to the trajectory, STALE and CLEARED states)
others: DeepSeek harness (turn-start vs turn-end snapshots; edit replay)
T3 Code (panel scope turn | branch | working tree, persisted per thread, stacked or split)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: R-t3-07-03: 2 of 9 sources; differentiator | R-t3-07-04: 5 of 9 sources; table-stakes
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Snapshot content hashes per path at turn start; Agent edits land in a pending layer instead of the durable copy.

verevonToday.gap: R-t3-07-03: workspace_hydrate::diff_and_upload already returns ChangedFile {path, content_hash, size_bytes, base_hash}, but it runs only once at lease release and the result goes to SnapshotSandbox, not to the user. | R-t3-07-04: Diffs are read-only (unified view, 2,000-line cap, stat-only fallback) and artifacts have a version stepper with a show-changes view.

items.approach: Reuse workspace_hydrate::diff_and_upload per turn; Antigravity's FILE/HUNK/ALL scope.
items.planeOwner: Model Plane (sandbox-manager, workspace) with Frontend Plane (card, review UI)
items.risks: Promote/reject semantics with concurrent runs; stale reviews.

verevon.exactGap: workspace_hydrate::diff_and_upload (workspace_hydrate.rs:102) returns ChangedFile with base_hash but runs once at lease release (sandbox_lease.rs:495-540) and feeds SnapshotSandbox, which upserts a per-run overlay (server.go:204-250); nothing surfaces it to the user, and no caller invokes PromoteWorkspace, so overlays are never merged into the Space today. sandbox-manager's workspace store exposes only GetManifest, UpsertOverlay and a whole-overlay Promote (store.go:73-215), so per-file accept or reject needs new list, discard and per-path promote RPCs plus a gateway route, and diff_and_upload shows no exclusion for the staged _verevon_main.py, .tmp and .mplconfig scratch paths, so a naive card would list them (INF from the code path). The UI has only read-only DiffView for tool output and artifact revisions (ChatMessages.tsx:2086, ChatArtifactPanel.tsx:311-343, 2,000-line cap in diff.ts:61) and per-call GeneratedFiles chips.
reuse: diff_and_upload and ChangedFile{base_hash} as the per-turn diff producer
the overlay versus Space-row split and the CAS compare-and-swap Promote (conflicting_paths) as the pending layer and merge
SnapshotSandbox changed_files for recording the overlay
DiffView, diff.ts hunks and GeneratedFiles chips for the card
the queued mid-run input path (QueuedInputStrip) for sending a rejection reason back to the run as steering
the gateway Work-tab pattern (shared_thread_read_decision_for plus proxy_model_json_with_sandbox) for a read route to the overlay
verevon.constraints: The overlay and Space rows are sandbox-manager data, so the gateway must reach them through a model-gateway or sandbox-manager route under a Space decision, never by direct DB access, and accept or reject authority must come from the Space member decision, not the agent. Workspace writes are durable (CAS plus overlay rows): ExecuteStep refuses persistence under ZDR (grpc.rs:899), and the same refusal should be confirmed on the run_agent path (grpc.rs:1259) before a review gate depends on it. Promote is compare-and-swap per path, so the review UI must handle stale and conflicting files.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Reorder: step 0 is deciding who calls PromoteWorkspace (today nobody does); a review gate is a variant of that call, not an add-on. Add sandbox-manager RPCs to list a lease's overlay, discard paths and promote selected paths, keep the overlay as the pending layer (it already is one), exclude the program file and scratch directories in diff_and_upload, and diff per turn only if code_interpreter edits warrant it; hunk-level accept can wait.
verevon.effortNote: M understates the work: new sandbox-manager RPCs (proto, Go store, Rust client), a gateway route with Space decision plumbing, the review UI and steering feedback. File-level only is L; hunk-level adds M.
verevon.verdictReason: Partial is right and the primitives are real, but the item omits that the promote step is unwired and that per-file accept or reject needs new sandbox-manager APIs; reword around wiring promote first and raise effort to L.

items.title: One action-registry-driven command surface: palette, slash commands, shortcut sheet and safe double-Escape stop
items.summary: Build a Solid command palette (Ctrl/Cmd+K) over the existing typed action registry, executing only low-risk reversible actions directly and opening the normal confirm dialog for the rest, with typed pickers for threads, projects and files and a content mode once server-side chat search lands. Move the fixed chat shortcuts into a declarative {command, key, when} table that renders a searchable Ctrl+/ sheet, add a double-Escape stop validated against the live run id and stream generation, and make the composer slash catalog and the palette read the same definitions.
items.whyItMatters: Power users and enterprise admins move faster, and the registry already carries zod I/O, owner plane, risk and reversibility, so palette actions are authority-checked for free. A safe keyboard stop for an agent run is also a trust feature.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: T3 Code (one palette reducer for commands, threads with content snippets, files and content search, with mutually exclusive modes; VS Code-style when-clauses, a key recorder and conflict flags) plus DeepSeek (searchable Mod+/ reference and a double-Escape stop bound to the live turn)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: Palette: 4 of 12; keyboard-first and shortcuts: 6 of 12; slash commands: 3 of 12 (common to differentiator).
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: A palette state machine reduceCommandPaletteUiState(mode: command|files|content) where re-pressing the shortcut toggles closed and modes never stack; items {kind: action|submenu, searchTerms, threadContentMatch}. A declarative keybinding table {command, key, when} with per-OS overrides and a context-key evaluator. Stop requires two Escapes within a short window, each validated against {sessionId, turn, generation, focused region}. Slash commands come from one registry {name, description, inputHint, surfaces, handler}; a typed command never silently becomes a prompt.

verevonToday.gap: Ctrl/Cmd+K and bare "/" open global search but no palette executes actions (grep for CommandPalette and cmdk in src finds nothing). Chat has a handful of fixed shortcuts (new chat, focus composer, thread switch, Esc), no shortcut sheet, no rebinding and no double-Escape stop. A typed slash catalog does exist, but only in DashboardComposer: ComposerCommand entries with bilingual aliases, descriptions and argument hints, and an unknown /name is deliberately sent as plain text, the opposite of DeepSeek's guarantee, so that choice should be made deliberately. Whether the chat-page composer shares it was not verified. There is no server-side conversation search for a content mode.

items.approach: Frontend Plane: (1) extract a declarative shortcut table from use-chat-shortcuts.ts and render the Ctrl+/ sheet from it (task I1), testing nb-NO layouts for AltGr collisions; (2) add the double-Escape stop wired to the run id and stream generation; (3) build the palette as a Solid overlay over action-registry.ts, filtering by risk metadata so only low-risk reversible actions run directly; (4) lift the DashboardComposer command catalog into a shared module that both the slash menu and the palette consume, and decide the unknown-slash behaviour; (5) add the thread-content mode when full-text chat search lands (task I12). Defer user rebinding.
items.planeOwner: Frontend Plane
items.risks: The palette must not become a back door around approval gates, so reuse registry risk and reversibility metadata. Bare "/" already opens search outside the composer, so pick one meaning per context. Needs verification that the chat-page composer shares the slash catalog.

alreadyPlanned.where: Shortcut sheet is task I1 (apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/apps/verevon-web/plans/system-audits/CHAT_GAP_CLOSURE_PLAN_2026-10-01.md:215), full-text chat search is I12 (:222) and user slash command templates are I13 (:223). The palette itself and the double-Escape stop were not found in the plan.

verevon.exactGap: No palette exists (Ctrl/Cmd+K and bare '/' open global search, and Escape only closes shell overlays), chat has four fixed shortcuts in matchChatShortcut with no table, sheet, rebinding or double-Escape stop, and the stop path (cancelRun in use-chat-controller) has no keyboard binding in either file. A typed slash catalog does exist and the chat page does render the same DashboardComposer (ComposerCommand with aliases, argument hints, built-ins plus skills, capabilities and connectors from chat-actions-client), but it does not read action-registry.ts and an unknown /name is sent as plain text.
reuse: action-registry.ts descriptors (ownerPlane, risk, requiresApproval, reversible, zod schemas) and the gateway /api/v1/actions/catalog route
ActionCommand.tsx preview-then-execute flow (previewAction/executeAction, approval-gated vs direct-run badge) as the palette's confirm step
use-chat-shortcuts.ts matchChatShortcut as the seed for a declarative shortcut table
use-chat-controller cancelRun(runId) for the double-Escape stop
DashboardComposer ComposerCommand type and chat-actions-client loadSpecializedActions for the slash catalog
existing global search panel (CoreNavbar searchOpen) as the host for a palette mode
verevon.constraints: Frontend Plane only, but the palette must never bypass approval gates: run through previewAction and executeAction and honour requiresApproval and risk. Escape is already consumed by CoreNavbar closeShellOverlays, ChatPage panel close and menu-local handlers, so the double-Escape stop must be lowest priority and ignore events when any overlay or menu is open. The plan assigns the DashboardComposer command region to tasks I7 (table-driven commands) and I13 (user slash templates) with one owner per region and a rule never to rewrite the file, so the shared-catalog step must be sequenced after them. Slash entries come from skills, capabilities and connector endpoints (Model Plane catalogs), not the registry, so a shared definition needs an adapter over two sources.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Replace 'verify the chat-page composer shares the slash catalog' with the confirmed fact that it does (ChatPage renders DashboardComposer). Start the palette with navigation plus a curated allowlist of parameterless, low-risk, reversible registry actions, because most registry actions need typed inputs, and use ActionCommand for the rest. Sequence the shared-catalog lift after I7 and I13; the shortcut table, Ctrl+/ sheet (plan I1) and double-Escape stop are independent and can go first.
verevon.effortNote: Unchanged; shortcut table, sheet and double-Escape are S, the palette over the registry is M.
verevon.verdictReason: Partial is correct; the open question about the chat composer is resolved and the plan-ownership conflict on DashboardComposer commands must be added.

items.title: Feedback surfaces and limit notices: shell toasts, composer banners, connection pill and role-aware limit messages
items.summary: Add a shell-level toast manager that outlives the panel that triggered it, a prioritised notice stack docked above the composer, and a connection pill driven by the chat stream state with hysteresis so healthy operation stays silent. Map the typed refusal codes and gateway 429s to inline notices that state the limit, the current value, the reset time and a role-aware action (member: ask your admin; owner: change plan or quota).
items.whyItMatters: Verevon spans many planes that fail independently, so calm, specific failure and limit feedback is a trust signal for an enterprise product. The typed refusal catalogue already exists, so the missing piece is the presentation layer.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: T3 Code (thread-scoped stacked toasts with expandable detail and copy-for-errors, composer banner stack) plus DeepSeek (toast vs in-place notice rule; connection pill with minimum-visible and recovered hold times) for feedback; Manus and Claude.ai (inline limit messages with reset, wait, upgrade or credits) for limits
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: Feedback surfaces: 4 of 12; limit presentation: 4 of 12 (both common).
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: One toast manager {threadRef, severity, detail, actions, copyable}; a composer banner stack with priority ordering; a connection indicator fed by the SSE/fetch layer that shows Reconnecting only after a short delay and holds Connected for about 2 s before hiding (DeepSeek, DOC); failed operations keep user data in place. Limits arrive as typed errors {limitKind, current, max, resetAt, actions[]} and map to inline notices with different calls to action for members and owners.

verevonToday.gap: Typed subscription, ZDR and capability refusal codes, org quotas and a 429 with Retry-After exist, and chat has reconnect handling in the live run panel with honest error events. The comparator's grep found no app-wide toast system (only ticket bulk actions) and no connection-status pill; how gateway 503 and 429 errors surface outside chat was not checked, so the feedback half is unknown. There is no live spend meter (task I16) and no inline notice of the form you hit X, resets at Y, ask your admin.

items.approach: Frontend Plane: add a toast manager and notice primitive in src/shared/ui, a ComposerNoticeStack in the chat composer, and a ConnectionPill fed by the chat-client stream state with an 800 ms minimum-visible and 2 s recovered hold. Map refusal codes (mp-contracts, model-gateway subscription_failure) and 429 responses to localised notices with role-aware actions. Model Plane cost-core exposes a per-run and per-month spend projection for the meter (task I16).
items.planeOwner: Frontend Plane
items.risks: Do not expose org spend to non-admin members. Avoid over-notifying: healthy stays silent. Needs verification of how non-chat pages surface gateway errors today and whether a toast primitive already exists under src/shared/ui.

verevon.exactGap: Chat already maps typed stream failures (subscription usage limit with reset time, rate_limited, reauth, ZDR refusal codes) to inline notices with a retry, wait or reconnect action in chat-normalizers streamFailurePresentation and ChatMessages, and chat-client resumes dropped streams with Last-Event-ID. Missing: any shell toast primitive (src/shared/ui has none; only a search-panel toast style exists), any connection pill (the only stream-level reconnect control found is the browser-watch fallback in ChatLiveRunPanel), a unified composer notice stack (several ad hoc status banners exist in DashboardComposer), role-aware limit wording, and chat mapping of budget_exceeded (it falls to the default branch in chat; only the Spaces composer renders an admin-pointing message).
reuse: streamFailurePresentation and StreamFailureAction (chat-normalizers.ts, chat-types.ts) as the typed refusal-to-notice mapper
ChatMessages verevon-chat-error-notice for inline notices
shared/i18n/errors.ts code-to-message table (includes budget_exceeded and budget_unavailable)
resumeStream and Last-Event-ID tracking in chat-client.ts as the connection-state source
model-gateway budget.rs 402 budget_exceeded and the gateway rate_limit.rs 429 with Retry-After
OrgDeletionBanner and the Spaces budget notice as precedents
verevon.constraints: Frontend Plane presentation only; Model Plane and Control Plane already own the refusal codes and quotas. The budget_exceeded 402 body carries current_cost_usd and current_tokens (org-level spend), so a member-facing notice must show only the message and an ask-your-admin action, and numbers only to admins. ZDR refusal copy must stay content-free as today. Healthy operation must stay silent.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Narrow the item: drop 'map refusal codes to notices', which exists for chat, and keep (1) a shell toast manager and notice primitive in src/shared/ui, (2) a ConnectionPill fed from the stream and resume state in use-chat-controller, (3) role-aware wording for budget_exceeded and 429 in chat using the same errors.ts text the Spaces composer uses, and (4) later, the live spend meter (plan I16).
verevon.effortNote: Reduced from M: refusal mapping, reset-time wording and resume already exist; S for toast plus role-aware budget notice, M only if the pill must be threaded deeply through use-chat-controller.
verevon.verdictReason: The feedback and limit-presentation gaps are real but smaller than stated; the item undersells the existing typed notices and misses the member-versus-admin spend exposure in the 402 body.

items.title: Typed feature-flag and settings registry served by Control Plane, with kill switches and an agent-access class
items.summary: Replace the sprawl of per-crate environment flags with one typed registry (name, stage, default, owner, kill switch, agentAccess excluded|read|write) whose values are evaluated per org by Control Plane, cached in each service with a TTL and served to the SPA in the BFF boot payload. Fold the fragmented composer, org and profile settings into the same schema so one source feeds the settings UI and any future agent settings tool.
items.whyItMatters: Verevon has many built-but-dark features (Do on subscription, hooks, MCP dispatch, fine-tuning); today turning one on or off needs a redeploy and there is no per-org staging or record of what is live. An agent-access class is required before the agent can be given a settings tool.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Claude desktop app
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: C-019: 4 of 12 (common). C-020: 5 of 12 (common)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Flags: layered sources (static map, remote refresh, disk cache, fallback), exposure events, and staleness windows that disable security-sensitive features when flags are stale. Settings: a zod schema where each key carries scope, default and agent access (excluded, read, write); security-relevant keys are excluded from the agent's own settings tool, main-only keys cannot be set from the renderer, and grant maps can only be reduced.

verevonToday.gap: SRC: features are gated by ad hoc environment variables (AGENTIC_SUBSCRIPTION_ENABLED, the fine-tune feature env and separate env_flag helpers in execution-core and session-core) plus a capability promotion ledger TSV; there is no central typed registry, no per-org evaluation and no runtime kill switch. The only flag-like store in Control Plane is billing-core's per-plan feature_flags JSON map. Settings are spread across composer settings, BFF org settings and server-resolved profiles; the profile already lets clients only tighten posture, which is the right idea at the wrong breadth.

items.approach: Define a flag and settings schema crate in mp-contracts (name, stage dev|beta|stable|deprecated, default, owner, scope, agentAccess); Control Plane org-core serves per-org values (billing-core plan feature_flags can seed entitlement-driven flags); each service caches with TTL and fails closed for security gates when stale; the BFF boot payload exposes the SPA-visible subset; link flag state to the capability promotion ledger so a capability cannot be live without ledger evidence. Flags may only restrict: a flag must never widen ZDR or authority posture.
items.planeOwner: Control Plane (registry), consumed by all planes
items.risks: Flag debt; a flag path that widens ZDR or authority would defeat the posture model; migration of existing settings rows.

verevon.exactGap: Per-org entitlements already exist in Control Plane (org-core org_entitlements table seeded with default feature.* keys, GET /organizations/:id/entitlements, proxied by the gateway and read by the SPA for the ZDR entitlement check) and billing-core keeps per-account feature_flags and entitlements that its feature check evaluates, but there is no typed registry (stage, owner, kill switch, agentAccess), no operator or admin write route for entitlements, and Model Plane services read none of it (org_quota.rs reads org-core quotas only; Go services use Control-signed decisions that carry an entitlement revision). Model Plane features are gated by independent per-service env vars (AGENTIC_SUBSCRIPTION_ENABLED, FINETUNE_ENABLED, LEARNING_RUN_EVENTS_ENABLED, PROMOTE_ON_USE_ENABLED and others) plus a promotion-ledger TSV, so changing one means a redeploy. The model-executable action allowlist (model-eligibility.ts) already acts as an agent-access gate and currently excludes every settings action.
reuse: org-core org_entitlements (per-org key and enabled), its GET route, the gateway /api/v1/orgs/{id}/entitlements proxy and the SPA organization-client
billing-core Account.Entitlements / FeatureFlags and the plan-driven refresh as the entitlement seed
org_quota.rs (service-token derivation per org, call pattern into org-core) as the template for a Model Plane flag client; its fail-open outage behaviour must not be copied for security gates
Control-signed decisions (ResolveRunActionAuthority, ResolveScheduledStepAuthority) that already re-resolve entitlement before an effect
mp-contracts agentic_subscription.rs (pure Switches value read at the edge) as the schema-crate pattern
action-registry ownerPlane/risk/requiresApproval/reversible plus MODEL_EXECUTABLE_ACTION_IDS as the existing agent-access model
CAPABILITY_PROMOTION_LEDGER.tsv as the evidence record to link flags to
verevon.constraints: Control Plane owns entitlements, quotas and billing, so extend org-core's entitlement store (billing-core stays the plan-driven seed) rather than create a second Control registry; registry definitions may live in mp-contracts but evaluation is per org through Control Plane with a TTL cache that fails closed for security gates. A flag may only restrict: it must never widen ZDR or authority posture. Some env switches are deployment-ordering gates (AGENTIC_SUBSCRIPTION_ENABLED is turned on only after the new execution-core is the one running, and its module states a deployed process never changes its environment), so those must stay env, not become runtime per-org flags. Nothing may expose a settings write action to the model until agentAccess exists.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Start from org-core entitlements: add an operator/admin write route and stage/owner metadata, then add a small Model Plane client modelled on org_quota.rs with a TTL cache, and migrate only flags with a real per-org use (hooks, MCP dispatch, Do-on-subscription staging, fine-tuning). Leave deployment-ordering env switches alone. Map agentAccess onto the existing action-registry and model-eligibility allowlist instead of a new concept, and serve the SPA subset through the entitlements endpoint the gateway already proxies (the SPA reads it today only for the ZDR entitlement check in organization-client.ts) rather than a new boot payload.
verevon.effortNote: Unchanged. Storage, read route, gateway proxy and SPA client already exist; the cost is the write path, the schema crate and a cached Model Plane client.
verevon.verdictReason: The claim of no per-org evaluation and no Control-side flag store is wrong for Control Plane and the SPA (org entitlements and plan feature flags exist) and right for Model Plane; reword as extending org-core entitlements, keeping deployment-ordering switches as env.

items.title: Library of generated and uploaded files across chats, with org publishing built on Data Plane documents
items.summary: Register generated files and promoted artifacts (non-ZDR) as Data Plane v2 documents with origin_thread metadata, and build the library as a filtered document view with search, type grouping and favourites instead of a new store. 'Publish' is then 'save the artifact as a document and share it through the existing resource_grants and Application Plane collaboration', not a parallel publishing platform.
items.whyItMatters: Users want to find 'that report Verevon made last week' without hunting threads, and agentic products that produce deliverables converge on a library. Reusing Data Plane documents avoids duplicate storage and keeps sharing under existing grants.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Manus (SRC) for the library; Claude desktop (SRC) for private-by-default published artifacts with roles
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 3 of 12 for the library (differentiator) and 3 of 12 for publishing (differentiator)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: A server file index keyed by owner with type, stage (process versus product), origin session, versions and share state; a library page with filters and batch download; storage quotas and recently-deleted restore (ChatGPT, DOC). Publishing: an artifact store with versions and an ACL (org, people, groups, email, public link; view, comment, edit), comments anchored to spots and @assistant comments routed to a watching session.

verevonToday.gap: No cross-chat file library: artifacts and generated files live per thread (partly client-side), and the Findings and Reports pages read the local transcript cache only. No artifact publishing, comments or runtime exist; the only sharing is document sharing through resource_grants in shares.rs, not chat artifacts.

items.approach: After R-t3-01-04, add a 'Save as document' action that creates a Data Plane v2 document with origin_thread metadata and reuses shares.rs and Control Plane grants for visibility. The library page is a filtered document view in the SPA. Comments and @assistant routing, if wanted, go through Application Plane collaboration rather than a new runtime. No durable library under ZDR.
items.planeOwner: Data Plane v2 (documents), Frontend Plane (library view), Control Plane (grants)
items.risks: Duplicated storage between session artifacts and documents; retention policy; public links conflict with ZDR and org data policies, so do not offer them by default.

verevon.exactGap: No cross-chat library exists: the Reports and Findings pages read the local transcript cache and a title regex (ChatUtilityPage), the artifact panel only exports Word, Excel, PowerPoint and PDF, and artifacts persist as per-thread message metadata in session-core. The document-backed pieces exist but are unwired: POST /api/v1/chat/documents and /api/v1/knowledge/documents create Data Plane documents (private by default for end users), the Knowledge page lists them and ShareDialog shares them through resource_grants, while execution-core's workspace_promote.rs is a ZDR-guarded promotion primitive with no caller. documents-api-go lists only by org, type and viewer visibility, so there is no origin-thread or source filter, and its documents are UTF-8 text up to 5 MiB, so binary artifacts cannot be stored there.
reuse: gateway POST /api/v1/knowledge/documents and /api/v1/chat/documents (proxy to documents-api /v1/documents)
Knowledge page document list plus ShareDialog and shares.rs over user-core resource_grants
documents-api-go visibility default (private for end users) and the type filter on GET /v1/documents
execution-core workspace_promote.rs reject_zdr_durable_mutation pattern
ChatArtifactPanel export menu as the place for a 'Save as document' action
verevon.constraints: Data Plane v2 owns documents and Control Plane owns grants, so 'publish' must stay 'save as document then share through resource_grants', never a parallel store or public link by default. The current chat-document upload route hard-codes zdr_classification 'internal' and shows no ZDR refusal, so a save action must refuse for ZDR sessions (ZDR must propagate) and keep end-user documents private. Space or org visibility must never be widened by the save; org-wide visibility needs an admin and is not the default.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Implement 'Save as document' in the gateway on the existing knowledge document create (not workspace_promote.rs, which is sandbox-only and has no caller), with a dedicated type value such as chat_artifact plus source and metadata carrying thread id, artifact id and version, so the existing type filter drives the library without a Data Plane schema change; add a source or metadata filter only if needed. Scope the first cut to text artifacts (document, code, html); binary kinds (spreadsheet, file, image, delivered as data URIs) need the blob store from F-t3-017. Surface the library as a filtered view inside the Knowledge page rather than a new store.
verevon.effortNote: Unchanged for text artifacts; L if binary artifacts are included, because documents-api accepts text only and a blob store is a prerequisite.
verevon.verdictReason: Status is partial rather than absent (document create, listing and sharing exist); the approach holds but must add the text-only limit, the ZDR gate on the save route and the type-based filter.

items.title: Teach mode: record a user's hosted-browser workflow and distil it into a reviewed, replayable skill
items.summary: Record the steps a user performs in a Quarry-hosted browser session (including takeover sessions) as step receipts, have a Model Plane run draft a parameterised routine, send it through the skill proposal path for review, and replay it with per-step confirmation under the same evidence trail. Desktop recording stays out of scope.
items.whyItMatters: Learning by demonstration (Claude teach mode, Manus) is a differentiator (3 of 12) that fits Verevon's receipt machinery, but it depends on the browser, takeover and learning-governance work first.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Claude (teach mode with a guided overlay plus watch-and-record with voiceover); ChatGPT's opt-in Computer History is a related activity memory (DOC) ; manus
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: R-t3-06-12: 2 of 12 sources (differentiator) | R-t3-08-11: 3 of 12 sources (differentiator).
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Record steps (events, frames, narration), have the model summarise them into a parameterised routine or skill, then replay it with confirmation. Manus ships a recorder addon sharing an MCP server with computer use: it captures action events, periodic screenshots and an optional voice transcript, uploads a recording bundle, a task summarises it into steps and frames and drafts the skill file, and the user reviews it before it is delivered.

evidence: No baseline record and a bounded grep did not complete; likely absent
verevonToday.gap: R-t3-06-12: Teach-by-demonstration browser routines are shortlisted (#3, effort L) in the cowork research but not built. | R-t3-08-11: Not verified: check the Ingestion Plane (Quarry browser sessions) and the Model Plane for a recording-to-skill flow.

items.approach: Shortlisted as #3 in the cowork research; build after F-t3-008, F-t3-026 and F-t3-007.
items.planeOwner: Ingestion Plane (Quarry traces) with Model Plane (distillation, skills)
items.risks: Recorded sessions contain personal data and credentials typed by the human; the trace must exclude them.

alreadyPlanned.where: R-t3-06-12: apps/VEREVON_UI_COWORK_RESEARCH_2026-08-13.md section 2.3 (teach-by-demonstration, shortlist #3, L)

verevon.exactGap: No demonstration recorder or recording-to-skill path exists in Quarry or Model Plane code, but substrate does: human takeover actions arrive over the live-view websocket and run through the same execute_ws_action path as agent actions, which appends step receipts with actor id (skipped under ZDR), and a RUN_COMPLETED learning loop writes transcript-derived skills into session-core. That loop persists skills with enabled=true and origin background_review and has no proposal or review state, and a Quarry plan (section 42, greenfield) already describes recording human takeover and compiling deterministic browser procedures with candidate/shadow/active/quarantined rollout.
reuse: Quarry step receipts and ReceiptBuilder (append-only, actor-tagged) as the recording substrate
the live-view websocket action path (execute_ws_action) and BrowserControlMode::HumanTakeover state
Quarry plan section 42 procedure compiler and rollout states for replay
capability-core sessionreview and skillsink plus the AgentSkill origin and enabled fields, once F-t3-007 adds proposal state
Quarry ClickSemantic and ClickRef locators (snapshot-scoped) instead of coordinates for replay
model-gateway trajectory recorder as a reference for the trace shape
verevon.constraints: Quarry owns recording, procedure compilation and execution; the Model proposes browser actions and Quarry executes or rejects them, so a taught skill should reference a Quarry procedure id and parameters and replay through Quarry with per-step confirmation, not re-drive the browser from skill prose. Under ZDR Quarry writes no receipts or checkpoints, so recording must be refused for ZDR sessions. Receipts store the full AgentAction (typed text included) and no redaction of typed text was found, so credentials a human types in takeover would be retained unless the recorder redacts or excludes secret fields first. Skills must pass the proposal path of F-t3-007 (owner-scoped, reviewed) because the current learning loop auto-enables skills.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Re-anchor the item on Quarry's planned section 42 (recorded browser procedure and compiler) rather than a new Model Plane recorder: Quarry records and compiles a candidate procedure from takeover receipts, Model Plane drafts the parameterised description and routes it through the F-t3-007 proposal path, and replay runs under Quarry rollout states with confirmation. Human takeover actions are coordinate-based (ClickPoint) and Type with selectors, so distillation must resolve them to semantic locators from observations. Add secret-field redaction as a hard precondition.
verevon.effortNote: Raised from L: Quarry's procedure compiler is greenfield with rollout states, and the recorder, redaction, review UI and skill wrapper all sit on top of F-t3-008, F-t3-026 and F-t3-007.
verevon.verdictReason: Planned, not partial: the feature itself is docs-only but the substrate and an existing Quarry plan change where it should be built, and two safety preconditions (ZDR, typed-text redaction) are missing from the item.

items.title: Upgrade voice input: streaming dictation with a cleanup pass first, local speech-to-text for ZDR later, realtime delegation only if un-parked
items.summary: Phase 1: add a streaming speech endpoint in model-gateway (a proxied WebSocket, so provider keys never reach the browser and cost stays metered), capture with an AudioWorklet at 16 kHz PCM in about 40 ms frames, and one dictation state machine (idle, starting, listening, finishing, with a length cap) shared by the composer and voice mode, with an optional cleanup pass through the governed loop. Phase 2 (optional): local WASM speech-to-text in a worker with pinned model hashes for ZDR and temporary chat. Phase 3, only if the owner un-parks it: a realtime voice front end with exactly two tools (delegate and stay_silent) so every action stays in the governed loop.
items.whyItMatters: Dictation is table-stakes (6 of 11 sources) and exists, but one governed call per utterance feels slow and has no live text, and users on ZDR or in temporary chat have no voice input at all. A delegation-only realtime front end answers the governance concern behind the owner's park decision.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Claude desktop (SRC) and Antigravity (SRC) for streaming dictation; DeepSeek harness (SRC) for local speech-to-text; Codex (SRC) for governed realtime delegation
others: ChatGPT web (DOC, Live voice UX bar)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: Dictation: 6 of 11 (5 distinct vendors), table-stakes. Realtime delegation: 2 of 11, differentiator. On-device speech-to-text: 1 of 11, unique
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Dictation: an AudioWorklet downsamples to 16 kHz PCM and posts about 40 ms frames; the page asks the backend for a short-lived speech credential or uses a backend WebSocket proxy; partial and final events return; a finishing state flushes; an optional cheap-model cleanup rewrites the final transcript using conversation context; a hard cap bounds session length. Local: lazy-download a quantised model (about 240 MB INT8) after explicit user preparation, verify size and SHA-256, run VAD plus recognition on the CPU, never send audio off the device. Realtime: WebRTC with a short-lived session secret; the realtime model has only delegate(text, mode new|steer|queue) and stay_silent, and delegate posts into the governed agent loop of the same thread; no spoken approvals.

verevonToday.gap: Dictation is shipped but is one governed call per utterance (record, upload, transcribe) with no live partials, no cleanup pass and an 8 MiB audio cap; no live microphone proof (DOC). Voice is refused under ZDR and blocked in temporary chat, so those users have no voice input. A realtime session mint exists (/v1/ai/realtime/session) but there is no browser WebRTC client; the bridge-core speech-LLM-speech pipeline is interfaces only; the owner parked duplex voice (OD19).

items.approach: Model Plane: a streaming speech route in model-gateway that proxies the provider WebSocket (cost and audit metered, ZDR refusal unchanged) or mints a short-lived scoped token; cleanup through the normal governed loop. Frontend Plane: AudioWorklet capture and the shared state machine in the composer and voice dialog; for phase 2 a worker running whisper.cpp or sherpa-onnx WASM with model files served from Verevon's CDN with pinned hashes, enabled only where the server path is refused, and tested on Norwegian audio. Phase 3 only after an owner ruling: the delegation endpoint calls the normal turn API, approvals stay on screen, and the realtime provider must be in an EU region with audio ZDR attested.
items.planeOwner: Model Plane (model-gateway streaming proxy, realtime broker) with Frontend Plane (capture, state machine, local speech-to-text)
items.risks: Direct browser-to-provider streaming would bypass gateway metering unless proxied; ZDR must keep refusing server audio; Norwegian accuracy of small local models is unproven; realtime adds per-minute cost, EU-region latency and accidental spoken consent.

verevon.exactGap: The cleanup pass is already shipped: /api/v1/ai/dictate runs speech-to-text then a fail-soft LLM cleanup in model-gateway ai_dictate (http_routes.rs:3960), and the composer and voice dialog both use it, so the item's "no cleanup pass" is wrong. Missing: streaming or partial transcripts (capture is MediaRecorder per utterance and STT providers are REST-only), AudioWorklet capture, local speech-to-text, and any browser realtime client (the realtime session mint is not routed by the BFF and nothing in the SPA calls it; bridge-core voice is interfaces only). Speech is refused under ZDR and blocked in temporary chat, and duplex voice sits under OD19 with park recommended and no owner ruling recorded.
reuse: ai_dictate cleanup stage and DICTATE_SYSTEM_PROMPT (keep it as the finishing step after streamed partials)
VoicePhase state machine and voice-recorder level meter and silence auto-stop
inference-core reject_unattested_zdr_modality, which already refuses speech under ZDR
The BFF ai.rs route layer and org ZDR posture raise (apply_org_zdr_posture) for any new streaming route
The realtime session mint in realtime.rs only as a later Phase 3 broker
verevon.constraints: The browser-speech ESLint guard forbids SpeechRecognition and any vendor recogniser so audio always goes through Verevon provider and audit controls. A new streaming route must stay proxied through the Rust gateway and model-gateway so cost is metered and ZDR keeps refusing server audio; the existing realtime mint returns a client_secret and websocket_url for browser-direct use, which would bypass metering and must not be the dictation path. Model Plane owns inference-core speech providers and model-gateway routes; the Frontend Plane owns capture and the state machine. Local speech-to-text for ZDR must serve model files from Verevon with pinned hashes and be proven on Norwegian audio. Duplex or realtime voice needs the OD19 owner ruling first.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Drop "cleanup pass first" from the item and rename it as streaming partials plus a final cleanup. Phase 1 needs a new streaming STT capability in inference-core (providers are REST only today) before the proxy and AudioWorklet work can matter. Keep local WASM speech-to-text as the only route to ZDR voice and keep Phase 3 behind the owner ruling.
verevon.effortNote: Raised from M: Phase 1 needs a new streaming STT provider in inference-core with ZDR handling plus a WebSocket proxy through two services and the SPA, not just a client change.
verevon.verdictReason: Dictation and its cleanup pass already exist, and the item's gap text says otherwise; the remaining value is streaming partials, ZDR-capable local speech-to-text and (if un-parked) realtime delegation.

items.title: Run admission controls: credit-aware pause and resume, an org-level agent pause switch and clamped per-turn overrides
items.summary: Add a Control-plane org flag ("agents paused") checked at run, schedule and trigger admission and again at each continuation, as an incident-response kill switch (drain.rs only handles redeploys today). Add a paused_for_credit run status when the cost reservation fails mid-run (persist state, resume on a billing event, and show queue position or a cheaper tier at admission). Add a typed per-turn override envelope (model, effort, approval posture) validated and clamped server-side against Control-plane entitlements.
items.whyItMatters: Long agent runs, goals and schedules make admission control matter: enterprise admins need a fast stop, and a run should pause rather than die at a credit boundary. Per-turn overrides let users move a hard step to a stronger model without losing context. All three are cheap once runs are resumable.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Hermes (install-wide pause through a fail-safe sentinel) for the kill switch; Perplexity (pauses rather than cancels on credit exhaustion) for credit pause; Codex (typed 27-field TurnStartParams) for overrides
others: Manus (per-tier wait estimates, idleness reporting and maintenance fence)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: emergency stop 2 of 12; credit-aware admission 2 of 12 (differentiator); per-turn overrides 4 of 12 (common)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: A global or org pause flag is checked at admission for runs, schedules and triggers. Before each round check the cost reservation; on shortfall set paused_for_credit and persist state, and a billing event resumes the run. A typed TurnStart{model, effort, approval_policy, ...} is validated server-side and clamped per surface and plan.

evidence: apps/Model Plane/rust/services/model-gateway/src/drain.rs:1-20 and 103 (graceful drain on redeploy with /readyz 503 and in-flight completion)

No baseline record for org-level pause, credit-aware pause or a typed per-turn override envelope; cost reservation (proposal section 18) is listed as not built per the cluster; normalize.rs not re-read
verevonToday.gap: Drain on redeploy exists. No org-level or global pause of new agent work was found, no paused_for_credit state, and whether Do runs accept a typed per-turn model or effort override clamped by entitlements was not verified.

items.approach: Control Plane org setting plus Model Plane admission. Gateway and capability-core read the org flag at run, schedule and trigger admission; cost-core reservation failure transitions the run to paused_for_credit via the continuation machinery; extend the invoke contract with typed per-turn overrides clamped by Control-plane entitlements.
items.planeOwner: Control Plane (flag, entitlements) with Model Plane (admission)
items.risks: Billing correctness around pause and resume; entitlement bypass if overrides are not clamped server-side; the policy for an unreadable pause flag (fail open or fail closed) must be an explicit, documented choice.

verevon.exactGap: What exists: drain.rs (graceful shutdown on redeploy only), a user pause (PauseRun/ResumeRun, an in-memory RunStatus::Paused honoured only by the browser-agent loop), a durable HITL pause (agent.rs pause_for_approval creates a session-core approval with a continuation descriptor and sets AwaitingApproval) whose cold resume through approval_delivery_worker.rs covers only three idempotent action kinds, admission-time budget checks (org_quota.rs reads org-core ceilings and fails open on an org-core outage, then cost-core check_budget returns a hard 402 budget_exceeded; no mid-run cost check was found), and per-turn model, effort (quick|standard|deep mapped server-side to a clamped thinking budget) and approval posture that a client can only tighten. What is missing: any org-level or global agent pause (searches for org pause, kill switch and emergency stop found only per-feature env switches), a paused_for_credit status and any loop-level cold resume (run status strings are queued, running, completed, failed, cancelled, awaiting_approval, and the worker's own header calls resuming a live loop a larger problem it does not attempt), and a typed per-turn override envelope clamped against Control entitlements (no entitlement clamp on the requested model was found).
reuse: durable HITL pause: agent.rs pause_for_approval (session-core CreateApproval with continuation descriptor, AwaitingApproval), ResumeRun with validate_granted_approval, and approval_delivery_worker.rs as the pattern for a credit-wait pause that a billing event can grant
execution-core RunStatus::Paused, StateStore pause/resume_paused and the PauseRun/ResumeRun RPCs (user pause resumes without an approval id)
budget.rs plus org_quota.rs admission path in sse.rs, which already runs once per turn before inference

Control-issued decisions (ResolveRunActionAuthority re-resolves entitlement before an effect; ResolveScheduledStepAuthority gates each scheduled step) as the place a pause can be enforced without a new flag plane
thinking.rs budget_tokens and profile.rs resolve_posture (stricter-only) as the clamp pattern for a typed override envelope
drain.rs as the model for in-flight completion semantics
verevon.constraints: Control Plane owns entitlements and org policy, so the pause flag must be a Control-side org setting with Model Plane only reading it at admission and at each continuation; the Control-decision path for effectful and scheduled steps is the natural fail-closed enforcement point, while org_quota's fail-open-on-outage behaviour is wrong for a kill switch and needs an explicit documented policy. Execution-core has no database, so a durable paused_for_credit state must be recorded through session-core (system of record, as approvals are today), and it is not possible for ZDR runs, which are persistence-free (run_control is refused for them): those must end with a clear failure rather than persist state. Overrides must be validated server-side and may only restrict or select within Control entitlements, never widen approval posture or ZDR.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Split into three pieces. (1) The org pause switch first: a Control org setting enforced in the gateway admission path next to org_quota, in Control's per-step decision issuance for effects and scheduled steps, and as a gate in the agent loop (only browser_agent polls Paused today). (2) A typed per-turn override envelope reusing the existing effort, posture and model fields with an entitlement clamp. (3) paused_for_credit last: a durable HITL pause exists, but cold resume only re-executes three idempotent action kinds and its own header says resuming a live loop is a larger problem, so a credit pause needs a round-boundary pause that a billing event can grant and a proven re-entry of run_agent from the durable transcript; the item's 'cheap once runs are resumable' premise is only partly true.
verevon.effortNote: Raised from M. The org pause switch alone is M and overrides are S to M, but paused_for_credit needs a new approval kind, a billing-event resume trigger and loop-level re-entry that the delivery worker does not provide, which is L and depends on durable run continuation (F-t3-002).
verevon.verdictReason: The three asks are genuinely missing, but the item understates what exists (PauseRun/Paused, the durable approval pause, the admission budget check, clamped effort and posture) and misjudges the cost of paused_for_credit; split it and lead with the org pause switch.

items.title: Per-Space environment specs and prebuilt sandbox images
items.summary: Let a Space or org define a sandbox environment declaratively (base image, setup script, env with secret refs, network policy, named actions) and prebuild it into a content-hashed image that is rebuilt on spec change or on a schedule, so agent sandboxes start fast on a healthy, reproducible base.
items.whyItMatters: Enterprise customers and Spaces can preinstall their tools and connectors, so agent runs skip install time and behave reproducibly. Without it every run pays setup cost or works with a fixed package set.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Claude (cloud environments with setup script, env vars and network policy, vendor or self-hosted) plus Cursor (prebuilt images with recurring rebuilds, build logs and health tracking)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 4 of 12 sources (common)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: A spec {base_image, setup_script, env (secret refs), network_policy, actions[]} is stored per org or Space; a builder runs it in a fresh VM and snapshots the result as an image with a content hash and logs; sandboxes boot from the latest healthy image; a rebuild runs on spec change or cron.

verevonToday.gap: code_interpreter runs in a fixed image with a fixed package set. There is no per-org or per-Space environment definition, no setup script and no image build pipeline.

items.approach: Model Plane: sandbox-manager (Go) owns the environment spec per Space; image builds run as durable workflows in orchestrator-core (it already hosts Temporal activities); secrets are referenced by id and resolved by the item 7 injection proxy, never baked into images; build logs and health are shown in the Space settings UI.
items.planeOwner: Model Plane (sandbox-manager, orchestrator-core)
items.risks: Supply-chain risk in setup scripts, image storage cost, and secrets leaking into images.

verevon.exactGap: There is no per-org or per-Space environment definition, setup script, image build pipeline or health tracking. code_interpreter runs under bubblewrap inside the execution-core container with network hard-set to Disabled (code_interpreter.rs:581) and its package set (numpy, pandas, matplotlib, openpyxl, docx, reportlab, pypdf, pillow, lxml, python-pptx) baked into the execution-core image (execution-core/Dockerfile:41-97). sandbox-manager (Go) is a lease, snapshot, workspace-overlay and process registry only, so there is no VM or image substrate for a builder to snapshot.
reuse: the execution-core Dockerfile package layer as the seed for curated named runtime profiles
sandbox-manager workspace store and the CAS client for per-Space files
capability-core registry and policy for org-level selection of a profile
the executor's require_requested_isolation egress-proxy gate as the existing fail-closed network posture
orchestrator-core Temporal worker for build workflows, but only once a VM or image substrate exists
verevon.constraints: The sandbox has no network and AllowDomains fails closed without an egress proxy (executor.rs:113-180), so a setup script that installs packages or a spec with a network policy cannot run today; secrets by reference need the injection proxy of F-t3-043, which does not exist. Space sandbox use needs a Control Plane Space capability decision bound to the calling member (sandbox_lease.rs:106-150), so environment specs must be Space- or org-owned records in Control or capability-core, and ZDR runs must refuse any durable image state. Customer setup scripts are a supply-chain surface and must build in isolation, never inside execution-core.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Blocked on the computer or VM substrate (F-t3-009) and the injection proxy (F-t3-043). Until then, offer curated, vendor-built runtime profiles (extra package sets in the execution-core image, selected per org through capability-core), which needs no builder, no customer scripts and no secrets. Keep the spec and policy in capability-core with sandbox-manager holding only lease and image references; orchestrator-core hosting image builds is a plausible later choice but has no substrate today.
verevon.effortNote: Unchanged but conditional: L only after F-t3-009 and F-t3-043 exist; building that substrate is separate and XL. Curated named profiles are M.
verevon.verdictReason: Absent and hard-blocked by two prerequisites that do not exist, with no demand evidence and a supply-chain risk; curated runtime profiles deliver most of the value sooner.

items.title: Sandbox computer extensions: persistent machine mode, execution-target picker, authenticated dev-server preview
items.summary: Once the sandbox computer exists, add a persistent flag on a lease that keeps its disk (installed tools, services, databases), a device_ref on runs so a task can move between an ephemeral sandbox and a persistent machine, and an authenticated preview URL per listening port that opens in the Quarry hosted browser so the agent can verify what it built.
items.whyItMatters: Teams that automate recurring work with installed software need a machine that survives between runs (and it is a revenue line), and agents that build small apps or dashboards need to preview and verify them. Value is moderate for an AI workspace and depends on item 3.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Manus (always-on Ubuntu, Windows and macOS cloud computers with chosen compute and region; one active-device concept that tasks can move between) plus Claude (preview auto-verify, element selection, port discovery) plus Cursor (port forwarding from cloud VMs into shareable previews)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 2 of 12 for persistent computers, 2 of 12 for device switching, 4 of 12 for dev-server preview
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: A long-lived VM with a persistent disk and a guest agent, billed monthly, backed up as disk snapshots. Task.device_ref {kind: sandbox | cloud_computer, id} resolves the host through the backend trait; switching rehydrates the workspace and re-runs from the last checkpoint. Preview: detect listening ports, probe HTML, expose through an authenticated proxy shown in the hosted browser surface.

verevonToday.gap: Files persist per Space through the CAS workspace, which covers the most common persistence need without paying for idle machines, but there is no persistent machine, no user-visible target choice (one implicit execution-core target and a Space-scoped lease), and no way to preview a server the agent runs: HTML artifacts render in a sandboxed srcdoc iframe only.

items.approach: sandbox-manager: a persistent flag on the item 3 lease that retains the VM disk, billed through cost-core; session-core adds device_ref on runs and the composer gets a picker; sandbox-manager issues an authenticated preview URL per port that Quarry's hosted browser opens (the Model proposes, Quarry executes). Require auth on every preview and apply Space ACLs.
items.planeOwner: Model Plane (sandbox-manager, session-core)
items.risks: Cost, abuse and data residency for persistent machines; public exposure of previews unless authenticated; partial-state confusion when moving a task mid-flight. Low confidence on demand for the picker.

verevon.exactGap: None of the three proposed pieces exists: there is no persistent machine (leases are per run with a one-hour TTL, and background processes die with their parent and are capped at one hour), no execution-target concept on runs or in the composer, and no dev-server preview (HTML artifacts render only in a sandboxed srcdoc iframe, and the sandbox network namespace is down). The item's premise that files already persist per Space is only partly true: hydrate, the per-run overlay and the PromoteWorkspace compare-and-swap merge are built, but nothing calls promote_workspace (the execution-core client method at sandbox_manager_client.rs:314 has no caller and the Go handler no other consumer), so a later run never sees an earlier run's edits.
reuse: S4.2 background processes: process_* tools, ProcessHost, registry rows and the Work-tab processes section (spaces.rs:2517-2580)
Space-scoped lease plus capability decision (sandbox_lease.rs:106-160)
CAS workspace hydrate, overlay and Promote (workspace_hydrate.rs, workspace/store.go)
Quarry's navigation guard as the agent-side check for any preview origin
ArtifactHtmlPreview sandboxed-iframe pattern for a human-facing preview
verevon.constraints: Quarry's navigation guard blocks loopback and private targets (navigation.rs:86-140), so agent-side verification through Quarry's hosted browser needs a public, authenticated preview origin admitted by an explicit browser grant, never a relaxed guard; the Model proposes the navigation and Quarry executes or rejects it. A persistent machine keeps customer data at rest outside the CAS and ZDR model, so it must be refused for ZDR runs, metered through cost-core, and gated by the Space capability decision on every attach and preview so Space access never widens an owner-plane ACL. The execution target must stay a server-resolved backend pin (the lease's BackendID), never a model- or client-supplied value.
verevon.approachAdjustment: First wire PromoteWorkspace (owner-gated or review-gated per F-t3-076) so Space files really persist across runs, which covers the common persistence need. Treat the persistent machine and the picker as dependent on F-t3-009 and a billing decision. For preview, start with a human-facing authenticated gateway proxy rendered in an iframe, and add agent verification through Quarry only with an explicit grant; run the dev server as an S4.2 background process and design port exposure deliberately because process networking is down today.
verevon.effortNote: Unchanged for the bundle; wiring promote is S to M and should be its own item, a human-facing preview is M, and a persistent machine is L to XL.
verevon.verdictReason: All three proposed pieces are absent and gated on F-t3-009, the item itself flags low demand confidence, and its file-persistence premise is overstated; the promote wiring should be pulled forward as a separate item.

items.title: Review as a run: read-only reviewer subagent with strict P0-P3 findings, merged with the deterministic source checks
items.summary: Add a 'review this' run for an artifact revision, a workspace turn diff or attached files. A read-only reviewer subagent returns findings in a validated schema (title, body, priority P0-P3, confidence, location, plus overall correctness) and may report nothing. Deterministic findings from source_validation.rs are merged into the same schema and card, and 'apply fix' sends a finding back as a scoped edit turn.
items.whyItMatters: A trustworthy, located second pass is useful for code, reports and contracts alike, and four of nine references ship a review run. Verevon already has a rare strength here (deterministic checks of numbers, dates, word counts and revision preservation against sources); putting both reviewers behind one findings card makes that strength visible and consistent.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Codex (review/start with four targets, inline or detached delivery, steering disabled during review, strict findings JSON and a 'report only what the author would fix' standard)
others: Claude desktop (best findings-card UX: walkthrough, apply fix, rerun)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 4 of 9 sources; common
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: review/start {target, delivery, threadId} spawns a read-only sandboxed reviewer with a target-specific prompt (uncommitted changes, merge-base diff, a commit, or custom instructions). Output is held to a schema {findings[{title, body, confidence_score, priority, code_location}], overall_correctness, overall_confidence_score}; an explicit-only review skill enforces 'no invented findings'. The UI renders a findings card and 'apply fix' sends a finding back as a scoped edit turn.

verevonToday.gap: There is no code or generic review run and no findings card. The existing source-bound review is automatic, document-only and reports inside the drafting flow rather than as a user-invokable, located, prioritised review. Subagents exist (subagent.* tools are bound to cap.agent.spawn) but there is no review profile.

items.approach: Model Plane: a review subagent profile with a read-only capability set (fs.read, fs.grep, read_artifact; no edit or process tools) and a findings JSON schema enforced through the structured-output path; drop findings without a location or below a confidence threshold. Targets: artifact revision diff, Space workspace turn diff (R-t3-07-03), attached code or documents. Map deterministic source_validation findings into the same schema as high-confidence items. Frontend Plane: a findings card with priority chips and 'apply fix', which sends a scoped revision turn: for artifacts through the selection-bound range splice in R-t3-07-05, for workspace files through R-t3-07-01's fs.edit.
items.planeOwner: Model Plane (model-gateway, execution-core) with Frontend Plane for the card
items.risks: False positives erode trust: enforce the 'only what the author would fix' standard, a confidence floor and a reviewer that cannot write. Reviewer cost doubles the work on big diffs, so make it explicit-only and budgeted. Keep deterministic and model findings visibly distinct.

verevon.exactGap: No user-invokable review run, located P0-P3 findings schema or findings card exists; the only reviewer is source_validation.rs, an automatic model reviewer (forced review_tool call returning per-segment supported/no_assertions/unsupported verdicts with source-line evidence and receipts) that gates artifact drafting inside model-gateway, with an opt-in proposal rule that is off and unvalidated. The subagent spawn path already passes a SubagentRole (agent.rs run_delegated_child) but parse_task accepts only goal and max_rounds (subagent/mod.rs:168-186), the agent loop sends structured_output_schema empty (agent.rs:1357), and the fs.read and fs.grep tools named in the approach do not exist (read_artifact is the only inline read tool, tool_loop.rs builtin_tool_defs), so workspace-diff targets depend on F-t3-030 and F-t3-076.
reuse: source_validation.rs review_tool schema, receipts and batching (structured forced-tool review with line-cited evidence) as the model for a findings call
SubagentRole::Reviewer lineage tag (mp-orchestration subagent.rs:19-33; session-core already maps 'reviewer') and run_delegated_child's role parameter
InvokeRequest.structured_output_schema (gateway.proto:218) for the inline chat path
ChatArtifactPanel revision diff and DiffView as the review target and rendering base
execution-core hook engine and the leaf blocklist for the reviewer-cannot-write guarantee, plus an explicit tool allowlist
verevon.constraints: The existing review is labelled fallible semantic evidence, not a factual guarantee or business authority (source_validation.rs:1-3), so the findings UI must keep source-check results and model findings visibly distinct and never present either as authority. Sources are bounded to the conversation and its attachments by scope notices (source_validation.rs:12); a reviewer that reads org knowledge or Space files must run under the caller's own Space read decision and never widen an owner-plane ACL. Under ZDR no findings or receipts may be persisted, and 'apply fix' must go back through the normal revision turn (the Model proposes; no direct write). Subagents are blocked from risky tools only by a keyword denylist (agent.rs:1643), so a read-only reviewer needs an explicit allowlist, not that denylist.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Build the first slice on the inline chat path in model-gateway (artifact revision and attachments as targets) with structured_output_schema plus server-side validation, not as an agent-loop subagent: the agent loop does not forward a schema and tool_arguments::validate_arguments ignores nested schema constructs. Add a typed review entry point beside source_validation (reusing its receipt and batching) and add the Reviewer-role subagent profile only when F-t3-030 gives it files to read. Reword 'deterministic source checks' to 'automatic source-bound model review plus deterministic local guards' and show its supported/unsupported segments as a separate source-check lane rather than forcing them into P0-P3.
verevon.effortNote: M holds for artifact and attachment targets on the chat path; it becomes L if the reviewer is an agent-loop subagent with workspace-diff targets (needs F-t3-030 and F-t3-076).
verevon.verdictReason: Absent is correct and nothing substantial exists to drop, but the item mis-describes the existing reviewer as deterministic and assumes fs.* tools and a subagent profile that do not exist; the realistic first slice is a chat-path review of artifacts and attachments.

items.title: Multi-file app build and preview: static web bundles first, built output next, screenshots through Quarry
items.summary: Let agents ship a small multi-file web app or dashboard safely. Phase 0: a multi-file static bundle artifact (HTML plus CSS/JS files, no build) rendered in the existing sandboxed iframe. Phase 1: build inside the Space sandbox with a pinned, pre-baked toolchain and serve the dist output from a per-run isolated origin through the Frontend gateway. Phase 2: dev-server ports and authenticated previews, which belong to R-t3-06-10. UI screenshots of the preview are taken through Quarry.
items.whyItMatters: 'Build me a small app or dashboard' is a headline use case for claude.ai, ChatGPT and Manus, and Verevon's agents can only produce single-file HTML. A safe preview extends an existing strength (sandboxed HTML artifacts) to multi-file outputs and closes a visible gap against the references.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Claude desktop (dev-server candidate detection, explanations for cold starts and port conflicts, request throttling, ask-Claude fallback)
others: Manus (checkpoint previews and webdev LSP presets)
ChatGPT web (preview of built apps, DOC)
Claude.ai web (artifacts shared between code and chat, DOC)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 4 of 9 sources; common
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: The workspace declares a start command and port, or the agent detects them, and the sandbox runs it. A reverse proxy exposes the port to a sandboxed iframe on a per-run origin. Checkpoints snapshot the workspace and serve a static build for comparison, and a screenshot tool captures the preview for the model.

verevonToday.gap: Single-file HTML artifacts render in an iframe with sandbox=allow-scripts and no same-origin, with a version stepper. The artifact kinds are code, document, html, spreadsheet, file and image, so there is no multi-file project kind. The Space sandbox has no network and no port exposure (process_start: 'NO NETWORK, read-only system'), and there is no build step, dev-server preview or screenshot-of-preview loop.

items.approach: Phase 0 (INF, no new infrastructure): a bundle artifact kind carrying a files map, composed into one srcdoc (or blob URLs) for the existing sandboxed iframe, with the no-same-origin rule unchanged. Phase 1: execution-core builds the leased workspace with a pinned toolchain from a pre-baked image (R-t3-06-08), since the sandbox cannot install dependencies, then publishes the dist folder to a per-run isolated origin served by the Rust gateway with a strict CSP and no cookies. Phase 2: hand over to R-t3-06-10 for ports and authenticated preview URLs. Screenshots of any preview go through Quarry (the Model proposes, Quarry executes), never a Model Plane browser.
items.planeOwner: Model Plane (execution-core, sandbox-manager) with Frontend Plane gateway for the preview origin
items.risks: Serving untrusted code needs strict per-run origins, a CSP and no cookies; keep allow-same-origin out. ZDR runs must not persist builds beyond the lease. A networkless build only works for projects whose dependencies are vendored or pre-baked, which limits what 'build' can mean at first.

verevon.exactGap: Single-file HTML artifacts render in a sandbox=allow-scripts iframe (no same-origin, no-network CSP); ArtifactKind has only code, document, html, spreadsheet, file and image with one text content string capped at 200,000 characters, so there is no multi-file bundle kind. The Space sandbox (process_start, code_interpreter) has no network, runs python or sh only and exposes no port, so there is no build step, no per-run preview origin and no screenshot-of-preview loop (screenshot_ref exists only on Quarry browser observations).
reuse: ArtifactHtmlPreview iframe and the sandbox-html.ts CSP wrapper
The artifact version stepper and kind registry in artifacts.rs (add a bundle kind there)
process_* tools and the space:processes lease for any build run
BrowserObservation.screenshot_ref via Quarry for preview screenshots
F-t3-045 hosted artifact runtime on a dedicated user-content origin, if it lands first
verevon.constraints: The preview CSP allows only inline script and style plus data: and blob: images and media, so blob: script URLs, external scripts and ES module imports would be blocked: a bundle must be inlined into one srcdoc or the CSP and origin model changed deliberately. allow-same-origin must stay out of the sandbox. A per-run preview origin needs strict CSP and no cookies. Quarry decides whether it may navigate to that origin (the Model proposes, Quarry executes), so the origin must be allow-listed with Quarry, never opened from a Model Plane browser. ZDR runs must not persist builds past the sandbox lease. The process tools need an entitled Space with the space:processes lease claim, and the sandbox has no node toolchain or network today.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Phase 0 should inline all bundle files into one srcdoc at render time (still no same-origin and the same CSP) rather than use blob URLs, and should reject module imports between files. Keep phases 1 and 2 behind F-t3-009 and F-t3-045; do not promise a build until a pre-baked toolchain image exists.
verevon.effortNote: Unchanged as a whole; Phase 0 alone (bundle kind, tool schema, SPA inlining) is M and can ship independently, while phase 1 is closer to XL because it needs the pre-baked toolchain and a served origin.
verevon.verdictReason: The multi-file, build and preview parts are absent and the single-file foundation is exactly as described; only the Phase 0 mechanism needs the CSP correction.

items.title: Code edit quality on demand: post-write diagnostics (decision H11) and an optional apply_patch format where a provider benefits
items.summary: After a code artifact or workspace file is written, run cheap syntax and lint checks in the hermetic sandbox and report only newly introduced errors with one bounded auto-repair; if an edit-success evaluation shows avoidable failures on the Codex route, accept a Codex-style patch as a second fs.edit argument form parsed by the same Rust crate.
items.whyItMatters: Cursor's shadow lints and Codex's grammar-constrained patches matter for coding products; for Verevon (not an IDE) they are conditional optimisations once file tools exist.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Cursor (shadow workspace computing lints for a change without touching the user's files, plus an explicit ReadLints tool with a 10 s timeout) ; Codex (Lark-grammar-constrained freeform apply_patch tool, shell-heredoc interception, line-ending preservation, streaming patch events)
others: Antigravity (auto-fix without a prompt and a verification mode that runs tests and builds)
Cursor (switches edit tools by model vendor in production: apply_patch for GPT-5 family, Write plus StrReplace for others)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: R-t3-07-08: 2 of 9 sources; differentiator | R-t3-07-09: 2 of 9 sources; differentiator
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: After each successful edit run the language toolchain on the changed files in the sandbox within a time budget (tsc, eslint, ruff, cargo check or go vet by extension). The tool catalogue builder switches on model family: gpt-5 and codex models register apply_patch as a freeform grammar-constrained tool, other families get write plus str_replace.

verevonToday.gap: R-t3-07-08: Only a typed LspQuery pass-through to an external bridge exists; | R-t3-07-09: No edit tool exists at all (R-t3-07-01), so there is no vendor variant.

items.approach: Execute H11 instead of an LSP bridge; gate apply_patch on measured need.
items.planeOwner: Model Plane (execution-core)
items.risks: Toolchain images grow; second edit format doubles test surface.

alreadyPlanned.where: R-t3-07-08: Task H11 in apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/apps/verevon-web/plans/system-audits/CHAT_GAP_CLOSURE_PLAN_2026-10-01.md (lines 270, 276, 504): deferred to Wave 6, revisit only on a concrete user need; OD18 default is to skip. Downgraded from the comparator's recommended tier for this reason

verevon.exactGap: No file edit tool, no apply_patch and no post-write code diagnostics exist; the nearest code is lsp.rs (a typed pass-through RPC to an external bridge, disabled when LSP_BRIDGE_URL is unset and not offered to the model as a tool) and post_mutation.rs (which verifies provider writes, not code). create_artifact runs only in the inline model-gateway loop, which has no sandbox, while code_interpreter runs in execution-core, so a diagnostics hook has no shared home yet.
reuse: code_interpreter hermetic sandbox (no network, read-only rootfs, timeout) for lint or syntax runs on code_interpreter output
The post_mutation append-one-line-to-tool-output pattern as the way to feed diagnostics back
lsp.rs request and response contract if a bridge is ever deployed
mp_contracts tool_arguments validation as the shared pre-dispatch hook point in both loops
verevon.constraints: The ChatGPT subscription route does not execute native Codex tools: inference-core encodes tools as a constrained JSON proposal envelope, so a freeform grammar-constrained apply_patch tool cannot be carried by it, and platform OpenAI and Azure calls use Chat Completions only. The inline chat loop refuses side effects by design, so diagnostics for create_artifact must either be a pure in-process syntax check in model-gateway or a call into execution-core, not a sandbox run inside the gateway. Verevon is not an IDE; the plan lists H11 as deferred to Wave 6 and the recommended owner decision OD18 is to skip it.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Drop the apply_patch half (no edit tool exists and the subscription route cannot carry it). Reduce H11 to an optional syntax or lint line appended to code_interpreter output in execution-core, and only on a concrete user need; do not deploy an LSP bridge.
verevon.effortNote: The plan sizes H11 itself at S; M covered the dropped apply_patch format and a second edit surface.
verevon.verdictReason: Nothing exists to build on, the plan defers H11 pending a real user need, the product is not an IDE, and the apply_patch half has no carrying route on the subscription provider.

items.title: Use Verevon from other agents and work tools: outward MCP endpoint and channel adapters
items.summary: Host an MCP server over the typed action registry (Streamable HTTP with OAuth) so users can reach Verevon from Claude, ChatGPT or Cursor, and let Quarry consume WebMCP site tools as proposals that the Model Plane may select and Quarry executes. Separately, build Slack, Teams and email entry points as channel adapters in the future Channel Plane, with identity binding, per-channel routing, progress mirrored back and a consent card stating who posts as whom.
items.whyItMatters: It grows usage by meeting users where they already work (channel entry points 5 of 12 sources; outward MCP or WebMCP 3 of 12). It is a later phase because it depends on the action registry being open to agents (item 05) and on a Channel Plane ADR.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Hermes (mcp serve exposes conversations as MCP tools; SRC) plus ChatGPT web (consumes WebMCP site tools whose instructions cannot authorise sensitive actions; DOC) for outward interop; Cursor (Slack, Linear, GitHub and Teams start cloud agents with routing rules and mirrored progress; SRC) with Claude desktop (a session bound to a Slack thread through a disclosure-bearing consent card; SRC) for channels
others: Manus and Manus web (email and IM channels)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: Channels 5 of 12, common; outward MCP and WebMCP 3 of 12, differentiator
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Outward: an MCP server endpoint (Streamable HTTP, OAuth) exposing selected typed actions and search over the user's workspace; WebMCP: the browser surface lists tools a page registers and offers them to the model under the same policy. Channels: adapters (webhook or events API) -> identity binding (channel user to platform user) -> routing rule -> run creation with the channel as origin -> progress and result posted back, with a consent card naming channel, workspace and posting identity.

verevonToday.gap: There is no outward MCP server and no WebMCP bridge (only the consumer-side mcp-bridge); planned as M4 after M2. bridge-core has an ingress adapter interface (CLI, VS Code, web, API), a session registry and a webhook adapter with a delivery worker, which is a stub for this purpose. The Channel Plane is docs-only and Slack or Teams continuity needs an ADR before code.

items.approach: Frontend Plane gateway hosts the MCP endpoint over the typed action registry (item 05), inheriting the same risk metadata, approval gates and witness stream; ZDR must propagate to outward calls. WebMCP discovery lives in Quarry (the Model proposes browser actions; Quarry executes or rejects). Channel adapters wait for the Channel Plane ADR and live in that plane, not in Model Plane; identity binding is Control-owned; Application Plane holds routing projections.
items.planeOwner: Frontend Plane (MCP endpoint) with Ingestion Plane/Quarry (WebMCP) and the future Channel Plane (adapters)
items.risks: External agents acting with user tokens; identity-binding errors post private data to shared channels; ZDR must propagate to outward calls; the WebMCP evidence is DOC and low confidence.

alreadyPlanned.where: Partly: outward MCP server and WebMCP bridge are Phase 4 / M4 of Verevon-ai-first-plan.md (lines 44 and 114-123, after M2); channel adapters are blocked on a Channel Plane ADR (architecture rule 7).
