verevon.exactGap: Verevon exposes no outward MCP server: model-gateway and the gateway mcp.rs only manage a registry of consumed servers and an OAuth client for connecting to them (mcp_oauth.rs), the mcp-bridge is consumer-side, and Control Plane has no OAuth authorization server for external agents. items.title: Time-based media on demand: transcribe recordings into documents, pull meeting minutes, and expose video generation and understanding
items.summary: Four optional capabilities on one pipeline, to schedule on demand. (1) Audio and video uploads become transcript documents: chunk by silence, transcribe with the existing governed speech-to-text, store a Data Plane document with a back-reference to the media. (2) Meeting minutes from Teams or Zoom transcripts pulled through integration-corev2 with no recording, summarised in the Model Plane, with action items written through governed actions. (3) Expose the existing Sora job API as an async video_generate tool behind a cost-confirmation approval. (4) Video understanding through a Gemini route behind capability gating.
items.whyItMatters: Meeting recordings, voice notes and training clips would become searchable knowledge and tasks, and marketing teams ask for video. All four are off the critical chat and agent path, need new providers or connectors, and rest mostly on documentation, so they follow the priority and recommended set.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Perplexity web (DOC) for transcribed audio and video with speakers; ChatGPT Meetings (DOC) for the privacy design (no bot, private by default, audio deleted after notes); Manus (SRC) for video modes and a cost confirmation; Antigravity (SRC) for the typed media part
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: Meetings 3 of 11 and video generation 3 of 11 (each 2 distinct vendors), common; audio and video uploads 2 of 11 (DOC only), video understanding 2 of 11, differentiator
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Uploads: object storage, transcode to 16 kHz mono, chunk by silence under the speech-to-text limit, transcribe with diarisation, stitch with timestamps, store the transcript as a document linked to the media and index it. Meetings: native recorder or platform connector, then transcript, summary with action items, then a page with linked tasks; raw audio deleted after processing. Video generation: async job tool video_generate{prompt, start_image?, ratio, length, quality} with an approval card that shows cost per quality tier. Video understanding: a typed media part {mime_type, blobref, duration_seconds, thumbnail} routed to a video-capable model or subagent.

evidence: SRC grep meeting.?(minutes|transcript|record) over apps (rs, go, ts, tsx): no matches (comparator, 2026-10-13)
verevonToday.gap: A governed speech-to-text API exists with an 8 MiB audio cap; no evidence of long-file chunking or of audio and video as an ingestible document type, which was not checked in imports-core (status unknown). Sora video jobs exist as an API with cost metering, but no chat or agent tool and no UI. No Gemini provider in inference-core, so no video understanding. No meeting capture.

items.approach: First check imports-core and the doc_indexed_consumer for audio MIME handling and transcript documents. Then Data Plane ingestion calls Model Plane speech-to-text per chunk (Data Plane owns orchestration and storage, Model Plane owns inference), with ZDR orgs refused persistence. Meetings: integration-corev2 transcript connectors for Teams and Zoom, summarisation in the Model Plane, tasks through governed actions. Video: expose the Sora job as an async tool with a cost-confirmation approval and a video artifact renderer in the Output panel; add a Gemini provider in inference-core before a video_analyze subagent that takes a Data Plane attachment id and is gated by R-t3-02-03.
items.planeOwner: Data Plane (transcript documents) with Model Plane (speech, video tools), Ingestion Plane (meeting connectors) and Frontend Plane (video artifact)
items.risks: Cost of long audio and of video generation; personal data in recordings (consent, retention, recording law); video-provider availability and residency in the EU; speaker identification is unreliable (ChatGPT documents this).

verevon.exactGap: Voice input already reaches model-gateway /v1/ai/speech and /v1/ai/dictate (Whisper-based provider, 8 MiB body cap, no chunking or diarisation), and Data Plane's embedding-engine already has a durable consumer for audio and video segment events (dataplane.audio_segments.created and video_segments.created, CLAP and X-CLIP embeddings, optional transcript stored for display only), but a search of apps/ found no producer of those events, so there is no segmenter, no transcript-document path and no media upload route (imports-core has no audio or video handling). Sora job routes exist (/v1/ai/video/*, ZDR-gated, 20 s and 4-variant limits) but no gateway or SPA route, chat tool, ArtifactKind::Video or spend metering was found, there is no Gemini provider in inference-core, and integration-corev2 has no meeting-transcript connector.
reuse: model-gateway /v1/ai/speech and zdr_posture::decide_content_route for governed transcription
Data Plane embedding-engine media_consumer subjects and the media-embedder service (consumer side is built; emit the existing segment events with transcript filled)
documents-api-go create (type, source, idempotency_key) for the transcript document
inference-core video job provider and the /v1/ai/video/* routes
model-gateway budget.rs pre-flight guard as the base for a cost-confirmation approval
artifacts.rs and ChatArtifactPanel for a new video artifact kind
verevon.constraints: Data Plane owns transcript documents and segment events while Model Plane owns inference, so the Data Plane job must call Model Plane speech with the delegated bearer rather than embed a provider. Media embedding is local-only (no egress, ZDR-safe by construction), but a transcript document is a durable mutation and must be refused for ZDR orgs; video generation is already rejected for unattested ZDR in inference-core. Meeting transcripts are fetched by Ingestion Plane integration-corev2 under Graph transcript scopes (admin consent), recording laws and retention rules apply, and the Channel Plane meeting-intelligence doc is future-only. Data Plane documents are UTF-8 text up to 5 MiB, so the media itself is not stored as a document.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Replace 'first check imports-core' with the finding: imports-core has no media path, and Data Plane's consumer already exists without a producer. Build the producer (ffmpeg segmentation, silence chunking under the speech limit, per-chunk transcription) as a Data Plane orchestrator job, create the transcript document first, then emit the existing dataplane.audio_segments.created and video_segments.created events with transcript text and start_ms/end_ms so retrieval cites timestamps. For video_generate, estimate and meter cost first (none found on the route), add a video artifact kind, then wrap the job as an async tool behind an approval card. Treat meetings, uploads, video generation and video understanding as four separate items.
verevon.effortNote: Raised from L as a combined item: the segment producer, Teams/Zoom transcript connectors, video cost metering and a Gemini provider are all missing; uploads-to-transcripts alone is M and video_generate alone is M.
verevon.verdictReason: Not unknown: the code shows what exists (speech API, media-embedding consumer, Sora routes) and what is missing (producer, connectors, tool, metering, Gemini); the item's claim of Sora cost metering and its imports-core check are wrong or obsolete.

items.title: Data-connected dashboards with visible queries, and sensitivity-label-aware document policy
items.summary: Two governance-flavoured options. (1) A dashboard artifact made of {chart spec, query, connector, refreshed_at} entries where every chart shows its query and last refresh and re-runs with the viewer's own connector credentials; first check whether Data Plane retrieval tools or the Reports page can already bind charts to stored queries. (2) Adopt Microsoft sensitivity-label checks in Data Plane document access through integration-corev2 Graph metadata, with allow and deny effects; Office add-ins themselves stay deferred.
items.whyItMatters: Showing the query beside each chart extends Verevon's habit of showing its sources to operational data. Label-aware policy mirrors the governance layer Claude desktop ships for add-ins and matters to Microsoft-centric customers, independent of whether add-ins ever ship.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: claude.ai (DOC) for per-chart query transparency; Claude desktop (SRC) for label-aware add-in policy
others: ChatGPT web (DOC, broader add-in coverage including Google Sheets)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: Dashboards: 1 of 11, unique (DOC only). Add-ins and label policy: 2 of 11, differentiator
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Dashboard artifact = list of {chart spec, query, connector, refreshed_at}; refresh re-runs queries with the viewer's connector credentials and the query is displayed with each chart. Label policy: a policy engine evaluates the document's sensitivity label (equals, starts with, any, none) before each action, with separate rules for opened and uploaded files; an Office add-in sidebar authenticates to the assistant and host tools operate on the open document.

verevonToday.gap: No baseline record for dashboards: whether Reports or a Data Plane feature can bind charts to stored queries was not checked. The result_query tool lets the model aggregate parked tool results (SRC tool_loop.rs, result_query definition), which is not a dashboard. No add-ins; editing existing Excel and PowerPoint in place and saving to OneDrive or Drive is planned behind owner decision OD14, and no sensitivity-label check was found.

items.approach: Dashboards: Data Plane owns query execution and connectors, Model Plane writes the query, Frontend Plane renders a dashboard artifact with visible queries and a refresh that uses the viewer's own permissions. Label policy: read the label through integration-corev2 Graph metadata and evaluate allow or deny in Data Plane document access before any action; revisit an Office add-in only after owner decision OD14.
items.planeOwner: Data Plane (query execution, label policy) with Model Plane (query authoring), Frontend Plane (dashboard artifact) and Ingestion Plane (integration-corev2)
items.risks: Query cost and permissions; stale data shown as current (always show refreshed_at); add-in marketplace review and support burden; label policy must never widen an owner-plane ACL.

alreadyPlanned.where: Office add-ins and in-place editing are planned behind OD14 (apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/apps/verevon-web/plans/system-audits/CHAT_PARITY_AUDIT_2026-10-01.md:63). Dashboards are not planned (INF, not found).

verevon.exactGap: Chart specs are static (ChartSpec holds categories and series values only), the Insights page has fixed tabs over Insight Core overview contracts, and result_query handles are conversation-scoped and expire, so nothing can store a re-runnable {chart, query, connector, refreshed_at}. No Microsoft sensitivity-label (MIP) reading exists in finspo-core or integration-corev2; the only related seams are finspo-core's fail-closed ClassifyVisibility (SharePoint ACL to org or private) and Data Plane's zdr_classification vocabulary (internal, public, sensitive, restricted).
reuse: finspo-core ClassifyVisibility (extend it into a label-aware downgrade rule that fails closed)
documents-api-go visibility (private|org|shared), VisibilityFromSource and resource_grants via gateway shares.rs
typed integration-corev2 provider read actions as the unit of a chart 'query' (Graph workbook and Sheets reads are planned as G4/G5)
chat-chart ChartSpec, ChatChart renderer and SVG export for the rendering half
result_query's select/where/aggregate grammar as the query vocabulary
shared/i18n/errors.ts personal_connection_forbidden handling for viewer-credential refresh
verevon.constraints: Data Plane stores and enforces visibility but does not read Microsoft labels; the label read belongs in the Ingestion Plane SharePoint ingest (finspo-core), which already owns ACL-to-visibility mapping. The rule may only narrow (org to private, or hold back from retrieval), never widen, to respect the rule that nothing widens an owner-plane ACL. A connector-bound chart refresh executes as an integration-corev2 provider action (Ingestion Plane), not in Data Plane, must use the viewer's own delegated connection, and must persist nothing durable under ZDR (result_query handles do not exist on ZDR turns). Office add-ins stay behind owner decision OD14.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Split into two items. (1) Label-aware ingest policy: extend finspo-core ClassifyVisibility to read the SharePoint/OneDrive sensitivity label through Graph and demote labelled items to private (missing label data fails closed), and record the label as document metadata; do not describe it as 'Data Plane document access' evaluation. (2) Dashboards: define a saved-query unit first (provider action id, typed params, viewer connection), because the chat chart fence and parked result handles cannot carry a re-runnable query; correct the item text that has Data Plane owning connectors and query execution.
verevon.effortNote: Unchanged overall, but the label half is about M (one seam in finspo-core plus a Graph label read and an admin-consent check) while the dashboard half is L to XL and speculative (1 of 11 sources, documentation only).
verevon.verdictReason: Status is absent (not unknown) and the approach misplaces label evaluation and connector query execution in Data Plane; reword and split, treating the dashboard half as the weaker option.

items.title: Model Council: parallel multi-model answers with a disagreement synthesis
items.summary: Add a council mode in which the gateway fans the same question out to N catalogue models through inference-core, then runs a synthesiser call that lists agreement, disagreement and unique contributions, shown side by side. Show the expected cost first, reusing the estimate card from R-t3-03-03.
items.whyItMatters: Multi-model use is a stated Verevon goal (the T3 Code reference) and disagreement surfacing supports the transparency and confidence story. It is distinctive but N-fold in cost, so it comes after the core research gaps.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Perplexity Model Council (web-perplexity-web-product-038, DOC)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 1 of 11 sources; unique (DOC only)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Fan out the same prompt to N models concurrently (3 on the web, 2 to 8 in Computer, per-model thinking toggles), collect answers, run a separate synthesiser model that compares claims as agree, disagree or unique, and render columns plus a synthesis.

evidence: grep model.?council in apps/Model Plane/rust and apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src: only demo fixtures (INF from grep)
verevonToday.gap: No multi-model fan-out answer mode. Verevon already has a model picker and inference-core routing that could serve it.

items.approach: Model Plane model-gateway: a council run type that calls inference-core for N models in parallel (bounded concurrency), then a synthesis inference; stream per-model answers into per-model panels. Cost estimate first. Frontend: side-by-side view in the chat turn. Under ZDR only models on ZDR-attested routes may join the council.
items.planeOwner: Model Plane
items.risks: N-fold cost; ZDR must hold for every council member; subscription-route rate limits (a single seat is shared across the org) make wide fan-out risky.

verevon.exactGap: No code path fans one question out to several catalogue models and synthesises a comparison; the only fan-out is execution-core subagent.research_fan_out (research_fan_out.rs), which runs N items on one model into a merged digest. The Agents page ChatbotPlayground.tsx has a disabled "Compare AI models" button whose comment says there is no backend, and MODEL_PLANE_IMPROVEMENTS_2026.md lists selective multi-model ensembles as future work.
evidence: apps/Model Plane/rust/services/inference-core/src/provider/fallback.rs:1261-1290 (request-level provider_hint and model, so a caller can address N models)
reuse: inference-core Infer with provider_hint and model per member, called in parallel from model-gateway
shared/chat-nodes keyed node registry for a council turn node
The F-t3-028 pre-run cost estimate card
research_fan_out merge pattern (per-member status, bounded digest) for the synthesis input
zdr_posture decide_content_route and the ZDR/privacy-tier gates in the chain to filter members
verevon.constraints: Every member must pass the same ZDR, privacy-tier and residency gates; under ZDR only attested routes may join. A subscription-route member spends the single org or user seat and is final on refusal (no substitute), so it must be opt-in and count against the cost estimate. Model Plane owns the run type; the answers persist through Session Core, so the turn shape needs a decision on which answer becomes context for the next turn. Background-style synthesis calls must still be metered under the org feature.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Place the fan-out in model-gateway as a non-agentic, tool-free council run (bounded concurrency, hard member cap) rather than in execution-core. Persist the result as one structured assistant node with per-member panels and a synthesis, and let the user pick the answer that continues the thread.
verevon.effortNote: Unchanged; this holds for a tool-free council persisted as one structured node. It becomes L if each member must stream into its own persisted message.
verevon.verdictReason: Confirmed absent by my own search of Model Plane, the SPA and the gateway; it is a unique, cost-multiplying feature and the nice-to-have tier fits.

items.title: Grow the corpus from research: arm promote-on-use safely and add a data-source catalogue with use_when and cost hints
items.summary: (a) promote_on_use.rs counts grounded fetches per (org, user, url) and promotes pages the agent keeps relying on into Data Plane v2, but it is off by default, dry-run first, keeps an in-memory counter, and is called only from the execution-core agent loop. Before arming it: mint a per-user token so promoted documents are owned by the user, make the counter durable, count citations rather than fetches, keep ZDR off, keep untrusted provenance, and add a 'promoted from web' badge on the Knowledge page. (b) Give Verevon's data tools (Brreg, SSB, Yr, shipping, traffic, news) a catalogue entry with use_when and cost hints that the model reads, as the base for later licensed Nordic sources.
items.whyItMatters: Research done once becomes reusable organisation knowledge, which feeds the Data Plane moat. A catalogue helps the model choose the right data tool and is the schema needed before any licensed premium source can be added.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Antigravity knowledge items (antigravity-agent-ux-and-gemini-023, SRC) for distillation limits; Manus data-source catalogue (manus-product-ux-044, SRC) for the use_when and billing_hint schema
others: Perplexity finance vertical and premium sources (web-perplexity-web-product-039 and -042, DOC)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 1 of 11 for knowledge items (unique); 3 of 11 for vertical data sources (differentiator)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: A background step every K turns writes bounded knowledge items with references and a retrieval step inserts the top items into later prompts. A catalogue of data APIs carries description, use_when and billing hint; calls go through a proxy that holds partner keys, results are cited like web sources and charged per call.

verevonToday.gap: SRC: promote_on_use is a complete no-op unless PROMOTE_ON_USE_ENABLED is set, dry-run unless PROMOTE_ON_USE_EXECUTE is set, uses a process-local counter, would attribute documents to the service principal today, and counts fetches rather than citations (its own doc lists these refinements as required before arming). It is not set in the deploy files I grepped. Norwegian public-data tools are shipped but have no catalogue schema; weather covers 10 cities and SSB only population (from the earlier baseline). No licensed premium sources.

items.approach: Model Plane execution-core: implement the two refinements named in promote_on_use.rs (per-user token minted through data-plane or Quarry so owner=user and visibility=private; durable per-org counter; citation-based signal) and wire the call site in the chat loop only after that. Data Plane: mark promoted documents with web provenance and untrusted trust class. Frontend: a 'promoted from web' badge and an undo on the Knowledge page. Model Plane: add use_when and cost_hint fields to the tool descriptions of the Norwegian data tools. Licensed sources follow only after a commercial decision, behind integration-corev2 with per-call cost in cost-core.
items.planeOwner: Data Plane
items.risks: Promoting web content imports injected text or stale facts, so keep untrusted provenance on promoted documents. Must be off under ZDR. Licence terms may restrict caching.

alreadyPlanned.where: promote-on-use is 'Phase 8' in apps/Model Plane/rust/services/execution-core/src/promote_on_use.rs module doc, with two refinements listed as required before arming (not scheduled in the gap closure plan).

verevon.exactGap: (a) promote_on_use.rs (maybe_promote, called from runtime_loop/mod.rs:786 only for web_fetch and Quarry web-read results in the execution-core agent loop, never from the chat-loop fetch_url) is a complete no-op unless PROMOTE_ON_USE_ENABLED, dry-run unless PROMOTE_ON_USE_EXECUTE, keeps a process-local counter, counts successful fetches rather than citations, and promotes through Quarry /v1/scrape with a service token so the document would be owned by the service principal; no Model Plane deploy or config file searched sets it. It also passes no ZDR flag, and Quarry ignores a service token's ZDR floor and trusts the body flag, so an armed promote would durably ingest pages fetched in a ZDR run, a blocker the module's own two listed refinements do not mention. (b) The Norwegian data tools carry only prose guidance in tool_loop.rs descriptions (get_weather covers 10 cities, get_statistics covers population only), the capability registry already has a coarse cost_class and seeded org skills steer tool choice, but no use_when or cost_hint field exists.
reuse: Quarry /v1/scrape ingest primitive (owner from signed claims, ZDR from the body flag, durable crawl and batch jobs refused under ZDR) and execution-core quarry_auth TokenSource
user-delegated, audience-bound bearer pattern in execution-core auth.rs (inference, browser-broker, data-plane, sandbox-manager) which already carries the zdr posture
execution-core provenance labelling of web tool output so promoted text keeps an untrusted source label
capability registry CapabilityDetail.cost_class, risk_level and description for (b), and seed_tool_knowledge.sql agent_skills for steering tool choice
KnowledgePage WebSourcesPanel and PrivacyBadge for the Knowledge-page badge and undo
verevon.constraints: Model proposes, Quarry executes: promotion must remain a Quarry ingest that execution-core only triggers, and the document must land owner=user with private visibility in Data Plane, which owns the document and its ACL. ZDR must be a hard gate in maybe_promote (pass the run's resolved posture and refuse when active or unknown) because Quarry's service-token path trusts the caller's body flag. Execution-core has no database of its own, so a durable counter belongs in session-core or Data Plane. Promoted web text re-enters retrieval as context, so untrusted provenance must be preserved. Licensed premium sources stay behind integration-corev2 with per-call cost in cost-core.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Add the missing precondition first: a ZDR gate in maybe_promote, then a user-delegated ingest credential (only inference, browser-broker, data-plane and sandbox-manager delegated bearers exist; a Quarry-ingest audience or routing through the delegated Data Plane bearer would be new). Wire the chat-loop call site only after that, and prefer a citation-based signal over fetch counts. Split (b) out as a small separate item: add use_when and cost_hint to capability tool metadata (cost_class already exists) and generate the model-facing description from it instead of hand-editing prose in tool_loop.rs.
verevon.effortNote: Raised from M. (a) needs a ZDR gate (S), a user-delegated ingest credential across Auth Core, Quarry and execution-core (M), a durable counter in session-core (M), a citation signal (M) and a badge with undo plus web provenance on Data Plane documents (M); (b) alone is S.
verevon.verdictReason: Stub confirmed and risks are real, but the item omits the ZDR blocker and the missing delegated credential, and (a) and (b) have very different size; keep (a) as a low-priority arming checklist and (b) as a small quick win.

items.title: Self-maintained team knowledge wiki generated from activity
items.summary: A scheduled Data Plane job reads new activity through a contract with session-core (no cross-plane DB access), extracts entities and decisions, and upserts source-linked wiki pages that the Model Plane proposes and users approve, with stale marking when sources change. Space ACLs govern visibility and personal memory never enters a shared wiki without opt-in.
items.whyItMatters: Perplexity's Brain shows demand for a knowledge base that maintains itself, and Verevon already ships an org knowledge base and a Data Plane that owns wiki and graph tools. It is a strong team feature but large, overlaps the Data Plane roadmap and rests on a single documentation-only reference.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: web-perplexity
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 1 of 12 sources (unique, documentation only, research preview).
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: An overnight refresh reads new activity, upserts markdown pages with source links into versioned storage, marks pages stale when sources change, and shows Concepts, Entities and Workstreams views; a shared project Brain has owner-controlled auto or manual updates and a personal-memory opt-in.

verevonToday.gap: The org knowledge base exists as a grounding corpus and the Data Plane owns wiki and graph tools, but nothing generates pages automatically from user activity; graph validity intervals are planned (Graphiti rejected).

items.approach: Data Plane owns the generator and storage; session-core publishes activity through a contract; the Model Plane proposes page edits through the R-t3-08-04 style approval path; Space ACLs decide who sees what. Treat as a roadmap bet after the learning loop and profile are in place.
items.planeOwner: Data Plane
items.risks: Cost, privacy of personal memory in shared wikis, and overlap with the Data Plane roadmap. Single documentation-only reference.

alreadyPlanned.where: apps/GRAPHITI_ADOPTION_ADR_2026-09-07.md (validity intervals only; Graphiti not adopted); no activity-to-wiki generator is planned

verevon.exactGap: Data Plane already has most of the approval half: wiki-store-go stores pages and versions, accepts agent proposals with source_refs (SubmitProposal, ReviewProposal), takes maintenance sweeps for stale, orphan and contradiction items, runs an operating-map proposal flow with human review in the Knowledge page, and data-orchestrator has a scheduled JobWikiRefresh; Model Plane exposes wiki_propose_edit and wiki_lint tools and POST /v1/wiki/proposals. What is missing is the generator and its feed: nothing reads session activity to draft pages (the refresh job only posts data-quality lint results, operating-map refresh is evidence-ref based, Dreaming writes personal agent_memory), SubmitProposal can only target an existing page, the BFF and Knowledge UI review only operating-map proposals, and staleness is lint and age based rather than source-change based. session-core already publishes RUN_COMPLETED events through its audit outbox (consumed by capability-core for skill learning) which a generator could subscribe to.
reuse: wiki-store-go proposals (page_id, proposed_content, source_refs, status) with ReviewProposal publishing a new version and emitting the wiki-published event
operating-map proposal, review route and KnowledgePage review UI as the human-approval surface to generalise
wiki_agent.rs propose_edit and lint tools and the model-gateway /v1/wiki/proposals routes
data-orchestrator JobWikiRefresh and the wiki maintenance sweep for stale and orphan marking
session-core learning_events RUN_COMPLETED outbox and the capability-core sessionreview consumer pattern (fetch transcript through an authorised read, then act) as the activity feed
Dreaming extractor (dream_extractor) for model-driven extraction with LLM-provenance links
verevon.constraints: Data Plane owns wiki storage and the page ACL (pages are scoped by org and workspace_id today), the Model Plane may only propose through the proposal route and humans accept, and session-core activity must reach Data Plane through a contract (the existing outbox events plus an authorised transcript read), never a cross-plane DB read. ZDR threads leave no durable transcript and wiki events are published with ZDR=false, so ZDR-origin content must be excluded at the source rather than filtered downstream. Personal memory (agent_memory user and thread scopes) must not enter a shared page without explicit opt-in, and Space access never widens a page's owner-plane ACL, so the source threads' audience must be intersected with the page audience.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Reuse the existing proposal-and-review path instead of designing a new approval path: add a create-page proposal kind (proposals can only edit an existing page today) and a generic wiki-proposal review view (only the operating map has one). Drive the generator from RUN_COMPLETED-style session-core events and start with Space or team scoped sources, not whole-org activity. Keep it a roadmap bet: its only external reference is documentation.
verevon.effortNote: XL stands for the generator, new-page proposals, a generic review UI and source-change staleness; the storage and approval half is already built, so it should not be re-sized upward, but it is also not a small extension.
verevon.verdictReason: The recommendation reads as greenfield but Data Plane already owns pages, versions, proposals, review and sweeps, and the Model Plane already proposes; reword to name the real delta (activity-to-page generator, new-page proposals, generic review UI) and keep it a late roadmap bet.

items.title: Second-order latency and cache levers: speed tier, prewarm, cache-preserving in-band changes, Responses continuation
items.summary: After the cache and effort basics are measured, add optional levers in this order: a user-facing speed tier (Standard or Fast) declared in the model record and mapped to provider priority processing with a cost multiplier in cost-core; a prewarm call on composer focus (connection warm-up first, cache priming only if measured to pay) with deadline-based optional context sources and a context-status block; append-only in-band updates for changed prompts, effort and added tools, with background forks reusing the exact parent prefix; and, last, an OpenAI Responses adapter mode with incremental continuation for non-ZDR turns.
items.whyItMatters: Lower time to first token and cost on long sessions and connector-heavy threads. Plumbing already exists for the priority tier on the Codex route, and turn_timing gives a baseline to prove any gain.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: codexagent (034 service tiers, 038 Responses WebSocket); cursor (134, 110 prewarm and progressive hydration); deepseek (037, 038 in-history updates)
others: hermes (103 time-bounded fast windows, 058 cache-parity review forks)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: speed tier 3 of 12, in-band changes 3 of 12 (differentiators); prewarm 1 of 12, Responses WebSocket 1 of 12 (unique)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Per-model service_tiers with multipliers and a default tier; a request-header tool diff that emits one developer message instead of rewriting the tool list; prewarm_request mirroring a run request without an action; previous_response_id continuation with HTTPS fallback. [SRC]

evidence: apps/Model Plane/rust/services/model-gateway/src/latency_levers.rs:1-20 (existing env kill-switch pattern for latency levers)
verevonToday.gap: A prefer_priority_service_tier flag exists (Codex route, some internal gateway paths) but there is no user-facing speed control, no tier on platform OpenAI routes and no cost multiplier. Prewarm, append-only prompt or tool updates, parent-prefix reuse by background calls, and Responses continuation have no baseline record (a grep for prewarm and previous_response_id in Model Plane Rust found nothing): check how a mid-thread connector or skill addition changes the tool list.

items.approach: Follow the latency_levers.rs kill-switch pattern for each lever. Speed tier: model-record service_tiers plus composer toggle, price in cost-core. Prewarm: model-gateway endpoint plus deadline-bounded context sources, using turn_timing to prove a gain. In-band changes: header diffing (system_hash, tools_hash, effort) in prompt_context, enabled per model only where tested. Responses mode: optional adapter flag, rebuildable from Session Core history and disabled on ZDR turns.
items.planeOwner: Model Plane
items.risks: Cost surprises from the fast tier (show the multiplier); prewarm cache-priming spends tokens; provider-held state (previous_response_id) conflicts with ZDR and durable Session Core history, so restrict to non-ZDR turns; provider-specific in-band semantics.

verevon.exactGap: More exists than the item states: the composer has a Quick/Standard/Deep effort selector (DashboardComposer.tsx) whose Quick value becomes a 1024-token budget in thinking.rs, and inference-core codex_service_tier maps that to the priority tier on the ChatGPT subscription route (prefer_priority_service_tier is also set internally for source review and project drafting). Missing: a tier declared per model record, any priority tier on platform OpenAI or Azure routes (the adapter is Chat Completions only), a cost multiplier (no priority or multiplier hit in cost-core), and any prewarm, append-only in-band prompt or tool updates, parent-prefix reuse or Responses continuation. Cache read/write accounting, Anthropic cache_control breakpoints and turn_timing already exist as the baseline.
reuse: The Quick/Standard/Deep selector and the thinking.rs profile contract as the UI and wire home for a speed control
codex_service_tier and prefer_priority_service_tier on InferRequest, extended to a declared per-model tier
latency_levers.rs kill-switch pattern for each new lever
turn_timing (phase spans and provider intervals) to prove any gain before enabling a lever
Existing cache-token parsing in openai.rs (reads both Chat Completions and Responses usage shapes) and the Anthropic breakpoint placement
F-t3-022 cache-hit measurement as the gate for prewarm and in-band changes
verevon.constraints: The subscription route goes through the Integration Core broker (BrokerRequest carries only model, messages, output_schema, reasoning_effort and service_tier), so Responses continuation can apply only to platform OpenAI or Azure routes (INF). previous_response_id keeps provider-held state, which conflicts with Zero-Data-Retention and with Session Core as the durable history, so it must be limited to non-ZDR turns. Prewarm and cache-priming calls spend tokens and must be metered through cost-core under the org; under ZDR or temporary chat no user content may be sent ahead of a send. The priority-tier price multiplier belongs in cost-core, the ledger of record.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Reword the baseline: a user-facing speed control already exists as the Quick response mode, but it conflates reasoning effort with the priority tier and works only on the subscription route. Split the speed tier from effort (declared tier per model record, cost multiplier in cost-core, platform-route mapping only after confirming the Azure or OpenAI deployment supports it, which I could not verify). Keep prewarm, in-band diffing and the Responses adapter behind F-t3-022 measurements, each with a kill switch.
verevon.effortNote: Unchanged in total, but the speed tier and connection warm-up are M each; the Responses adapter (a new provider adapter beside Chat Completions) and append-only in-band updates are the L parts.
verevon.verdictReason: The item is not absent: part of the speed-tier mechanism is live behind the Quick mode, so its gap statement (no user-facing speed control) is wrong. The rest is real and unbuilt.

items.title: Tighten-only runtime monitors: asynchronous action reviewer and information-flow control
items.summary: If the owners revisit the standing 'no LLM on the permission path' ruling for a restricted role, add an asynchronous reviewer between capability policy and the human card that can only deny or escalate and never grant, fed user turns plus the proposed tool call and never tool outputs, using a versioned rule set (must-name intent-clearing rules, agent-authored argument provenance, deterministic forced-card checks) and failing closed to a human card. Separately, add admin-defined data classification on threads and connectors with session taint and approval on downward flows, built from the existing restricted-context write block and privacy tiers.
items.whyItMatters: A trajectory monitor is a second line of defence against injection-driven actions in Do-mode, and classification-aware flow control stops confidential Data Plane content leaking to Slack or email through agents. Neither is needed to make approvals usable: that is delivered deterministically by R-t3-11-02, -03 and -04. The comparator rated the reviewer priority (7 of 12 sources) but Verevon's architecture rules exclude the approval-granting form, so it is re-tiered here.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Codex Guardian v2 (asynchronous trajectory scoring with thresholds, gating later actions, fail closed) plus Claude (classifier policy discipline: must-name rules, tool-result blindness, forceAsk escalations) for the reviewer; Manus (admin classification levels, per-connector input and output levels, approval on downward flow) for flow control
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: auto-review 7 of 12 (table-stakes elsewhere); classifier policy text 1 of 12 (unique); flow control 3 of 12 (differentiator)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Reviewer gets user messages plus proposed tool name and arguments (not tool outputs) and a policy prompt, returns {decision, reason, risk 0..1}; allow below a threshold, escalate above it, deny on clear violation; N consecutive denials pause the run; reviewer failure fails closed to a human card; every verdict is logged. Flow control: ordered levels, a session level that rises when it reads higher-classified data, connector max input levels, writes above the destination level need approval or are blocked, downgrades explicit and audited.

verevonToday.gap: No reviewer model exists; risk is a coarse substring classifier. The repo has a standing decision against LLM-on-the-permission-hot-path (HAP WS-3, CHD 13.3 anti-pattern) and ownership-matrix rule 12 says effectful calls need a signed durable authorisation, so an LLM auto-approve tier is excluded. Flow control is partial: a consent-to-disclose predicate, a restricted-context write block and privacy-tier routing exist, but no admin-defined classification with session taint.

items.approach: execution-core: Reviewer step after EvaluatePolicy using a cheap inference-core route; the verdict can only lower Allow to Ask or Deny, consecutive denials pause the run, verdicts go to the run trace and audit outbox, ZDR runs use a ZDR-attested reviewer or force a human, and NeverAuto and hard floors stay outside the classifier. Policy text is versioned data in capability-core with red-team fixtures. Flow control: Data Plane labels documents, Model Plane raises a thread's level on retrieval, capability-core stores connector levels, execution-core checks before provider writes and routes to HITL with an explicit audited downgrade.
dependencies: ADR: LLM on the permission path (HAP WS-3, rule 12)
items.planeOwner: Model Plane (reviewer, taint checks); Data Plane (document labels); Control Plane (classification levels)
items.risks: Conflicts with the standing decision if it ever grants; keep it tighten-only and asynchronous. Classifier false negatives under injection and policy drift from tool semantics. Taint over-propagation makes threads unusable, so provide a reviewed downgrade.

verevon.exactGap: No action reviewer exists: permission evaluation is posture mode plus a keyword risk list (permission/mod.rs:43-70, 229-290), and capability policy is asked with tool name, run id and org id only (capability_policy.rs:55-70, 135-145), never the call arguments or user turns. Flow control is absent: there is no admin-defined data classification, no session taint and no per-connector input or output level; precursors are TrustClass tool-result provenance (moderation.rs:206), the consent-to-disclose and restricted-context-write predicates (permission/mod.rs:160-181), privacy-tier provider routing (inference.proto:85-97) and a descriptive integration dataClass label. A sampled, detached LLM shadow classifier for tool results already exists as audit-only (semantic_screening.rs:1-40), which is the repo's own precedent for a first step.
reuse: hook engine (execution-core hook/mod.rs): PreToolUse Allow/Deny/Ask where Allow only defers to the permission engine, so it is already a tighten-only lattice and the natural host for a reviewer verdict
autonomy rung ladder (permission/mod.rs rung_required_for, mp_contracts::autonomy)
semantic_screening.rs shadow-pass pattern (sampled, detached, audit event, never changes behaviour) and security_events.rs hash-only events
ToolProvenance and TrustClass in both loops (model-gateway moderation.rs, execution-core provenance.rs) as the integrity side of flow control
requires_durable_owner_approval, requires_consent_to_disclose and is_restricted_context_write as hard floors that stay outside any classifier
capability-core safety_policies and the models.privacy_tier column as policy-as-data homes
verevon.constraints: A standing decision rules out an LLM on the permission hot path (harness-adoption-execution-plan.md:914-916; claude-hermes-deepseek.md anti-pattern near 1278), and ownership matrix rule 12 (master-ownership-matrix.md:168) says Model Plane never invents approval authority; a reviewer is compatible only if it can move Allow to Ask or Deny, never grant, and fails closed to a human card. ZDR: reviewer prompts carry user turns and tool arguments, so under ZDR it needs a ZDR-attested route (min_privacy_tier rides on every round) or must be skipped in favour of a human card. Flow control crosses planes: classification levels are Control Plane policy and document labels Data Plane, and Space access must never widen an owner-plane ACL, so Model Plane cannot infer taint alone. 'NeverAuto' in the approach is not an existing construct; the real hard floors are the predicates listed under reuse.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Split the item. (a) Reviewer: ship it first as a shadow-only evaluator on the semantic_screening pattern (sampled, detached, verdicts to the audit outbox, no enforcement), feeding it user turns plus proposed call arguments and never tool outputs, then promote it to tighten-only through the hook engine once agreement data exists. (b) Flow control: treat it as a separate cross-plane program behind an ADR (classification owner in Control Plane, labels in Data Plane) and start from TrustClass integrity provenance rather than a new confidentiality model.
verevon.effortNote: Unchanged for the whole; the shadow reviewer alone is L and flow control alone is XL, gated by an owner ADR and Control and Data Plane work.
verevon.verdictReason: Absent status and the conflict with the standing no-LLM-on-the-permission-path decision are confirmed. Reword to begin with a shadow-mode reviewer on the existing INJ-3 precedent via the hook engine and to split flow control into its own ADR-gated item; it is already the lowest tier so no further demotion is needed.

items.title: Reader and appearance polish: conversation TOC and chapters, font size and dyslexia-friendly font, org accent and environment identity, calm tips, reasoning translation

An organisation accent or admin banner would be Control Plane org branding that does not exist today. Reasoning translation is a second inference on model reasoning: it must be opt-in, cost-isolated, never fed back to the model and refused or kept non-durable under ZDR.
